item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
8th All India Conference of GRP Chiefs Concludes in New Delhi; Focus on Intelligence-Led Policing and Stronger Coordination among RPF, GRP and State Police
GRP Personnel Onboarded on RailMadad Platform for Improved Grievance Redressal, Timely Information-Sharing and Complaint Monitoring
Safer Railway Journeys During Diwali and Chhath: Emphasis on Crowd Management, Advance Planning and Efficient Passenger-Flow Management
From Drone-Assisted “Pink Patrol” to Project DISHA, Women-Led and Community-Based Safety Initiatives Deliberated at GRP Chiefs’ Conference
Posted On: 24 OCT 2026 10:47AM by PIB Delhi

The 8th All India Conference of Government Railway Police (GRP) Chiefs, convened by the Railway Protection Force (RPF), concluded successfully in New Delhi on 23 October 2026. It provided a platform for discussing emerging security challenges, sharing best practices and strengthening coordination among RPF, GRP and State Police.

The high-level conference was presided over by Director General, RPF, Ms. Sonali Mishra, and attended by Chairman and CEO, Railway Board, Shri Satish Kumar, members of the Railway Board, and GRP chiefs from various States and Union Territories.

A key highlight was the onboarding of GRP personnel onto the RailMadad platform by the Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS), aimed at improving passenger grievance redressal, timely information-sharing and complaint monitoring.

Detailed deliberations were held on various initiatives aimed at enhancing railway security and passenger safety.

South Central Railway’s “Pink Patrol: Eyes in the Sky, SHAKTI on the Ground” showcased a women-led model integrating drone-assisted surveillance with rapid-response teams under the SHAKTI framework.

Stone-pelting on trains was highlighted as a challenge, with emphasis on hotspot-based patrolling, enhanced surveillance, strict action against offenders, youth outreach and stronger RPF-GRP coordination. Community awareness and preventive engagement were recognised as important deterrents.

The conference also deliberated on crowd management during Diwali, Chhath and other festivals. Northern Railway’s Delhi Division highlighted coordinated efforts with Delhi Police, GRP and Delhi Metro authorities, supported by CCTV surveillance, public announcements, barricading, designated holding areas and dedicated control rooms. Emphasis was laid on advance planning, efficient passenger-flow management and coordinated deployment of security personnel to ensure safe and orderly passenger movement during peak periods.

Central Railway’s Pune Division highlighted Project DISHA (Dedicated Initiative for Safety, Harmony & Awareness), an initiative aimed at engaging children living near railway tracks through educational and recreational activities, safety awareness sessions and community-based interventions. Collaboration with NGOs, National Service Scheme (NSS) volunteers and local communities fosters awareness about railway safety and responsible behaviour, while discouraging stone-pelting, theft, trespassing and other unsafe practices.

Deliberations also covered joint RPF-GRP training, sabotage prevention and prompt information-sharing on narcotics detection. Digital evidence handling, standardised procedures, intelligence-sharing, strengthened investigative capabilities and supporting infrastructure were emphasised.

Addressing the gathering, the Chairman and CEO, Railway Board, highlighted the importance of coordinated efforts, technological advancements, innovation and a shared commitment among railway authorities, RPF, GRP and State Police to effectively address the evolving security challenges on Indian Railways. He also emphasised the need to build passenger confidence, ensure courteous and professional policing, and leverage technology and innovation to enhance productivity and operational efficiency.

The conference concluded with closing remarks by DG/RPF, who emphasised the need for intelligence-led policing to strengthen railway security.

****

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Manik Sharma

Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister congratulates Himanshu Nandal on winning Bronze at the Asian Para Games
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 10:19PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today congratulated Himanshu Nandal for winning Bronze in the Men’s 100m Freestyle S11 event at the Asian Para Games.

Shri Modi stated that with three Bronze medals to his name in this edition, he has shown impressive performance, expressing hope that he continues to excel and achieve greater success while wishing him the very best for the journey ahead.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister's Office shared:

"Congratulations to Himanshu Nandal on winning Bronze in the Men’s 100m Freestyle S11 event at the Asian Para Games! With three Bronze medals to his name in this edition, he has shown impressive performance. May he continue to excel and achieve greater success. Wishing him the very best for the journey ahead: PM @narendramodi"

With three Bronze medals to his name in this edition, he has shown impressive performance. May he continue to excel and achieve greater success. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-CRRI Inaugurates Indian Airport Pavement Symposium (IAPS 2026) in New Delhi
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 9:21PM by PIB Delhi

 

CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI), in association with Bharat Tiki Tar Shell India Private Limited (BTS), successfully organized the Indian Airport Pavement Symposium (IAPS 2026) today at the CSIR-CRRI Auditorium, New Delhi. Convened under the theme "Advancing Performance-Based Airport Pavements for a Resilient and Sustainable Aviation Future," the national symposium brought together key stakeholders—including regulators, airport operators, armed forces, academic leaders, and global pavement experts—to chart a comprehensive technical roadmap for India’s expanding airside infrastructure.

The symposium was inaugurated by Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, Government of India, and emphasized the importance of indigenous research and development, technological innovation and institutional collaboration in strengthening critical national transportation infrastructure.

As guest of honour Mr. Manoj Menon, Executive Director, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), delivered the special address, highlighting the role of industry-driven innovation and material technologies in meeting the evolving requirements of aviation infrastructure.

Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI, highlighted the Institute’s longstanding contributions to pavement engineering, road and airport infrastructure research, asset management and the development of technical standards. He underscored the importance of translating scientific research into practical engineering solutions to enhance the durability, safety and sustainability of airport pavements.

The welcome address and contextual remarks were delivered by Dr. Ashish Walia, Sr.Scientist, CSIR-CRRI & Organizing Secretary. The vote of thanks was proposed by Dr. K. Ravinder, Head, Information, Liaison and Training, CSIR-CRRI.

The technical sessions address key challenges in pavement planning, quality control, sustainable airfields, and modified bituminous materials. The symposium underscores CSIR-CRRI’s commitment to translating scientific research into innovative engineering solutions for India’s rapidly expanding aviation infrastructure.

A key highlight of the symposium was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between CSIR-CRRI and Bharat Tiki Tar Shell India Private Limited to promote collaborative research, technology development and deployment in advanced modified bituminous binders and specialized airport pavement solutions.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Soliciting public opinion and stake holders input on Design of Network Architecture for the proposed Broadband Public Protection and Disaster Relief (BB-PPDR) System
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) purposes to implement Pan India dedicated Broadband Public Protection and Disaster Relief (BB-PPDR) Network to provide Mission Critical Push-to-Talk (MCPTT), Mission Critical Data and Mission Critical Video capabilities to State/UT Police, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs), National Disaster Relief Force (NDRF), Fire Service, Medical Service and other public safety agencies across the country.

For designing the reference architecture, MHA is soliciting public opinion and stake holders input on Design of Network Architecture for the proposed Broadband Public Protection and Disaster Relief (BB-PPDR) Communication System. Inputs may be provided on design options, technology to be adopted, its’ comparative merits and de-merits, cost efficiency and suitability to Indian conditions. The Concept Note has been uploaded on the websites of MHA (Home/Documents/Orders and Circulars) and DCPW (Home/Documents/ Stakeholder Consultations, Home/Announcements & Home/What’s New).

All stakeholders are invited to send their comments/inputs to dd-ppdr@dcpw.gov.in and ad.ppdr@dcpw.gov.in latest by 5th November 2026, with the subject line “BB-PPDR Architecture — Stakeholder Feedback”.

item.description: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways India's First Maritime NBFC SMFCL Scales up with Rs 5,107 Crs Disbursed, Aims for Rs 60,205 Crs by 2031 Sarbananda Sonowal calls SMFCL's role vital to propel India's maritime growth under PM Narendra Modi's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 Maritime Development Fund (MDF) moves towards first close of Rs 5,000 crore Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal inaugurated the corporate office of Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL)…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
India's First Maritime NBFC SMFCL Scales up with Rs 5,107 Crs Disbursed, Aims for Rs 60,205 Crs by 2031
Sarbananda Sonowal calls SMFCL's role vital to propel India's maritime growth under PM Narendra Modi's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047
Maritime Development Fund (MDF) moves towards first close of Rs 5,000 crore
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:48PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal inaugurated the corporate office of Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL) at the Institute for Studies in Industrial Development (ISID) in New Delhi today, giving a permanent home to what he called India's first dedicated Non Banking Financial Company (NBFC) in the maritime sector.

The new office opens at a time of fast progress. As on 30 September 2026, SMFCL has sanctioned Rs 11,563 crore of financing and disbursed Rs 5,107 crore, with more than half of the sanctioned amount still to be drawn as projects advance.

The corporation's plan looks well beyond today. It aims to reach cumulative disbursements of Rs 60,205 crore by the end of FY2031, a build-up that depends on equity support to scale up in line with RBI norms and its debt-to-equity ratio.

"As India's first dedicated NBFC in the maritime sector, SMFCL is playing a pivotal role in mobilising long-term finance for port-led development, enhancing shipbuilding and coastal connectivity and catalysing the overall growth of our maritime economy. It has a vital role to play in propelling India’s maritime growth towards achieving the vision of PM Narendra Modi of becoming a leading maritime nation of the world by 2047,” Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The Maritime Development Fund (MDF), which has two components, is also taking shape. For its MIF component, SBI Ventures Limited has been appointed official Fund Manager. Registration as an Alternative Investment Fund with SEBI is due to be completed by the end of November, and the first close of Rs 5,000 crore is targeted by January, 2027.

The Interest Incentivisation Fund (IIF) is already delivering. Its online portal, www.iifmdf.in, is live, and loans of Rs 4,500 crore have been supported so far. About Rs 25 crore of interest subvention has been released against interest paid by borrowers.

"Under PM Narendra Modi’s transformative Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, India is building a stronger, more self-reliant and globally competitive maritime sector," Sonowal said.

The schemes SMFCL runs now cover a maritime project from first idea to final loan. The Government of India's contribution to the Maritime Investment Fund, up to Rs 9,800 crore, is channelled through SMFCL, while SBI Ventures, selected as Fund Manager, brings professional management to the fund.

The Interest Incentivisation Fund eases the cost of borrowing for eligible shipyards, with SMFCL working out the incentive, running the application and claims portal, and releasing the interest support. Under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme, the credit risk cover corpus is managed centrally and backed by premium and claims review, giving shipyards and lenders a safety net against payment risk.

SMFCL's own lending appraises, sanctions and monitors projects across ports, rail and road links, inland waterways, coastal infrastructure, port-hinterland logistics, shipbuilding and ship repair. It also oversees the release and use of Sagarmala and National Maritime Heritage Complex (NMHC) funds, so that money reaches projects and is tracked until it is spent.

 

***

item.description: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026 India Advances Agrivoltaics Cooperation for the Global South 7th AgriVoltaics World Conference concludes with a call to accelerate farmer-centred solutions; France to host the 8th edition in 2027 Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi India brought the priorities of farmers and the Global South to the heart of the agrivoltaics dialogue as the 7th AgriVoltaics World Conference (AWC) 2026, hosted by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India, concluded…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
AgriVoltaics World Conference 2026
India Advances Agrivoltaics Cooperation for the Global South
7th AgriVoltaics World Conference concludes with a call to accelerate farmer-centred solutions; France to host the 8th edition in 2027
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:33PM by PIB Delhi

India brought the priorities of farmers and the Global South to the heart of the agrivoltaics dialogue as the 7th AgriVoltaics World Conference (AWC) 2026, hosted by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India, concluded here today. Three days of scientific exchange, farmer experiences and industry engagement sharpened the focus on a shared opportunity of using agricultural land to produce food and solar power, strengthen farm incomes and advance the clean energy transition.

The conference highlighted India’s contribution as a platform for connecting research, field experience and international partnerships. Policymakers, researchers, industry leaders, development partners and farmers examined how agrivoltaics can respond to the linked challenges of food security, energy access and climate resilience across India and the Global South.

The focus was firmly on implementation. Discussions examined agro-climatic zoning, crop selection, water-use efficiency, innovative financing and technology, with farmer-centred models at the core. The deliberations reinforced the need for solutions that countries can adapt to their own agricultural conditions and development priorities.

A session co-convened by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the International Water Management Institute (IWMI) examined how agro-climatic zoning can guide agrivoltaic deployment. Discussions covered shade-tolerant crops, water-use efficiency indices and the microclimatic impacts of solar arrays across different agro-climatic zones.

These exchanges placed scientific evidence at the centre of expansion. India’s engagement in this research dialogue offers a basis for wider knowledge exchange with Global South partners seeking to integrate solar power with productive agriculture. Location-specific evidence will be essential to identifying what works for farmers and where it can be deployed effectively.

A dedicated session led by GIZ brought progressive farmers, Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) federations and rural entrepreneurs into the discussion. Participants shared experiences from agrivoltaic installations, covering operational lessons, revenue diversification and maintenance practices.

Their message gave the deliberations a clear practical direction: project design must respond to farmers’ needs and field conditions. For India and other Global South countries, economically viable models that sustain agricultural production will be central to wider adoption. Farmer experience must help shape how projects are designed, financed and operated.

Presenting an overview of the conference proceedings and key outcomes, Shri Ashish Khanna, Director General, International Solar Alliance (ISA), highlighted opportunities to advance agrivoltaics through research, innovation and international collaboration.

Addressing participants at the closing ceremony, Shri Mayank Tewari, Additional Secretary, MNRE, emphasised the importance of carrying the deliberations forward through continued collaboration and practical action.

The discussions brought renewed attention to the contribution India can make through shared learning and partnerships. Connecting Indian research and farmer experience with international expertise can help develop agrivoltaic approaches suited to diverse agricultural and energy needs across the Global South.

Dignitaries presented Excellence Awards recognising outstanding contributions to the agrivoltaics sector. The National Agrivoltaics Pitch-Hub Award recognised promising enterprise and start-up innovations with the potential to advance viable solutions.

Best Paper Awards across six scientific themes honoured research spanning system design, agronomy, monitoring, business models and socio-economic equity. The awards recognised the researchers, innovators and entrepreneurs working to turn scientific knowledge into practical advances for agriculture and renewable energy.

The closing ceremony marked the formal handover of hosting responsibility for the 8th AgriVoltaics World Conference in 2027 to France. The handover carried forward the momentum built in New Delhi and the continuing international effort to share knowledge, strengthen partnerships and advance agrivoltaic solutions across diverse farming contexts.

Ms. Taina Dyckhoff, Counsellor and Head of the Climate and Environment Division, Embassy of Germany in India, delivered the vote of thanks at the close of the ceremony.

New Delhi’s call to action was clear: bring agrivoltaics into the field through sound science, viable financing and sustained cooperation with farmers. By bringing these priorities together, India has helped strengthen a global dialogue rooted in the needs of the Global South. As the conference moves to France in 2027, the task ahead is to translate that momentum into solutions that make land more productive, diversify farmer incomes and expand clean energy for shared prosperity.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Legislative Department Reviews Office Cleanliness and Pendency under Special Campaign 6 to Promote Swachhata
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi

Legislative Department reviews its offices under ‘Special Campaign 6’ to institutionalise Swachhata and minimise pendency in government offices.

The Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, conducted a review of its various sections, office rooms and sanitation facilities on the 4th floor of Kartavya Bhawan 2, New Delhi, on 23rd October, 2026, under Special Campaign 6, aimed at institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency in government offices.

The review was led by Shri G. Panmei, Joint Secretary & Legislative Counsel (JS&LC) and Nodal Officer, along with Smt. Rachna, Under Secretary, and staff of the Admn.-II Section.

During the review, Shri Panmei inspected the cleanliness and upkeep of office premises and common facilities. He interacted with the officers and staff members and emphasised the importance of maintaining cleanliness, hygiene and proper organisation of official spaces. He also directed all Section Officers to ensure that their respective sections and rooms remain clean, well-organised and free from unnecessary and obsolete materials.

The review underscored the importance of collective responsibility, regular monitoring and the active participation of all officers and staff in maintaining a clean, hygienic and conducive working environment. The initiative reaffirmed the Legislative Department’s commitment to the objectives of Special Campaign 6 and to fostering a culture of cleanliness, efficiency and workplace discipline.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance Delhi Customs officers foil another major smuggling attempt at Air Cargo Complex, New Delhi Over 23 kg hydroponic weed seized worth around ₹8.12 crore Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi On the intervening night of 21 st /22 nd October, 2026 , Air Cargo Complex (ACC) Imports Commissionerate, Delhi Customs officers have made another major breakthrough in their ongoing investigation against narcotics trafficking networks. Preliminary testing confirmed the recovered substance to be Hydroponic Marijuana (Hydro Weed) . In…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Delhi Customs officers foil another major smuggling attempt at Air Cargo Complex, New Delhi
Over 23 kg hydroponic weed seized worth around ₹8.12 crore
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:11PM by PIB Delhi

On the intervening night of 21st/22nd October, 2026, Air Cargo Complex (ACC) Imports Commissionerate, Delhi Customs officers have made another major breakthrough in their ongoing investigation against narcotics trafficking networks. Preliminary testing confirmed the recovered substance to be Hydroponic Marijuana (Hydro Weed). In total, 23.220 kg of the narcotic substance was recovered and seized.

The seized narcotics are estimated to have a market value of approximately ₹8.12 crore, with an estimated street value of nearly ₹23 crore in India. The contraband, along with the concealment and packing materials used for smuggling, has been seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

Acting on intelligence gathered from the during the previous bust of 148.675 kg ganja from Bangkok, Customs officers intercepted another suspicious import consignment arriving from Bangkok, which had been declared as containing lamps. The earlier seizure led to the unearthing of a larger smuggling syndicate and triggered a series of coordinated follow-up operations across 11 locations in three States.

The consignment came under scrutiny following the interrogation of an individual found to be linked with the person arrested earlier on 15th October,2026 in the first seizure. Detailed examination of the shipment, conducted in the presence of the importer, revealed several lamps mounted on a wooden pallet. While the goods appeared innocuous, X-ray imaging indicated unusual patterns. Subsequent examination led officers to dismantle the base of the wooden pallet, resulting in the recovery of 23 vacuum-sealed packets containing a compressed green leafy substance concealed within the pallet structure.

The current operation led to the arrest of one more person on 22nd October, 2026, who was produced before the jurisdictional Magistrate in the late evening on the same day. Further investigation is on.

With this latest seizure, Delhi Customs has seized nearly 172 kg narcotics in the ongoing investigation and arrested two individuals, making significant dent in the trafficking network.

Delhi Customs remains steadfast in its commitment to safeguarding society from the menace of drugs through intelligence-driven enforcement, enhanced risk assessment, and coordinated inter-agency action. The Department will continue to maintain a high level of vigilance to detect and disrupt such criminal networks.

item.title: DRI seizes 5.6 kg of heroin in Phagwara, Punjab; Four drug traffickers arrested in intelligence-led operation
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance DRI seizes 5.6 kg of heroin in Phagwara, Punjab; Four drug traffickers arrested in intelligence-led operation Intelligence-led interception in Phagwara exposes an attempt to transport a substantial heroin consignment through the public transport network Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) in continuation to its crackdown on narcotics trafficking has seized 5.6 kg heroin, and arrested four persons in an intelligence-led operation conducted on 21 st October 2026 in Phagwara, near…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes 5.6 kg of heroin in Phagwara, Punjab; Four drug traffickers arrested in intelligence-led operation
Intelligence-led interception in Phagwara exposes an attempt to transport a substantial heroin consignment through the public transport network
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) in continuation to its crackdown on narcotics trafficking has seized 5.6 kg heroin, and arrested four persons in an intelligence-led operation conducted on 21st October 2026 in Phagwara, near Jalandhar, Punjab.

Acting on specific intelligence regarding the movement of narcotic drugs by some individuals travelling on a public transport bus, officers of DRI mounted a surveillance in the Phagwara area and intercepted a bus and four suspected individuals travelling as passengers were identified by the DRI team.

A personal search conducted in accordance with the provision of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, led to the recovery of five packets wrapped in yellow adhesive tape, concealed in a backpack kept on the lap of one of the suspects. Each of the five packets contained two smaller packets, making a total of ten packets. Field testing of the substance in all ten packets yielded positive results for Heroin, also commonly known as Chitta in Punjab. The total of 5.6 kg contraband was recovered, and was seized under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and all four persons allegedly involved in the transportation and possession of the contraband were arrested under the Act.

Heroin is a highly addictive opioid that depresses the central nervous system and carries a serious risk of dependence, respiratory depression, overdose and death. In India, it is a prohibited narcotic drug regulated under the NDPS Act, 1985. Unauthorised possession, trafficking, transport or sale attracts stringent penalties; for a commercial quantity, Section 21(c) prescribes rigorous imprisonment of 10–20 years and a fine of Rs. 1–2 lakh, with provision for a higher fine.  

This significant seizure in Punjab underscores DRI’s sustained efforts to disrupt narcotics supply chains, and bring those involved in the trafficking of illicit narcotics to justice.

****

KT/KMN

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI busts another attempt to circumvent ban on Pakistani goods under ‘operation deep manifest’; seizes around 25,000 kg Pakistan-origin watermelon seeds; two arrested
Investigation uncovers Dubai-routed transshipment and misdeclaration of country of origin; Detection of total 46,920 kg Pakistani origin watermelon and muskmelon seeds smuggled into the country
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), under Operation Deep Manifest, has unearthed another attempt to circumvent India’s prohibition on the import of goods originating in or exported from Pakistan. The operation, conducted between 11 September and 22 October 2026, led to the interception of a consignment of around 25,000 kg Pakistan-origin watermelon seeds that had been routed through Dubai and falsely declared as of UAE origin to evade the import prohibition. Two persons were arrested on 22nd October 2026.  

Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers examined a consignment of around 25,000 kg seeds, declared as of UAE-origin muskmelon seeds, imported through Nhava Sheva Port. Although, examination revealed that the goods were watermelon seeds, with evidence indicating their Pakistani origin.

Preliminary investigation revealed a deliberate transshipment arrangement designed to conceal the true origin of the goods. The seeds were initially shipped from Karachi Port, Pakistan, to Jebel Ali Port, Dubai, in one set of containers aboard a vessel. Following transshipment at Jebel Ali, the goods were transferred into another set of containers and loaded onto a different vessel for onward shipment to India. The change of containers and vessels, coupled with the misdeclaration of country of origin and fabricated import documentation, was intended to disguise the Pakistani origin of the consignment. The investigations yielded crucial documentary evidence, clearly establishing the movement of the consignment from Pakistan through Dubai to India, contradicting the declared UAE origin.

The investigation further revealed that the import was in contravention of the applicable import policy on two counts. First, the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan is prohibited under DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 2 May 2025. Second, watermelon seeds have been restricted for import into India with effect from 1 July 2024, vide DGFT Notification No. 02/2023 dated 5 April 2024. Accordingly, the consignment, having a market value of approximately Rs. 2.02 crore, was seized on 14 October 2026 under the relevant provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

Further investigation revealed that the importer had brought in an earlier consignment of 22,000 kg muskmelon seeds in February 2026 from the same Dubai-based supplier, declaring the goods as UAE-origin.  The evidences indicates that this consignment had also been transshipped, thus casting serious doubt on the declared country of origin.

Investigation has revealed the involvement of two related persons, the son and nephew of the Importer Exporter Code (IEC) holder, who were allegedly handling different legs of the operation. The son is the owner and director of the Dubai-based supplier firm, while his cousin was handling import-related formalities and domestic sales in India. Both persons were arrested on 22 October 2026.  

This operation follows DRI’s recent major enforcement actions against Pakistani-origin goods routed through third countries to evade India’s import prohibition. In September 2026, DRI seized over 362 metric tonnes of Pakistani-origin dry dates packed in 13 containers at CFS Ambad, Nashik, after uncovering their transshipment through Jebel Ali, Dubai, and misdeclaration of origin. More recently, in Oct.2026, DRI detected an illegal import of 295 containers carrying 7,311 metric tonnes of Pakistani-origin industrial/Himalayan rock salt routed through Colombo, Sri Lanka, using fabricated certificates of origin and invoices.

Following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, the Government of India prohibited the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, in the interest of national security and public policy, vide DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 2 May 2025.

DRI remains committed to identifying and dismantling networks engaged in customs fraud and the circumvention of import prohibitions, thereby safeguarding the integrity of India’s trade controls and economic security.

item.title: DDWS Organises National-level Training of Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 to Strengthen Community-led Rural Drinking Water Management
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Jal Shakti
item.description: Ministry of Jal Shakti DDWS Organises National-level Training of Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 to Strengthen Community-led Rural Drinking Water Management Story-based capacity-building package launched to strengthen grassroots leadership and sustainable management of village water supply systems Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:04PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised a National-level Training of Trainers (ToT) programme for State-Level Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 today…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
DDWS Organises National-level Training of Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 to Strengthen Community-led Rural Drinking Water Management
Story-based capacity-building package launched to strengthen grassroots leadership and sustainable management of village water supply systems
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 8:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised a National-level Training of Trainers (ToT) programme for State-Level Trainers under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 today at India Habitat Centre, New Delhi. The programme brought together representatives from State Institutes of Rural Development (SIRDs), Public Health Engineering Departments (PHEDs), Rural Development institutions and other key stakeholders from State/UTs to strengthen capacities for large-scale community training and institutional development aimed at sustaining rural drinking water services across the country.

The training programme focused on the newly developed Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 Capacity Building Package comprising of 8 Modules titled “The Story of Panipur: A Story-Based self-learning Handbook on Rural Drinking Water Supply Management” and a “Trainer’s Facilitation Manual”. The package has been designed to build the capacities of Gram Panchayat representatives, Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), Sujalam Shakti Groups and other grassroots institutions involved in the management and sustainability of rural drinking water services.

Delivering the keynote address, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission, stressed that the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water systems depends fundamentally on community ownership and institutional responsibility. The drinking water infrastructure being created today is intended to serve rural communities for the next several decades and therefore requires active participation of GPs, VWSCs and community groups from the very beginning.

He emphasised that achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 would require not only creation of infrastructure but also sustained efforts to ensure its effective operation and maintenance through strong local institutions.

Referring to emerging examples of improved service delivery in several States, Shri Soan highlighted the need to prepare village institutions for progressively higher service standards and sustainable management of water supply systems. He urged participants to instil a strong sense of ownership among Panchayat representatives and community institutions so that drinking water infrastructure is viewed as a community asset that must be preserved and maintained collectively.

A key focus of his address was the convergence of JJM with Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs), Panchayati Raj Institutions, Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) and dovetail from 16th Finance Commission tied grants and VB-G RAM G. He urged States to ensure that Panchayat representatives understand the financial resources and planning instruments available to them so that water source sustainability, operation and maintenance requirements and local drinking water priorities are adequately incorporated into development plans.

Shri Soan further highlighted the importance of user-charge collection, financial sustainability, source protection and community monitoring for ensuring the long-term functionality of rural water supply systems.

Calling for institutionalisation of the training programme, he urged States to integrate the capacity-building modules into existing Rural Development and Panchayati Raj training systems so that learning and capacity building continue beyond the Mission period and become part of a sustained support mechanism for rural drinking water service delivery.

Smt. Swati Meena Naik, Joint Secretary, Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation, emphasised the critical importance of capacity building in ensuring the long-term success of the Mission. She observed that while significant investments are being made in creating rural drinking water infrastructure, the sustainability of these assets depends on informed communities and capable local institutions that can effectively operate, maintain and manage drinking water systems over time. Emphasising on the purpose of the training she said, it is not merely to impart technical knowledge but to enable trainers to communicate complex concepts in a simple, practical and relatable manner to village communities. She noted that the newly developed modules employ storytelling, folk communication methods, role plays, community interactions and gamification techniques to make learning more engaging and effective.

She highlighted that the ultimate objective of the initiative is to strengthen community-led management of rural drinking water systems by building the capacities. Village-level institutions are expected to play an increasingly important role in water distribution, operation and maintenance, user-charge management, grievance redressal, functionality monitoring and service improvement planning.

Smt. Naik also emphasised the importance of transparency and equitable access to information through digital platforms and dashboards, enabling citizens, Gram Panchayats and higher administrative levels to access programme information uniformly and participate more effectively in rural water governance. Noting that nearly 54 lakh stakeholders are proposed to be covered under the broader training programme, she urged State/UTs to establish robust dissemination mechanisms and training ecosystems to enable timely implementation.

Smt. Meena also highlighted the role of technology-enabled governance through initiatives such as Sujalam Bharat and layered dashboards. She emphasised that digital platforms should become tools for transparency, accountability and informed decision-making, enabling Gram Panchayats and citizens to actively monitor and improve service delivery. Emphasising the role of Sujalam Shakti Groups and noted that the initiative offers significant opportunities for women’s leadership, community mobilisation and livelihood enhancement while strengthening drinking water governance at the grassroots level.

In his concluding remarks, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM, emphasised that the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water services depends on community ownership, responsible water use and effective local management of water supply systems. He underlined the importance of protecting drinking water sources for future generations and called upon States to sensitise communities on water conservation, source sustainability and judicious water use as integral components of the capacity-building initiative.

Shri Soan highlighted that user charges should be viewed not merely as a financial mechanism, but as a tool for fostering responsibility and ownership among rural communities towards their drinking water systems. Stressing the distinction between water as a natural resource and drinking water service delivery, he observed that user contributions help communities appreciate the investments, operation and maintenance efforts involved in delivering safe drinking water to households and encourage greater participation in sustaining these services.

He further emphasised that while Panchayats should take a leading role in the day-to-day operation and management of village water supply systems, technical support from the concerned departments would continue to remain essential for addressing major repairs and technical challenges. Referring to the transformative impact of household tap water connections on dignity, convenience and equitable access to drinking water, he urged the participants to carry forward the key messages of community ownership, behavioural change, water conservation and institutional responsibility during the rollout of training programmes across States and Union Territories.

Resource persons from NJJM viz. Director, Deputy Secretary, Deputy Advisor and NPMU members introduced the story-based self-learning handbook and Trainer’s Facilitation Manual and delivered the training. The training package, built around the fictional village “Panipur”, comprises eight interconnected modules covering village water supply systems, source sustainability, water quality, institutional arrangements, operation and maintenance, digital governance, community ownership and the development of sustainable Sujal Gaons. The modules have been designed to promote participatory learning and help communities translate knowledge into practical action.

Representatives from partner organizations UNICEF and UNOPS shared their field experiences, key considerations, and practical approaches for preparing trainers and conducting effective grassroots-level training, while adhering to the prescribed module content and coordinating with SIRDs. They also assured that in their implementing states; they will support the state PHE/Rural Water Supply Department in delivering state-level and district-level trainings.

The National-level Training of Trainers marks an important step in operationalising the capacity-building architecture of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. By creating a strong network of State Master Trainers and equipping them with standardised training resources, the Mission seeks to strengthen Gram Panchayats, VWSCs and community institutions, deepen community ownership, and ensure the sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure and services across the country.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
A high-level team lead by Chairperson, CAQM reviews Paddy Stubble Management measures in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:32PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level team led by the Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), visited thermal power and CBG plants, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), farm fields and biomass plant in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar in the State of Punjab. The team reviewed the preparedness and took stock of various in-situ and ex-situ measures being implemented on ground for effective paddy straw management and prevention of stubble burning incidents during the ongoing paddy harvesting season. CAQM directed the State authorities to achieve co-firing targets in thermal power plants with special focus on ensuring compliance with emission norms. During the visit to KVK, the team saw demonstration of machinery for in-situ and ex-situ use.

The team also assessed the adequacy and availability of machinery to facilitate farmers in managing paddy residue. In addition, the team reviewed the arrangements and mechanisms in place for the maximum utilisation of paddy straw in thermal power plants and biomass plants utilizing paddy stubble as part of ex-situ management.

With paddy harvesting gaining momentum, the Commission emphasized the need for intensified and concerted efforts by all concerned authorities to ensure that farmers have adequate access to CRM Machinery on time. The Commission directed that facilitation of farmers be maximized, with particular focus on ensuring the availability and effective deployment of machinery in accordance with the emerging requirements during the peak harvesting period.

The Commission directed State Authorities to strengthen these ecosystems for paddy stubble management to minimize stubble burning incidents. The need for proactive field-level monitoring and timely resolution of operational gaps was also emphasized to ensure effective implementation of the ongoing paddy straw management interventions.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chairs 30th Meeting of Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) in New Delhi, today
FSDC reviews macro-financial stability amid rising geopolitical uncertainties, AI boom and sharp rise in global bond yields
FSDC stresses heightened vigilance and proactive measures to mitigate emerging risks to India’s financial stability
Union Finance Minister calls for more frequent FSDC meetings amid global economic uncertainties
FSDC deliberates on strengthening domestic investment ecosystem, enhancing capital flows and deepening financial sector reforms
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:30PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 30th Meeting of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) along with FSDC members in New Delhi, today.

The FSDC, inter alia, deliberated on issues related to macro financial stability and India’s preparedness to deal with them. Considering the importance of regulatory improvisation and digital modernization in the financial sector, the FSDC discussed measures towards promoting innovation in the Fintech sector and exploring the prospects of tokenisation of financial assets and other real-world assets.

The Council reviewed the cyber resilience of the Indian financial sector and took note of the Financial Sector Cyber Security Strategy (FSCSS) formulated by an Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG) comprising of financial sector regulators and cybersecurity agencies, in coordination with the DEA, DFS and MeitY. The implementation of the FSCSS is expected to strengthen the overall resilience of the Indian financial sector. The discussions also covered India’s preparedness to protect the Critical Information Infrastructure and resilience of protection systems and improving cybersecurity preparedness of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs).

The FSDC also discussed issues relating to formulating a strategy for implementing the past decisions and the budget announcements, which included:

  • strengthening the domestic investment ecosystem and improve resource flow for investment including in the GIFT-IFSC;
  • simplification and digitalization of the KYC processes and digital onboarding for NRIs and FPIs;
  • reforms to scale up DPIs in India including the Account Aggregator and Unified Lending Interface (ULI) framework with specific focus on MSMEs;
  • reducing cost of intermediation in the financial sector, improving the responsiveness of regulations and rationalization of Credit Guarantee Schemes in India.

The FSDC took cognizance of the emerging trends from domestic and global macro-financial situation and stressed upon the need to be vigilant especially in view of the ongoing geopolitical uncertainties, AI boom and steep rise in global bond yields. The Council recognised the need for proactive efforts to mitigate potential risks to financial stability while adopting adequate safeguards for financial system’s resilience. The members decided to strengthen the inter-regulatory coordination for wider development of the financial sector.

The Union Finance Minister also urged the regulators and stakeholders concerned to expedite the process of refund of unclaimed assets (banks deposits, dividends, shares, post office accounts, insurance and pension funds etc.) to their rightful owners.

The FSDC noted the success undertaken by stakeholders under “Your Money, Your Right” campaign at the district level to refund the existing unclaimed financial assets and guided Ministries and Regulators to pursue additional efforts for timely refund to rightful owners.

Given rising geopolitical headwinds and global uncertainty, Smt. Sitharaman urged the Council to hold FSDC meetings at more frequent intervals with a predefined schedule.

The FSDC also took note of the activities undertaken by the FSDC Sub-Committee chaired by the Governor, RBI, and the action taken on the pending past decisions of the FSDC.

The FSDC meeting was also attended by Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor, Reserve Bank of India; Ms. Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance; Shri Sanjay Lohiya, Secretary, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance; Shri Arvind Shrivastava, Secretary, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance; Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology; Dr. Pallavi Jain Govil, Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser, Ministry of Finance; Shri Tuhin Kanta Pandey, Chairperson, Securities and Exchange Board of India; Shri Ajay Seth, Chairperson, Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India; Shri K. Rajaraman, Chairperson, International Financial Services Centres Authority; Shri S. Ramann, Chairperson, Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority; Shri Jayanti Prasad, Acting Chairperson, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India; Dr. Sanjay Bahl, Director General, Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In); and Ms. Aparna Sinha, Secretary of the FSDC, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance.

The Inter-Caste Marriage Incentive Scheme implemented by the Government of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
A New Beginning Through the Inter-Caste Marriage Incentive Scheme
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:25PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of Mr. Amit Patil and Mrs. Sneha Deshmukh (names changed) reflects the positive impact of the progressive initiative with regard to encouraging inter caste marriage in order to establish a tradition of inter community harmony and peaceful co-existence besides strengthening equality, mutual respect and social harmony.

The Inter-Caste Marriage Incentive Scheme implemented by the Government of Maharashtra encourages inter-caste marriages and promotes a society free from caste-based discrimination.

After their marriage, the couple faced financial constraints and social challenges while establishing their new household and adjusting to their responsibilities as a family. These challenges made it difficult to manage daily expenses, purchase essential household items and plan for their future financial security.

During this important phase of their life, financial assistance under the Inter-Caste Marriage Incentive Scheme provided valuable support. The assistance helped the couple purchase essential household items, meet daily needs and take initial steps towards securing their financial future. It eased some of the financial pressures associated with beginning a new life together and strengthened their confidence in building an independent and stable household.

Beyond its immediate financial benefits, the scheme carries a broader social message. Inter-caste marriages can help break down caste-based barriers, foster mutual understanding between communities and encourage a culture of equality and inclusion. By supporting eligible couples who take this progressive step, the scheme reinforces the values of fraternity, dignity and social unity.

For Mr. Amit Patil and Mrs. Sneha Deshmukh, the assistance has been an encouraging step towards a more secure and self-reliant future. Their experience highlights how targeted government support can help couples navigate the initial challenges of married life while advancing the larger objective of social integration.

The couple expresses sincere gratitude to the Government and the Social Welfare Department for implementing this beneficial initiative. They hope that more eligible couples will benefit from the scheme and build stable family lives founded on equality, mutual respect and understanding.

Their journey demonstrates that welfare initiatives can extend beyond financial assistance to promote meaningful social change and contribute to an inclusive society where individuals are respected beyond the boundaries of caste.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
Department of Rural Development Makes Steady Progress Under Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Rural Development is implementing Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata, reduce pendency and dispose of e-waste. It was launched on 2 October 2026 with a pledge administered by Secretary (Rural Development), followed by Shramdaan at Kartavya Bhavan-03.

Between 2 and 23 October, the Department achieved 100% of its targets for cleanliness campaigns and IMC references. It reached 77% for public grievance appeals, 76% for physical file review, 69% for public grievances and 63% for e-file review. Progress stood at 60% for Parliament assurances, 51% for references from MPs, 50% for State Government references and 33% for PMO references.

So far, 690 physical files have been weeded out and 1,177 e-files closed. The Department's store at India Habitat Centre was also cleared of unused furniture and equipment. Disposal of e-waste and unused furniture is expected to generate about ₹15.29 lakh and free up 43,186 sq ft of office space.

Other activities included the Nirmal Desk Challenge, distribution of indoor plants and anti-tobacco awareness. Essay and poster competitions were held, and Safaimitras were felicitated. On 22 October, the Department held a health camp in coordination with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for over 250 outsourced staff, including Safai Karamcharis. The camp offered blood pressure, blood sugar, eye and ENT check-ups.

The Department aims to achieve 100% of its targets by 31 October 2026.

The journey of Amit (Name Changed), a 31-year-old man from Kamrup Metropolitan district of Assam, highlights how coordinated medical care and sustained rehabilitation can support…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Critical Overdose To Sustained Recovery
Kamrup Assam’s Amit’s Journey Of Hope And Rehabilitation
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:12PM by PIB Delhi

Timely medical intervention, evidence-based treatment and continued family support plays an important role in helping individuals overcome substance dependence and rebuild their lives.

The journey of Amit (Name Changed), a 31-year-old man from Kamrup Metropolitan district of Assam, highlights how coordinated medical care and sustained rehabilitation can support long-term recovery and social reintegration.

Amit is a graduate and self-employed individual whose journey towards recovery began following a life-threatening heroin overdose. He was admitted to the emergency department of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Guwahati, with severe respiratory depression requiring urgent medical attention. During his hospitalisation, he was also diagnosed with Hepatitis C. His opioid dependence had significantly affected his health and overall well-being, making timely and comprehensive treatment essential.

Despite these challenges, Amit remained motivated to overcome substance dependence. The encouragement and practical support of his family played an important role in helping him continue treatment and work towards recovery. Following initial stabilisation, he was shifted to the Neuropsychiatry ward, where he was initiated on Opioid Substitution Therapy (OST) using buprenorphine. He also received medical care for Hepatitis C and underwent relapse prevention therapy, addressing both his medical needs and the psychosocial challenges associated with substance dependence.

After discharge, Amit continued treatment under medical supervision, including buprenorphine-naloxone medication, psychosocial interventions, nursing support and regular follow-up consultations. Continuous monitoring and counselling helped him adhere to his treatment plan and maintain progress towards recovery. The coordinated approach ensured that his treatment extended beyond emergency care to include ongoing support for his physical and psychological well-being.

An important milestone in Amit’s rehabilitation was securing employment within two to three months of recovery. This achievement enabled him to resume productive activities, contribute financially to his family and regain greater stability in his personal and social life. His progress demonstrated how appropriate treatment and continued support can help individuals rebuild their livelihoods and move towards greater independence.

Amit has maintained adherence to treatment and abstinence from substance use for over a year without relapse. With his recovery progressing steadily, his medication doses are now being gradually reduced under medical supervision. His journey reflects the importance of timely emergency care, evidence-based treatment, relapse prevention, regular follow-up and family involvement in supporting sustained recovery from substance dependence.

Through the Addiction Treatment Facility (ATF) at AIIMS Guwahati, Amit received coordinated medical and psychosocial support that helped him move from a life-threatening emergency towards sustained recovery. His experience highlights the importance of accessible treatment and rehabilitation services in helping individuals regain their health, strengthen family relationships, rebuild livelihoods and reintegrate into society. His journey offers a message of hope that, with appropriate treatment, continued support and personal commitment, recovery from substance dependence is possible.

UP Government presented 11 key initiatives that the State Government has taken so far and the activities…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Secretary (MoEFCC) reviews UP Government's Action Plan to address Air Pollution in Delhi NCR
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:11PM by PIB Delhi

Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, Shri Narendra Bhooshan, today reviewed the action plans of Uttar Pradesh State Government and Urban local bodies, to address the air pollution in Delhi-NCR and winter preparedness.

UP Government presented 11 key initiatives that the State Government has taken so far and the activities planned to achieve the saturation of air quality improvement interventions address various sources of air pollution namely, road dust, construction and demolition (C&D) activities, open burning of biomass, vehicular pollution, traffic decongestion, industrial pollution, greening, paddy stubble management. The State Government in coordination with various agencies and local bodies has already implemented several measures which have achieved considerable progress.

The Secretary reviewed various interventions such as redevelopment of roads, traffic decongestion at hotspots, deployment of electric buses and EV charging infrastructure, establishing the solid waste processing facilities for processing of 100% solid waste generation, remediation of legacy waste dump sites, C&D waste processing facilities and secondary collection centres, monitoring and enforcement of air pollution control measures at Construction sites and industries.

While reviewing progress on interventions concerning vehicular pollution, Shri Bhooshan requested that State Government needs to actively engage truck and bus associations for faster adoption of benefits under PARIVARTAN scheme for replacing old trucks and buses. He suggested that Transport Department should play facilitative and proactive role in providing NOC for shifting of old vehicles out of NCR. The Secratary urged the State for faster installation of ANPR cameras at all fuel stations to enforce ‘No PUCC No fuel’ policy to address vehicular pollution.

Shri Bhooshan reviewed the adequacy of C&D waste processing facilities proportionate to C&D waste generation. He suggested that Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) already functional in several cities can integrate monitoring and enforcement actions such as remote monitoring of construction sites, tracking of vehicles carrying C&D waste and solid waste, mechanical road sweeping, traffic decongestion, functioning of mechanical road sweepers, etc. He has also suggested that Dust portal developed by UP Pollution Control Board for monitoring construction sites. It was informed that the State has already achieved the greening targets. The Secretary suggested that Urban local bodies must be encouraged to develop Namo Vans under Nagar Van Yojana of MoEF&CC.

Shri Bhooshan also reviewed the preparedness of industries installing Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) to meet the revised emission norms by specific category of industries as prescribed by CAQM. UP Pollution Control Board and Industry Departments were suggested to hold meetings with industries and associations to closely monitor the implementation and remove bottlenecks.

The meeting has been attended by the senior officials of Union Ministries of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Power; Road Transport and Highways, besides CAQM, CPCB, NCR Planning Board, and various Departments of Uttar Pradesh State Government, Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board along with District Collectors and Municipal Commissioners of Ghaziabad, Meerut, Noida, Greater Noida, Bulandsahr, Hapur, Baghpat, Muzaffarnagar and Shamli.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Electronics & IT
item.description: Ministry of Electronics & IT STPI inaugurates new incubation facility in Dehradun to strengthen Uttarakhand’s technology and startup ecosystem 30,000 sq. ft. facility to support IT/ITeS companies, startups and technology-driven entrepreneurship in the state New facility to provide modern infrastructure and a collaborative environment for innovation, product development and employment generation Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
STPI inaugurates new incubation facility in Dehradun to strengthen Uttarakhand’s technology and startup ecosystem
30,000 sq. ft. facility to support IT/ITeS companies, startups and technology-driven entrepreneurship in the state
New facility to provide modern infrastructure and a collaborative environment for innovation, product development and employment generation
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, inaugurated its new incubation facility at IT Park, Sahastradhara Road, Dehradun, Uttarakhand. The facility was inaugurated by Shri Jitin Prasada, Hon’ble Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology and Commerce & Industry, Government of India, in the presence of Shri Pradeep Batra, Hon’ble Minister of IT & Good Governance, Government of Uttarakhand, and Shri Ganesh Joshi, Hon’ble Agriculture Minister, Government of Uttarakhand. The new facility aims to strengthen the state’s IT/ITeS ecosystem by providing modern infrastructure to technology companies and startups, while fostering innovation, entrepreneurship, product development and employment generation.

Spread across approximately 30,000 sq. ft. across four floors, the new incubation facility offers semi-furnished office spaces, high-speed internet connectivity, an air-conditioned and eco-friendly working environment, an auditorium, two meeting rooms, two conference rooms and a Network Operations Centre (NOC). The facility has been designed to provide a conducive working environment for technology enterprises, enabling collaboration, business development and growth.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Jitin Prasada, Hon’ble Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology and Commerce & Industry, Government of India, said, “India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation is driven by two key engines: technology and trade. In an increasingly interconnected world, technological self-reliance is essential to ensure that the country is not dependent on external sources for critical technologies such as semiconductors. The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated how chip shortages can disrupt entire industries, underscoring the importance of building domestic manufacturing capabilities. Our focus on strengthening the semiconductor and electronics manufacturing ecosystem is aimed at securing India’s technological future while continuing to engage with the world and adopt global best practices.”

He further added, “STPI’s new incubation facility in Dehradun will provide a vibrant environment where startups and technology enterprises can collaborate, exchange ideas and develop innovative solutions. With Uttarakhand already having more than 1700 recognised startups, such initiatives can further strengthen the state’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. Alongside efforts to promote electronics manufacturing, including component manufacturing and the development of an Electronics Manufacturing Cluster in Kashipur, this facility will help attract investment, generate employment and create opportunities for young talent. Our aim is to build a self-reliant India that is equipped to compete globally and contributes meaningfully to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

Shri Pradeep Batra, Hon’ble Cabinet Minister of IT & Good Governance, Government of Uttarakhand, said, “The vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 goes beyond infrastructure development; it requires a transformation in our thinking, our aspirations and our commitment to the nation. Uttarakhand, our Devbhoomi, has immense potential to progress further, supported by the capabilities and dedication of its people. As the state attracts growing interest from tourists and businesses, strengthening infrastructure and improving access to modern facilities will be essential to meeting these aspirations. Initiatives such as STPI’s new incubation facility in Dehradun will help create an enabling environment for technology, innovation and entrepreneurship, contributing to Uttarakhand’s growth and India’s larger vision of a developed nation.”

Shri Ganesh Joshi, Hon’ble Agriculture Minister, Government of Uttarakhand, said, “Inspired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat, we must create opportunities for our youth beyond the traditional IT hubs. Dehradun, already recognised as an education hub, has the potential to emerge as a prominent IT destination like Bengaluru and Hyderabad. I am confident that this new centre will open up new avenues for growth, strengthen Uttarakhand’s technology ecosystem and create greater opportunities for young people over the next five years.”

Shri Pankaj Pandey, IT Secretary, Government of Uttarakhand, said, “The new STPI incubation facility is a major addition to Uttarakhand’s technology ecosystem, offering young entrepreneurs the infrastructure and support including initiatives like the Centre of Entrepreneurship to convert their expertise into successful businesses. Alongside this entrepreneurial push, Uttarakhand is advancing digital governance by offering around 1,000 services online. Together, these combined efforts strengthen the state’s digital footprint, encourage innovation, and unlock new opportunities for Uttarakhand’s youth.”

Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, said, “One of STPI’s key strengths is its nationwide network, which enables startups to access investors, expertise and technology solutions from across the country, beyond their immediate ecosystem. The new incubation facility in Dehradun will provide infrastructure for emerging IT/ITeS enterprises looking to establish or expand their operations, while also supporting startups through mentorship, industry connections and Centres of Entrepreneurship focused on addressing real-world challenges, including cybersecurity. The facility will help to create a comprehensive support ecosystem for technology-led businesses in Uttarakhand. With the state government strengthening its focus on IT/ITeS and startup policies, we believe Uttarakhand is well positioned to accelerate the growth of its technology and startup ecosystem.”

Established in 2001 with the support of the Government of Uttarakhand, STPI Dehradun has been working to promote and support the state’s IT/ITeS industry through incubation services and the implementation of STP, Non-STP and EHTP schemes. The existing incubation facility at IT Park, Dehradun, offers approximately 19,533 sq. ft. of super built-up space, with multiple IT/ITeS units currently availing its facilities. The new facility will further augment the infrastructure available to technology enterprises in the region.

STPI Dehradun’s initiatives also extend to startup development and funding support. Under the Next Generation Incubation Scheme (NGIS), 52 startups have been selected through challenge programmes, with 17 receiving seed funding amounting to ₹4.25 crore and more than 26 receiving stipends of ₹90,000 each. These initiatives complement STPI’s broader efforts to encourage technology innovation, support emerging entrepreneurs and facilitate the development of scalable products and solutions.

The inauguration marks a further step towards strengthening Uttarakhand’s technology ecosystem by improving access to incubation infrastructure and fostering collaboration among government, industry, academia and entrepreneurs. Through its continued engagement with stakeholders, STPI aims to support the growth of IT/ITeS enterprises, promote innovation and intellectual property creation and contribute to technology-led economic development and employment generation in the state.

About STPI:

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), engaged in promoting the IT/ITES industry, innovation, research and development, startups, and product and intellectual property creation in emerging technology domains. These include the Internet of Things, blockchain, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, robotics, augmented and virtual reality, animation and visual effects, and data science and analytics. STPI supports innovation across domains such as gaming, fintech, agritech, medtech, autonomous and connected mobility, ESDM, cybersecurity, Industry 4.0 and drones.

****

The Mela is showcasing India’s rich and diverse heritage of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026
Visitors Witness India’s Rich And Diverse Heritage Of Traditional Handicrafts And Handloom Products At Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati
Galaxy Of Artists Present Traditional Musical And Dance Programmes 
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi

As part of bringing together artisans from across the country, including the North-Eastern States, the 08 days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 is underway at Guwahati, the State Capital of Assam.

The Mela is showcasing India’s rich and diverse heritage of traditional handicrafts and handloom products.

Organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, the Mela will continue until October 28 Wednesday.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela remains open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock. He said the visitors are exploring the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.

The visitors are also enthralled to witness a galaxy of artists presenting traditional musical and dance programmes.

 

The Official said a total of 75 artisans, including 31 women artisans, are participating in the Mela, displaying approximately 40 varieties of handloom and handicraft products.

He said the event is providing participating artisans with a platform to exhibit and sell their products directly to visitors, establish connections with prospective customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach.

 

By facilitating direct interaction between artisans and consumers, the Mela seeks to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and improve livelihood opportunities for participating artisans, he added.

The Official said the Guwahati edition features a wide range of traditional crafts and handloom products representing different regions of India.

The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added.

He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.

The Official further said a key focus of the Mela is the promotion of BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), an initiative aimed at facilitating the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms.

 

By promoting access to wider markets and digital channels, the initiative is aimed to strengthen market linkages, expand customer outreach and create additional opportunities for artisans to enhance their earnings.

 

It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.

The Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM-2026) is an important initiative of the Ministry to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC).

The first edition of SSM 2026 concluded in Mysuru on October 19, with thousands of visitors thronging the nine days Mela at Dasara Exhibition Ground, Mysuru in Karnataka.

Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”, the Mela is promotiong the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs).

 

The Mela is providing a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.

In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela is creating awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations.

The initiative is complementing financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.

It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of communities having financial constraints, by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.

The Mela is enhancing the visibility of participating artisans, expanding awareness of their products and encouraging greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Holds High-Level Economic Engagements in Berlin to Strengthen India–Germany Trade and Investment Ties
Shri Piyush Goyal and German Federal Minister Katherina Reiche Discuss Industrial Cooperation and India–EU FTA
Posted On: 23 OCT 2026 5:08PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal held a series of high-level engagements in Berlin on October 22nd to strengthen India–Germany trade, investment and industrial cooperation. The engagements included a bilateral meeting with German Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy Ms. Katherina Reiche, the inauguration of the India Centre at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP), an India–Germany Business Roundtable and participation in the Berlin Global Dialogue.

During the bilateral meeting, Shri Piyush Goyal and Ms. Reiche discussed opportunities for closer industrial collaboration and the potential of the India–EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) to expand bilateral trade and investment. The two Ministers jointly inaugurated DGAP’s India Centre in Berlin, which is intended to promote policy research and dialogue on India–Germany relations.

The Union Ministers also co-chaired an India–Germany Business Roundtable organised with DGAP and the Asia-Pacific Committee of German Business (APA), with participation from German CEOs and business leaders. In their keynote addresses, Shri Goyal addressed accelerating growth and forging a new trade era, while Ms. Reiche spoke on transforming the FTA into industrial reality. The subsequent interaction focused on translating the prospective India–EU FTA into concrete trade and investment opportunities.

At the Berlin Global Dialogue, Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the panel discussion titled “New Era, New Alliances: The Third Path?” alongside Personal Representative of the German Chancellor for Investment, Mr. Martin Blessing; Singapore’s Minister for Manpower and Minister-in-charge of Energy and Science & Technology, Dr. Tan See Leng; and Chairwoman and CEO of Marcegaglia Steel, Ms. Emma Marcegaglia and the session was moderated by Prof. Dr. Lars-Hendrik Röller. Shri Goyal highlighted the importance of trust, complementary economic strengths and resilient supply chains in international partnerships.

Shri Goyal also held individual meetings with Member of the Board of Management of Bayer AG, Mr. Stefan Oelrich, and President of its Pharmaceuticals Division; Mr. Murat Akyildiz, Managing Partner of Knauf Group; and CEO of Fresenius SE & Co. KGaA, Mr. Michael Sen, to explore opportunities for business and investment cooperation.

Shri Goyal is accompanied on his visit to Germany and the Netherlands by a delegation of around 100 Indian businesses and startups. The Berlin engagements form part of ongoing efforts to deepen the India–Germany Strategic Partnership, particularly in trade, investment, technology and industrial cooperation.
