item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
8 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 To Begin in Guwahati Tomorrow
75 Artisans, Including 31 Women, to Showcase Around 40 Varieties of Handloom and Handicraft Products
Mela to Promote Market Access, Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Livelihoods for Artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs)
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 7:55PM by PIB Delhi

The 08 days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will begin in State Capital Guwahati of Assam, from tomorrow. The Mela is being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, until October 28 Wednesday.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela will be open to public at Farm Gate, Khanapara, Guwahati, from 11 A.M. onwards till 9 O’ Clock. He said the visitors will explore the diverse range of traditional products to purchase the creations and support the artisans.

He said the Mela will bring together artisans from across the country, including the North-Eastern States, to showcase India’s rich and diverse heritage of traditional handicrafts and handloom products.

The Official said a total of 75 artisans, including 31 women artisans, are participating in the Mela, displaying approximately 40 varieties of handloom and handicraft products.

He said the event will provide participating artisans with a platform to exhibit and sell their products directly to visitors, establish connections with prospective customers and explore opportunities to expand their market reach. By facilitating direct interaction between artisans and consumers, the Mela seeks to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and improve livelihood opportunities for participating artisans, he added.

The Official said the Guwahati edition will feature a wide range of traditional crafts and handloom products representing different regions of India. The participation of artisans from the North-Eastern States, alongside those from other parts of the country, will provide visitors with an opportunity to appreciate the diversity of India’s artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and cultural heritage, he added.

He said the event aims to also encourage greater appreciation of the skills and creativity of artisans whose work contributes to preserving traditional knowledge and craft practices.

The Official further said a key focus of the Mela will be the promotion of BHARAT-TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), an initiative aimed at facilitating the marketing of products made by artisans belonging to the target groups through physical outlets and e-commerce platforms. By promoting access to wider markets and digital channels, the initiative seeks to strengthen market linkages, expand customer outreach and create additional opportunities for artisans to enhance their earnings. It also supports the preservation and promotion of traditional arts and crafts by connecting artisans and their products with evolving consumer markets, he said.

Shilp Samagam Mela (SSM-2026) is an important initiative of the Ministry to provide marketing support to artisans and beneficiaries associated with its three National Corporations: the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), and the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC).

The first edition of SSM 2026 concluded in Mysuru on October 19, with thousands of visitors thronging the nine days Mela at Dasara Exhibition Ground, Mysuru in Karnataka.

Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas”, the Mela seeks to promote the economic empowerment of artisans belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Safai Mitras and Denotified Tribes (DNTs). It provides a dedicated platform for these communities to showcase their skills, market their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance through sustainable livelihood opportunities.

In addition to promoting the sale of traditional products, the Mela will help create awareness among visitors and participating communities about the welfare, financial assistance and development schemes implemented by the Ministry and its three National Corporations. The initiative seeks to complement financial and developmental support with market-oriented interventions, enabling artisans to translate their traditional skills and craftsmanship into viable livelihood opportunities, the official said.

It is pertinent to mention that through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to advance its efforts towards the socio-economic empowerment of disadvantaged  communities by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating market access and supporting sustainable livelihoods.

The Mela is expected to enhance the visibility of participating artisans, expand awareness of their products and encourage greater public engagement with India’s rich handloom and handicraft traditions.

*****

PR-174-TAR/KV/GA/RK

(Release ID: 2325534)

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Text of PM's address at the Vijaya Dashami celebrations in Delhi
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय !

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय !

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय !

विजयदशमी के इस पावन पर्व पर मैं प्रभु श्रीराम, माँ जानकी और बजरंग बली के चरणों में प्रणाम करता हूँ। इस पवित्र वातावरण में, मैं सभी देशवासियों को विजयदशमी की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ देता हूँ।

साथियों,

आज भारत का कोना-कोना राममय है। गाँव-गाँव, शहर-शहर रामलीला के रस में देश डूबा हुआ है। देशभर में रामलीलाओं का मंचन, प्रभु श्रीराम के आदर्शों को जीवंत रखने की परंपरा, अत्याचार और आतंक के अंत का उद्घोष और असत्य पर सत्य सनातन की विजय का विश्वास, हमारे लिए ये केवल त्योहार नहीं है, ये भारत की प्राण ऊर्जा है। इसलिए, आज जब देश का जन-जन अधर्म पर धर्म की विजय का उद्घोष कर रहा है, तो आइये, फिर एक बार मेरे साथ बोलिए -

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय!

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय!

सियावर रामचंद्र की जय!

साथियों,

इस देश ने, इसकी संस्कृति ने और इसके पूर्वजों ने हजारों वर्षों से प्रभु श्रीराम की उपासना की है। ये आस्था केवल इसलिए नहीं है कि, श्रीराम ने राक्षसराज रावण का अंत किया था। ये आस्था इसलिए भी है, क्योंकि प्रभु राम ने हमें ऐसे आदर्श दिये, जो मानवता के इतिहास में अतुलनीय है।

साथियों,

प्रभु श्रीराम ने अपने जीवन में कितनी ही कठिनाइयों का सामना किया, लेकिन उन्होंने सच्चाई और नीति का रास्ता कभी नहीं छोड़ा। उनका चरित्र ही ऐसा है, ‘प्रसन्नतां या न गत अभिषेकतः तथा,न मम्ले वनवास दुःखतः॥’ अर्थात्, प्रभु राम के चेहरे पर न राजपद पाने की प्रसन्नता हुई, और न वन जाने से उन्हें कोई दुख हुआ। उन्होंने हर संकट को सहकर भी धर्म का पालन किया और सत्य की स्थापना की। जब हमारे राम जंगल गए, तो वहाँ उन्होंने निषादराज को गले लगाया, माता शबरी को सम्मान दिया। उन्होंने दया, करुणा, प्रेम और सौहार्द के मानदंड स्थापित किए। और जब वापस आकर प्रभु राम अयोध्या के राजा बने, तो ऐसे रामराज्य की स्थापना की, जो आज भी सुशासन का, गवर्नेंस का मानदंड माना जाता है। रामराज्य अर्थात् ऐसा शासन, जहां किसी के प्रति भेदभाव नहीं हो, जहां सबको न्याय मिले, जहां सबको समान अवसर मिलें, जहाँ सत्ता का उद्देश्य शासन करना नहीं, जन-कल्याण का हो। और इसलिए ही गोस्वामी तुलसीदास जी ने कहा था - ‘दैहिक दैविक भौतिक तापा। राम राज नहिं काहुहि ब्यापा॥’ यही मर्यादा पुरुषोत्तम प्रभु श्रीराम का आदर्श है। इसलिए हमें हमेशा जनता को जनार्दन मानकर, नागरिक देवो भव के मंत्र पर आगे बढ़ना है। हमें गरीब, वंचित की सेवा को सर्वोपरि रखना है।

साथियों,

प्रभु राम के जीवन से हमें बहुत बड़ी सीख मिलती है। संकट कितना भी बड़ा क्यों ना हो, चुनौती कितनी भी कठिन क्यों ना हो, हमें दूसरों के भरोसे नहीं बैठना है, हमें अपना सामर्थ्य पहचानना है, हमें अपने संसाधनों पर विश्वास करना है, अपने संकल्प को शक्ति बनाना है, और अपने परिश्रम से समाधान निकालना है। प्रभु राम ने हमें सिखाया कि रास्ते की कठिनाइयाँ, हमारी यात्रा को रोक नहीं सकतीं। समुद्र सामने था, लंका दूर थी, लेकिन संकल्प अडिग था। इसलिए राम जी ने जनता की सामूहिक शक्ति को जगाया, जनभागीदारी को अपना संबल बनाया, उपलब्ध संसाधनों को जोड़ा। और असंभव लगने वाले लक्ष्य को संभव बनाया। यही सफलता का मूल मंत्र है। अपनी शक्ति पर विश्वास, अपने सामर्थ्य पर भरोसा, अपने संसाधनों का सही उपयोग और अपने लक्ष्य के प्रति अटूट संकल्प। आज हमें भी इसी मंत्र को लेकर आगे बढ़ना है। हमारे सामने विकसित भारत का लक्ष्य है, हमारे सामने आत्मनिर्भर भारत का लक्ष्य है। हमें जनशक्ति से जनकल्याण करते हुए, जनता की हर आकांक्षाओं को पूरा करना है और इसके लिए भी हमें भगवान राम से ही प्रेरणा भी लेनी है।

साथियों,

एक राष्ट्र तभी प्रगति करता है, जब उसके पास आत्मसम्मान का भाव होता है। और इस आत्मसम्मान में बहुत बड़ी भूमिका उसकी विरासत की होती है। इसलिए, आज देश अपनी विरासत और पहचान को भी संरक्षित करने में जुटा है। सदियों तक हमारी धरोहरों को लूटकर विदेश ले जाया गया, लेकिन आज हम अपनी उन धरोहरों को वापिस ला रहे हैं। बीते 12 वर्षों में साढ़े छह सौ से ज्यादा प्राचीन मूर्तियों को भारत वापिस लाया गया है। इसी तरह, भारत अपने सांस्कृतिक केन्द्रों को दुनिया में नई पहचान दिलवा रहा है। बीते वर्षों में, हमारे कितने ही स्थानों को यूनेस्को वर्ल्ड हेरिटेज साइट्स की लिस्ट में शामिल किया गया है। पिछले साल दीपावली को भी यूनेस्को ने मानवता की अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक विरासत की सूची में शामिल किया है। ये करोड़ों भारतीयों की सामूहिक इच्छाशक्ति का ही परिणाम है। हमें इसी निष्ठा से आगे भी काम करना है।

साथियों,

विजयदशमी, विजय का पर्व है, जीत का पर्व है। ये पर्व हमें साहस देता है कि शत्रु कितना भी बड़ा क्यों न हो, लेकिन जब हम सच्चाई और मानवता के साथ होते हैं, तो अंत में जीत हमारी होती है। विजयदशमी की यही भावना हमेशा से भारत की विचारधारा रही है। हमारे ऋषियों ने हमें प्रेरणा दी है - ‘समानो मन्त्रः समितिः समानी समानं मनः सह चित्तमेषाम्।’ अर्थात्, हमारे विचार समान हों, हमारी समितियां,अर्थात् राष्ट्र की सभी संस्थाएं, सभी राजनीतिक दल, राष्ट्रहित के लिए एक साथ खड़े हों। हमें इसी भावना पर चलना होगा, हमें देश के दुश्मनों के साथ मिलकर लड़ना होगा। देश के मान-सम्मान को चोट पहुंचाने वाली ताक़तें, समाज को बांटने वाले लोग, हमारी संस्कृति से नफरत करने वाले की मानसिकता, ये देश के दुश्मन हैं। आज विजयदशमी के शुभ पर्व पर हमें अपना संकल्प फिर दोहराना है, हमें मॉं भारती के शत्रुओं को पहचानना होगा, उन्हें परास्त करना होगा। और राष्ट्र प्रथम का संकल्प लेते हुए, सबको एक साथ आना होगा। मुझे विश्वास है, अयोध्या मंदिर में प्राण प्रतिष्ठा समारोह के दौरान ‘राम से राष्ट्र’ और ‘देव से देश’ की जो संकल्पना हमने की है, उसे हम जरूर पूरा करेंगे। मैं एक बार फिर सभी देशवासियों को दशहरे की बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूँ।

जय सिया राम !

जय सिया राम !

जय सिया राम !

भारत माता की जय।

भारत माता की जय।

बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

*****

 

MJPS/SS/SS/RK

(Release ID: 2325527)

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister congratulates Himanshu Nandal on winning Bronze at the Asian Para Games
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 7:49PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today congratulated Himanshu Nandal for winning the Bronze medal in the Men's 400m Freestyle S11 event at the Asian Para Games 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah participates in Vijayadashami festival in Ludhiana, Punjab, and performs burning of the symbolic Ravana of ‘Chitta’
I have been hearing since childhood that if one wants to see Ravana Dahan, one should go to Ludhiana, where the Ramlila Committee has been organising the programme for 200 years
At three places in Punjab, Home Minister met families who had lost their sons in the fight against drugs
Tears in the eyes of relatives, their questions, and their pain are enough to shake anyone to the core
Punjab government has handed over the probe of one murder to the CBI; it should also hand over the investigation of the remaining two murders to the CBI
Once the investigation is handed over to the CBI, no matter how big a person is involved in these murders, the Modi government will track them down and put them behind bars
On Vijayadashami, we take this resolve that by 31 December 2029 we will free the entire Punjab from the drug trade and make it a drug-free Punjab
If the people of Punjab provide information about the drug trade on the Narcotics Control Bureau’s toll-free helpline, the Modi government will take action on it
The Modi government has a record of fulfilling what it has said
Article 370 and 35A are gone, terrorism is on the verge of being eliminated, and we have ended Naxalism, now we will also eliminate the drug menace
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 7:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today participated in the Vijayadashami festival in Ludhiana, Punjab, and performed the burning of the symbolic Ravana of ‘Chitta’ (Drugs).

In his address, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that in our tradition, the burning of Ravana’s effigy is a symbol of the victory of good over evil. Vijayadashami is the day for every person to eliminate the ego, pride, greed and other evils within themselves. On this very day, thousands of years ago, Lord Shri Ram achieved victory over Ravana, and since then the entire world has been celebrating Lord Shri Ram’s victory as the triumph of good over evil. He said that he has heard since childhood that if you want to see Ravana Dahan, go to Ludhiana, where the Ramlila Committee has been organising the Ravana Dahan programme for 200 years.

Shri Amit Shah said that today he met families at three places in Punjab who had lost their sons in the fight against drugs. He said that the tears in the eyes of those relatives, their questions, and their pain are enough to shake anyone to the core. Shri Shah said that the Punjab government has handed over the investigation of one murder to the CBI. He urged the Punjab government to hand over the investigation of the remaining two murders to the CBI as well. The Home Minister expressed confidence that justice will be done in these cases. Once the investigation is handed over to the CBI, no matter how big a person is involved in these murders, the Modi government will track them down and put them behind bars.

Union Home Minister said that on this Vijayadashami itself, we take this resolve that by 31 December 2029 we will free the entire Punjab from the drug trade and make it a drug-free Punjab. He said that there can be no greater tribute than this to these three brave individuals who lost their lives. Shri Shah said that if the people of Punjab provide information about the drug trade on the Narcotics Control Bureau’s toll-free helpline, the Modi government will take action on it.

Shri Amit Shah said that the Modi government has a record of fulfilling what it has promised. Article 370 and 35A are gone, terrorism is on the verge of being eliminated, and we have ended Naxalism. He said that now we will also eliminate the drug trade.

 

****

RK/RR/PS/PR

item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment 9 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Concludes In Mysuru Karnataka Thousands Visit Mela Showcasing Traditional Handicrafts, Handloom Products of Artisans from 12 States/UTs Mela Featured 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans Hon’ble Minister Ramdas Athawale, Union Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Visits Shilp Samagam Mela Mysuru Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi The Nine Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 successfully concluded with thousands of people visiting Dasara Exhibition Grounds at…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
9 Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Concludes In Mysuru Karnataka
Thousands Visit Mela Showcasing Traditional Handicrafts, Handloom Products of Artisans from 12 States/UTs
Mela Featured 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans
Hon’ble Minister Ramdas Athawale, Union Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Visits Shilp Samagam Mela Mysuru
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Nine Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 successfully concluded with thousands of people visiting Dasara Exhibition Grounds at Mysuru in Karnataka. The Mela was organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

The Mela aimed to provide a marketing platform for traditional handicraft and handloom products made by beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis, including artisans supported by the three National Corporations functioning under the Ministry, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

Deputy General Manager in the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) Shri Rajnish Banker said the initiative sought to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for the target groups.

He said the Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022, and 975 artisans have been benefited through 13 such fairs organised so far.

Shri Banker said the Mysuru edition was the first Shilp Samagam Mela of the financial year 2026–27.

The Official said a total of 83 stalls had been put up at the Mela, out of which 80 were allotted to artisans, including 37 women artisans. Food stalls serving traditional delicacies had also been set up for visitors.

The Mela featured artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, he added.

The DGM informed that the exhibition showcased a wide range of traditional products, including handicraft items, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed products, Kanjivaram sarees, leather goods, wooden toys, bags and purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers.

The platform enables artisans to display their products to a wider audience and connect with prospective customers, while promoting India's diverse cultural heritage and traditional skills.

The official further said that Shilp Samagam Mela also serves as a platform to disseminate information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and its three national corporations—NSFDC, NBCFDC and NSKFDC. The initiative seeks to enhance awareness about available assistance and development opportunities for eligible beneficiaries, while encouraging entrepreneurship and economic empowerment.

The Ministry has also introduced BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) to expand market access for products made by the target groups through various digital platforms in India and abroad. Under this initiative, products are branded as BHARAT TULIP to enhance their visibility and facilitate online sales. The programme aims to strengthen artisans' livelihoods while preserving traditional art forms and promoting India's rich craftsmanship to a wider audience.

The Official said the Ministry facilitates the participation of artisans by providing free stalls and support covering travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods, and meals, including lunch and dinner. This assistance helps artisans participate in the mela and showcase their products without bearing stall rental costs and specified participation-related expenses.

Union Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale during his visit to Shilp Samagam Mela highlighted the Central Government’s commitment to the economic and social empowerment of socially vulnerable sections.

The Minister inspected stalls with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience.

Union Secretary of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant also visited the Mela.  

During his visit to Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds, the Secretary inspected stalls and interacted with the Stall Managers and visitors.

The Union Secretary was on a two days official visit to Mysuru to take comprehensive review of the Ministry’s Schemes, Programmes and Initiatives under implementation, with the State Social Welfare Department.

Shri Pant said through such initiatives, the Ministry continues to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and advance the economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities.

The Shilp Samagam Mela offered visitors an opportunity to explore India’s traditional crafts and handloom products while supporting the livelihoods of artisans.

It is pertinent to mention that during the Financial Year 2026–27, the Ministry is organizing additional SHILP SAMAGAM FAIRS At Guwahati, Dilli Haat in New Delhi, Jodhpur And Lucknow.

The Ministry and its three National Corporations will also participate in major exhibitions, including the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in Faridabad in February 2027.

Through initiatives such as Shilp Samagam Mela and BHARAT TULIP, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote market access, entrepreneurship and livelihood opportunities for artisans from the target groups, while supporting the preservation and wider recognition of India's traditional arts and crafts.

item.title: India’s Nuclear Programme Dedicated to Peaceful Purposes, Says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh; Nuclear Energy to Power AI-Driven Future
item.dc:creator: Department of Atomic Energy

item.content:encoded:
Department of Atomic Energy
India’s Nuclear Programme Dedicated to Peaceful Purposes, Says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh; Nuclear Energy to Power AI-Driven Future
Dr. Homi Bhabha’s vision continues to guide India’s peaceful nuclear journey as the country advances towards energy security and clean power: Dr. Jitendra Singh
“One has to be intelligent enough to use Artificial Intelligence”, Dr. Jitendra Singh stresses responsible, human-led use of AI across sectors
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has opened critical and sensitive sectors to non-government players, creating wider opportunities for private sector participation
India targets 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047 and Net Zero emissions by 2070, with nuclear energy set to meet growing demand for reliable, clean electricity: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh has said that India’s nuclear programme is dedicated to peaceful purposes and not warfare, reaffirming the vision that has guided the country’s nuclear journey since its inception.

In an exclusive conversation on the sidelines of ‘Bloomberg Economy Forum 2026’, the Minister said nuclear energy would play an increasingly important role in meeting India’s future energy requirements, including the growing demand for reliable electricity to support Artificial Intelligence (AI) and data centres.

Recalling the vision of Dr. Homi Bhabha, the architect of India’s nuclear programme, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India had consistently pursued nuclear energy for peaceful applications and national development. The commitment to the peaceful use of nuclear technology, he said, remains central to the country’s approach as it expands its capabilities to meet emerging developmental and technological needs.

The Minister said India’s nuclear energy ambitions must be viewed in the context of its long-term development goals and clean energy commitments. With the country targeting 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047 and Net Zero emissions by 2070, nuclear energy is expected to complement other sources of power by providing a continuous and reliable supply of clean electricity.

Linking nuclear energy with the next phase of technological growth, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the expansion of Artificial Intelligence and data centres would require dependable sources of electricity capable of meeting their substantial and continuous energy needs. Nuclear energy, he said, would supplement India’s other energy programmes and contribute to meeting the power requirements of an increasingly technology-driven economy.

On the expanding role of Artificial Intelligence, the Minister said AI should be viewed as a tool applicable across sectors rather than as a domain in itself. From Space and life sciences to other areas of scientific and technological development, AI is set to become an increasingly necessary instrument. Emphasising the importance of human judgement in its application, he said, “One has to be intelligent enough to use Artificial Intelligence.”

Dr. Jitendra Singh said AI offers significant advantages across domains, but ensuring its optimal use without allowing it to be misused by individuals or other actors remains a key challenge. While regulations are in place, he said integrity at both the individual and national level is fundamental to ensuring that the technology is used responsibly. India, he added, has made appreciable efforts in this direction under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The Minister also referred to the wider opening of critical and sensitive sectors to non-government players under the Modi Government. He said the approach has expanded the scope for private sector participation in areas that were traditionally more restricted, creating opportunities for industry to contribute to technological advancement, innovation and national development.

Dr. Jitendra Singh’s remarks bring together two important dimensions of India’s development trajectory: strengthening nuclear energy as a dependable source of clean power and harnessing emerging technologies such as AI through responsible, human-led application. As India advances towards its 2047 development goals and its 2070 Net Zero commitment, reliable energy infrastructure and wider participation in strategic sectors will remain important to sustaining the country’s technological and economic ambitions.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Defence

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
25th SCO Council of Heads of Government Meeting: Raksha Mantri calls for unified action to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism
“There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, no place for its supporters”
Connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty & territorial integrity of all countries: Shri Rajnath Singh
“SCO’s success lies in creating opportunities for youth, entrepreneurs, farmers & small businesses”
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 1:16PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Member States to make concerted efforts to dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism, describing the menace as one of the gravest threats to peace and development. He was addressing the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (CHG) of SCO in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 20, 2026.

“Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment & commerce. It radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists,” said Raksha Mantri.

Shri Rajnath Singh recalled the deliberations at the SCO Summit in Bishkek in August-September 2026, when Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi underlined the need for concrete steps by the Organisation on issues related to security, connectivity, and opportunity. Raksha Mantri underscored India’s belief that economic engagement should be inclusive and mutually beneficial for all Member States. “India believes that the SCO must remain efficient and steadfast in its adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, consensus, and mutual respect. A greater number of institutions does not necessarily translate into greater achievements. New mechanisms should focus on clearly identified needs, avoid duplication, and prioritise delivering practical value to Member States,” he said.

Raksha Mantri emphasised the need for the SCO to build consensus and translate it into concrete action to address the uncertain global economic environment marked by geopolitical tensions, disruptions to trade and supply chains, concerns over energy and food security, and emerging technological divides. There is a need to strengthen resilient supply chains, facilitate trade and investment, and leverage technology to drive development, he said. Stressing that the benefits of economic cooperation must reach all sections of society, he reaffirmed India’s support for the adoption of an Action Plan for the Multilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation Programme for the period 2026-2030.

Shri Rajnath Singh welcomed the decisions taken at the SCO Summit in Bishkek to establish the Universal Centre in Tashkent and the Anti-Drug Centre in Dushanbe as permanent bodies of the Organisation. Their effectiveness, he said, would depend on efficient coordination and timely execution of tasks.

Underlining the importance of connectivity for shared prosperity, Raksha Mantri stated that India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new avenues for development. He said that initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chabahar Port can contribute significantly to connecting Central Asia with broader markets.

Shri Rajnath Singh stressed that connectivity must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries, adding that projects not founded on these principles will not be sustainable. He emphasised the need to move beyond physical connectivity by simplifying customs procedures, promoting digital documentation, improving logistics and adopting interoperable digital solutions to reduce the cost of doing business across the region.

Raksha Mantri highlighted the symposium on financing infrastructure projects in Central Asia, held in Mumbai earlier this month, and expressed gratitude to Central Asian countries and SCO partners for their active participation. He also acknowledged the organisation of the first-ever SCO Asian Economic Dialogue.

“Our success should be measured by the opportunities we create for youth, new markets we open for our entrepreneurs, technologies we make available to our farmers and small-scale business owners, and the connections we foster among societies,” said Shri Rajnath Singh.

Raksha Mantri asserted that India’s own development experience demonstrates the transformative potential of technology and innovation that drive growth and deliver solutions. He highlighted the country’s Digital Public Infrastructure, which has transformed public service delivery and enhanced financial inclusion. He added that India has built one of the world’s largest start-up ecosystems, and the nation’s emphasis on women-led development is rooted in the belief that women play a defining role in shaping the path of development.

Shri Rajnath Singh underlined that India’s global initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure contribute to affordable clean energy & climate-resilient development. He added that Mission LiFE promotes sustainable lifestyles and responsible consumption, while the Global Biofuel Alliance fosters cleaner and more sustainable energy solutions.

Raksha Mantri urged the SCO to build on the strong foundation established over the past 25 years and chart a forward-looking roadmap focused on consensus-driven cooperation and tangible outcomes. He reaffirmed India’s commitment to working closely with all Member States towards achieving these objectives. He invited Member States to participate in the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum being hosted by India later this year.

The meeting reviewed progress in multilateral economic and trade cooperation among SCO Member States and discussed measures to further strengthen cooperation in areas such as transport, finance, digital economy and social development.

The Heads of Delegation adopted the Joint Communiqué of the 25th Meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government, including the SCO budget for 2027, relevant financial and administrative decisions, and the PMTEC Action Plan for 2026-2030.

The SCO CHG is an important mechanism of the Organisation responsible for promoting economic and other areas of practical cooperation among Member States. India has been a full member of the SCO since 2017 and continues to participate actively in its various mechanisms.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings on RSS Sthapana Divas
PM shares motivating address by Dr. Mohan Bhagwat Ji during the Shatabdi Varsh Shri Vijayadashami Utsav
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 11:49AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today extended his greetings to all Swayamsevaks on the special occasion of RSS Sthapana Divas and shared a motivating address by Sarsanghchalak Dr. Mohan Bhagwat Ji delivered during the Shatabdi Varsh Shri Vijayadashami Utsav in Nagpur.

In a series of posts on X, the Prime Minister shared:

"Today, on the special occasion of RSS Sthapana Divas, my greetings to all Swayamsevaks. I also pay homage to all those greats who have nurtured the RSS over the years.

The RSS has completed a remarkable century of service, nation-building and social harmony. Countless Swayamsevaks have worked for society with a deep sense of duty and a nation-first spirit.

May this spirit keep strengthening national development in the times to come.

राष्ट्रीय स्वयंसेवक संघ के स्थापना दिवस के विशेष अवसर पर सभी स्वयंसेवकों को मेरी हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं! मैं उन सभी विभूतियों को भी नमन करता हूं, जिन्होंने अपने अथक परिश्रम और सेवाभाव से संघ को सींचा और संवारा है।

राष्ट्रीय स्वयंसेवक संघ ने सेवा, राष्ट्र निर्माण और सामाजिक प्रतिबद्धता का गौरवशाली शताब्दी वर्ष पूर्ण किया है। अनगिनत स्वयंसेवकों ने अपने समर्पण, कर्तव्य-निष्ठा और राष्ट्र-प्रथम की भावना से सदैव समाज के उत्थान के लिए कार्य किया है।

मुझे विश्वास है कि यह भावना आने वाले समय में भी देश को और सशक्त एवं सुदृढ़ करेगी।"

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
WWF-India EIACP launches nationwide Green Diwali Campaign from 20th October to 8th November 2026; Urges Citizens to celebrate a Cracker-free Diwali
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 10:48AM by PIB Delhi

WWF-India’s Programme Centre – Resource Partner (PC-RP),  supported by Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, has launched a nationwide Green Diwali Campaign from 20.10.2026 to 08.11.2026, urging citizens to avoid firecrackers and celebrate a clean and green Diwali in line with Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment). The campaign will reach schools, colleges, educational institutions, resident welfare associations and local communities, with a special focus on the 130 cities covered under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP).

As part of the campaign, citizens are encouraged to take the Green Diwali Pledge to avoid firecrackers, encourage family and neighbours to do the same, use diyas and energy-efficient lights, avoid single-use plastic, segregate waste and choose local products. Educational institutions and community groups are encouraged to organise pledge drives during assemblies, classes, rallies and community meetings.

Citizens are also encouraged to take WWF-India’s Carbon Footprint Survey to understand how their daily activities and consumption contribute to their environmental footprint and identify more sustainable habits. The survey is available at: https://wwfindiawebgis.in/Carbon_Footprint/Carbon_Footprint.html. Schools, colleges, EIACP centres, community groups and individuals participating in the campaign are requested to share details of their activities through the online form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/15hDbjbqZzeo68kNjAxeHQA_SMIQ7lUlPdvCIi-gvwdY/viewform.

Submissions should include the institution or organisation’s name and location, activity details and date, the number of participants who took the pledge, geo-tagged photographs and a brief report. Selected entries may be featured on EIACP websites and social media platforms.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister greets everyone on the occasion of Vijayadashami
Posted On: 20 OCT 2026 8:39AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today extended his heartiest greetings to everyone on the occasion of Vijayadashami.

The Prime Minister expressed hope that this auspicious festival of joy and faith infuses new strength into everyone’s resolves. Shri Modi wished for a life enriched with happiness, good fortune, and success for all.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared:

"आप सभी को विजयादशमी की अनंत शुभकामनाएं। उल्लास और विश्वास का यह विजय पर्व हर किसी के संकल्प को नई शक्ति प्रदान करे। सभी का जीवन सुख-सौभाग्य और सफलता से समृद्ध हो, यही कामना है।"

item.content:encoded:
UPSC
COMBINED DEFENCE SERVICES EXAMINATION (II), 2026  DECLARATION OF WRITTEN RESULT THEREOF
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 9:02PM by PIB Delhi

On the basis of the result of the COMBINED DEFENCE SERVICES EXAMINATION (II), 2026 conducted by the Union Public Service Commission on 13th September, 2026, 8956 candidates with the following Roll Numbers have qualified for being interviewed by the Service Selection Board of the Ministry of Defence, for admission to (i) Indian Military Academy, Dehradun 163rd (DE) Course commencing in July, 2027 (ii) Indian Naval Academy, Ezhimala, Kerala, Course commencing in July, 2027 (iii) Air Force Academy, Hyderabad (Pre-Flying) Training Course [222 F(P)] commencing in July, 2027 (iv) Officers Training Academy, Chennai (Madras) 126th SSC (Men) (NT) (UPSC) Course commencing in October, 2027 and (v) Officers Training Academy, Chennai (Madras), 126th SSC Women (NT) (UPSC) Course commencing in October, 2027.

2. There are some common candidates in the four lists for various courses except for OTA (Women).

3. The candidature of all the candidates, whose Roll Numbers are shown in the lists below, is provisional. In accordance with the conditions of the admission to the examination, they are required to submit the original certificates in support of age (Date of Birth), educational qualifications, NCC (C) (Army Wing/Senior Division Air Wing/Naval Wing) etc. claimed by them to IHQ of MoD (Army) / Dte Gen of Rtg (Rtg A) CDSE Entry Section for SSC male candidates and SSC women entry Section for female candidates, West Block III, R.K. Puram, New Delhi-110066 in case of IMA/SSC first choice candidates, and IHQ of MOD (Navy) “DMPR” (OI & R Section), Room No. 204,‘C’ Wing, Sena Bhawan, New Delhi-110011 in case of Navy first choice candidates, and Dte of Personnel (Offrs), Kasturba Gandhi Marg, New Delhi-110001 in case of Air Force first choice candidates by the following dates failing which their candidature will stand cancelled. The original Certificates are to be submitted not later than 01st July, 2027 for IMA & INA, not later than 13th May, 2027 for AFA and not later than 1st October, 2027 in case of SSC course only. The candidates must not send any original Certificates to the Union Public Service Commission.

4. The candidates who have qualified in the written examination and given their first choice as Army (IMA/OTA) are required to register themselves on the recruiting directorate website viz. www.joinindianarmy.nic.in, enabling them to receive call up information for SSB interview. Those candidates who have already registered on the recruiting directorate website are advised not to register again.

5. In case, there is any change of address, the candidates are advised to promptly intimate directly to the Army Headquarters/Naval Headquarters/Air Headquarters as the case may be.

6. The Union Public Service Commission has a Facilitation Counter near Examination Hall Building in its Campus. Candidates may obtain any information/clarification regarding this examination on working days between 10.00 AM to 5.00 PM in person. Alternatively, candidates can also contact the Candidate’s Help Desk over telephone numbers 011-24041001 and 011-40303444 between 9:00 AM to 8:00 PM all days. In addition, for SSB interview related matters, the candidates may contact over telephone no. 011-26175473 or visit Joinindianarmy.nic.in for Army as first choice, 011-23010097 / Email: officer-navy[at]nic[dot]in or Joinindiannavy.gov.in for Navy/Naval Academy as first choice and 011-23010231 (Extn. 7645 / 7646 / 7610) or visit www.careerindianairforce.cdac.in for Air Force as first choice. Candidates can also obtain information regarding their result by accessing the Commission’s website http://www.upsc.gov.in.

7. The marks-sheet of the candidates will be available on the Commission’s website (www.upsconline.nic.in) within 15 days from the date of publication of the final result of OTA course

(after conducting SSB Interview) and will remain available on the website for a period of 30 days.

item.title: DRI foils major ganja trafficking attempt; seizes 591 kg cannabis smuggled from Nepal
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance DRI foils major ganja trafficking attempt; seizes 591 kg cannabis smuggled from Nepal Intelligence-led operation uncovers 81 packets of ganja concealed in ingenious compartments in a truck suspected to be carrying contraband from Nepal Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi In a significant crackdown on cross-border narcotics trafficking, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized 591.3 kg ganja (cannabis) , in an intelligence-led operation conducted during 17–18 October 2026 in Uttar Pradesh. The operation exposed an elaborate…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI foils major ganja trafficking attempt; seizes 591 kg cannabis smuggled from Nepal
Intelligence-led operation uncovers 81 packets of ganja concealed in ingenious compartments in a truck suspected to be carrying contraband from Nepal
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant crackdown on cross-border narcotics trafficking, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized 591.3 kg ganja (cannabis), in an intelligence-led operation conducted during 17–18 October 2026 in Uttar Pradesh. The operation exposed an elaborate concealment method involving specially fabricated cavities in a truck suspected to be transporting the contraband from Nepal.

Acting on specific intelligence that a truck carrying ganja from Nepal would enter Uttar Pradesh through Sonauli, DRI officers at Gorakhpur launched a coordinated surveillance operation with teams at Lucknow, Patna and Varanasi. After more than four hours of sustained surveillance, the suspect vehicle was identified and intercepted on the road between Gorakhpur and Kushinagar.

A meticulous search of the vehicle revealed two specially engineered concealed cavities — one above the hood and another behind the driver’s seat. These compartments contained 81 packets of ganja weighing a total of 591.3 kg. 

The entire consignment, along with the truck used to transport it, was seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

 

This major seizure demonstrates DRI’s resolve to disrupt narcotics supply chains through intelligence-led enforcement and the detection of sophisticated concealment techniques employed by traffickers. The operation also underscores the importance of sustained vigilance against suspected cross-border drug trafficking routes.

 

****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes more than 43 lakh foreign-origin smuggled cigarettes worth Rs. 8.64 crore in Mizoram; one arrested
Intelligence-led interception on Champhai–Aizawl Road again exposes suspected cigarette smuggling from Myanmar
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 8:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has dealt a significant blow to cross-border cigarette smuggling in the North-Eastern region, seizing 43.2 lakh sticks of foreign-origin cigarettes valued at Rs. 8.64 crore in an intelligence-led operation in Mizoram, today. The consignment suspected to have been smuggled from Myanmar, was intercepted while being transported towards Aizawl.

Acting on specific intelligence that a truck was transporting a substantial quantity of foreign-origin cigarettes towards Aizawl, officers of DRI Aizawl Regional Unit mounted surveillance along the Champhai–Aizawl Road. The vehicle was intercepted at Tuirial village. A thorough examination of the truck led to the recovery of 432 cases containing 43,20,000 sticks of “Patron” brand foreign-origin cigarettes.

Examination revealed that the cigarette packets did not carry the mandatory pictorial and health warnings prescribed under the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003. The cigarettes, along with the truck, were seized under Section 110 of the Customs Act, 1962. The driver of the truck was arrested.

Preliminary investigation indicates that the cigarettes had been smuggled into Mizoram from Myanmar through the Zokhawthar sector of the Mizoram–Myanmar border, highlighting the use of cross-border routes for the illicit movement of foreign-origin tobacco products.

This significant seizure underscores DRI’s continued efforts to dismantle cross-border smuggling networks, curb the illegal movement of foreign-origin goods and strengthen enforcement along vulnerable international border routes.

****

KT/KMN

item.title: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Reviews Functioning of Divisions, Bureaus and Institutions under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Reviews Functioning of Divisions, Bureaus and Institutions under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Directs Officials To Adopt A 360-Degree Approach To Ensure Effective Implementation Of Welfare Schemes And Saturation Of Eligible Beneficiaries Emphasises Centre–State/UT Coordination, Whole-Of-Government And Whole-Of-Society Approach, And Wider Dissemination Of Scheme Benefits And Success Stories Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Reviews Functioning of Divisions, Bureaus and Institutions under Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Directs Officials To Adopt A 360-Degree Approach To Ensure Effective Implementation Of Welfare Schemes And Saturation Of Eligible Beneficiaries
Emphasises Centre–State/UT Coordination, Whole-Of-Government And Whole-Of-Society Approach, And Wider Dissemination Of Scheme Benefits And Success Stories
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar chaired a high-level meeting to undertake a comprehensive review of the functioning of various Divisions, Bureaus, Corporations and institutions under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, in the National Capital here this evening. 

The meeting focused on strengthening the implementation of key Central Government schemes, enhancing inter-departmental coordination and ensuring that the benefits of welfare programmes reach all eligible beneficiaries, particularly those at the last mile.

The meeting was attended by senior officials from the Minister’s Office, Joint Secretaries and other senior officers representing the various Divisions and Bureaus of the Ministry.

The review reaffirmed the Ministry’s focus on coordinated implementation, effective public outreach and strengthened delivery mechanisms to ensure that the benefits of its social justice and empowerment programmes reach eligible beneficiaries across the country.

Addressing the officers, Dr. Kumar emphasised the need to adopt a comprehensive 360-degree approach towards the planning, implementation, monitoring and communication of the Ministry’s schemes and programmes. He called upon officials to ensure that every initiative is designed and implemented with a clear focus on the needs of prospective beneficiaries, effective service delivery and measurable outcomes on the ground.

Recalling the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas”, the Minister underscored the importance of a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to social empowerment.

 

He advised officers to strengthen coordination with the Social Welfare Departments of States and Union Territories, as well as other relevant stakeholders, to facilitate smooth, seamless and effective implementation of welfare schemes.

Dr. Kumar directed senior officers to work diligently, carefully and proactively in formulating and implementing schemes, programmes, initiatives and action plans that respond to the needs of all stakeholders. He stressed that effective coordination, regular monitoring and timely corrective measures are essential to overcome implementation gaps and ensure that the intended benefits of government interventions reach eligible individuals and communities across the country.

The Minister also emphasised the need for greater public awareness of the Ministry’s schemes and programmes through systematic dissemination of information on their objectives, eligibility criteria, benefits and application procedures. He called upon officers to ensure that prospective beneficiaries receive clear, accessible and timely information so that eligible individuals can avail themselves of the benefits for which they qualify.

Emphasis on Publicity, Outreach and Beneficiary Awareness

Dr. Kumar directed officials to give greater visibility to the progress, achievements and impact of the Ministry’s flagship schemes and initiatives through print, electronic, digital and social media platforms. He stressed that effective communication must complement implementation efforts, enabling information about government support to reach the intended beneficiary groups across the country.

 

The Minister specifically reviewed the need to publicise the progress and achievements under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) and the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA); Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY); National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE); Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY); and the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) and Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).

He further underscored the importance of disseminating information on measures for strengthening the machinery for the enforcement of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. He also called for wider outreach regarding the SMILE initiative, including its components relating to the comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in the act of begging and the welfare of transgender persons, as well as schemes for the construction of hostels for OBC boys and girls.

The Minister observed that the systematic dissemination of scheme-related information, implementation progress and success stories would help improve awareness, encourage eligible beneficiaries to access available support and strengthen public understanding of the Ministry’s welfare interventions. He emphasised that communication efforts should be closely aligned with implementation priorities and directed towards reaching the intended beneficiary sections, including those who may not have adequate access to information about government schemes.

Focus on Transparency, Effective Implementation and Last-Mile Delivery

Reiterating the importance of transparency, accountability and efficiency, Dr. Kumar called upon all officers and officials to ensure that the Ministry’s schemes and initiatives are implemented effectively and that all eligible prospective beneficiaries are identified and covered in accordance with the applicable scheme guidelines.

He encouraged officers to share constructive suggestions, innovative ideas and practical feedback for improving the Ministry’s functioning, strengthening institutional coordination and enhancing the overall effectiveness of its programmes. The Minister appreciated the ideas and feedback received from officers and emphasized the importance of a responsive and collaborative administrative approach in achieving the Ministry’s objectives.

Earlier, the Minister also inspected various sections of the Ministry and interacted with officers and officials. He appreciated their dedication and hard work and sought their continued commitment towards improving the delivery of welfare services and the effective implementation of the Ministry’s programmes and initiatives.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Power
India and Saudi Arabia Discuss the bilateral Electrical Interconnection Initiative
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power, held a virtual bilateral meeting with H.E. Eng. Nasser Al-Qahtani, Assistant Minister of Energy for Electricity Affairs, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to review the progress of the India–Saudi Arabia Electrical Interconnection initiative and explore avenues for strengthening cooperation in the power sector.

The discussions focused on the progress of the proposed electrical interconnection between India and Saudi Arabia, which holds significant potential to deepen bilateral energy cooperation. Both sides exchanged views on the way forward and underscored the importance of sustained engagement to advance the initiative.

The two sides also explored opportunities to broaden cooperation in other areas of mutual interest in the power sector, with an emphasis on technical collaboration, knowledge sharing and the exchange of best practices.

The Saudi Arabian side expressed interest in enhanced cooperation in the areas of Extra High Voltage (EHV) transmission systems, addressing technical and operational challenges associated with higher penetration of renewable energy in the grid, strategies for accommodating the growing power requirements of emerging data centres, and updating grid codes to address evolving power system requirements.

Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining constructive dialogue to further deepen the India–Saudi Arabia partnership in the power sector.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
5TH EDITION OF INDIA-AUSTRALIA JOINT MILITARY EXERCISE AUSTRAHIND COMMENCES AT THIRUVANANTHAPURAM
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi

The 5th edition of the India-Australia Joint Military Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026 commenced today at the Foreign Training Node, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

The exercise, being conducted from 19 October to 01 November 2026, will witness participation of approximately 120 personnel each from the Indian Army and Australian Army. The fourth edition was held at Irwin Barracks, Perth, Australia, from 13 to 26 October 2025.

The Indian Army contingent comprises troops from the Garhwal Rifles, along with personnel from other arms and services, while the Australian Army contingent comprises troops from 13 Brigade.

The exercise will be conducted on the theme “Joint Sub-Conventional Operations in Island and Coastal Environment under Chapter VII of the UN Mandate”. It is aimed at enhancing interoperability, jointmanship and operational coordination between the two armies while developing a common understanding of tactics, techniques and procedures for operations in island and coastal terrain.

During the exercise, troops of both armies will undertake joint planning, tactical drills and combat-oriented training in realistic operational conditions, including aerial and maritime dimension. The training will focus on coordinated operations in coastal and island environments, surveillance and reconnaissance, protection of vital installations and response to Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief contingencies, besides exchange of professional experience and best practices. As a first, an observer delegation from New Zealand will also be participating in the exercise.

Exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026 will further strengthen military-to-military cooperation, interoperability and mutual trust between India and Australia. It will reinforce their shared commitment towards peace, stability and security in the Indo-Pacific region.

Organised by the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-NIScPR Successfully Concludes Two-Week Skill Training Programme on Library Automation, Digitisation and Artificial Intelligence for Libraries
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

The CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (CSIR-NIScPR) successfully organised a two-week skill training programme on “Skill Training in Library Automation, Digitization and Artificial Intelligence for Libraries” during 5–16 October 2026 under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III). Organised by the Institute’s Training Division, the programme aimed to strengthen the technical competencies of library and information science professionals, academicians, researchers, students and IT professionals in library automation, digitisation, digital repository management and the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in library services. A total of 16 participants from universities, research institutions, libraries, and other organizations across the country attended the programme.

Dr. Geeta Vani Rasayam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, inaugurated the programme and encouraged participants to actively engage in the training. Shri Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division, CSIR-NIScPR, introduced the objectives of the programme and highlighted the importance of skill development in library automation, digitisation and the adoption of emerging technologies. Shri Salim Ansari moderated the inaugural session.

Designed with an emphasis on experiential learning, the programme combined expert lectures, demonstrations and hands-on sessions on Koha Integrated Library Management System (ILMS) and DSpace digital repository software.

The Koha sessions covered open-source software fundamentals, installation of the Linux operating system and Koha, catalogue management, patron management, circulation workflows, report generation, system customisation, and backup and restoration. Participants gained practical experience in configuring and managing library automation functions and workflows.

The DSpace sessions focused on installation and administration, management of communities and collections, item submission, e-people registration and authorisation, Dublin Core and Bitstream Registry management, basic customisation, and backup and restoration. These sessions provided practical exposure to digital repository management for the organisation, preservation and dissemination of scholarly and institutional knowledge.

The programme also covered emerging applications of Artificial Intelligence in libraries, including AI tools and metadata extraction using AI. A special session on iThenticate was conducted on 15 October 2026 to familiarise participants with text similarity checking and its relevance to responsible academic and scholarly writing.

As part of the programme, participants visited the National Science Library to gain insights into its resources and services. The academic sessions were conducted by Shri Mukesh Pund, Shri Sanjay Burde, Dr. Avinash Kshitij, Shri Salim Ansari and Shri Bharath Natarajan. The practical exercises enabled participants to apply the concepts covered during the training.

The valedictory session acknowledged the participants’ engagement and encouraged them to apply the knowledge and practical skills acquired during the training in their respective institutions. The programme was coordinated by Ms. Meetali Bharti, Programme Coordinator and Nodal Principal Investigator (PI), with Mr. Salim Ansari, Co-PI and Course Co-Coordinator, and Mr. Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division and Course Coordinator.

Through the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III), CSIR-NIScPR continues to strengthen professional capacity in library and information science and promote the adoption of open-source technologies and Artificial Intelligence in library services, contributing to the modernisation of libraries and digital knowledge management across academic and research institutions.

item.title: India–New Zealand FTA to Come into Force on 20th October 2026 on Vijay Dashmi, Opening New Opportunities for Indian Exporters
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry India–New Zealand FTA to Come into Force on 20th October 2026 on Vijay Dashmi, Opening New Opportunities for Indian Exporters 100% Duty-Free Access to New Zealand Market to Create Opportunities for Indian MSMEs, Artisans, Farmers and Women Entrepreneurs: lUnion Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal India Flags Off First-Ever JCB Machine Export to New Zealand New Zealand Commits to Facilitate USD 20 Billion Investment into India under India–New Zealand FTA Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Commerce…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India–New Zealand FTA to Come into Force on 20th October 2026 on Vijay Dashmi, Opening New Opportunities for Indian Exporters
100% Duty-Free Access to New Zealand Market to Create Opportunities for Indian MSMEs, Artisans, Farmers and Women Entrepreneurs: lUnion Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
India Flags Off First-Ever JCB Machine Export to New Zealand
New Zealand Commits to Facilitate USD 20 Billion Investment into India under India–New Zealand FTA
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and New Zealand’s Minister for Trade and Investment, Hon. Todd McClay, today jointly announced through a virtual conference that the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) will enter into force on 20 October 2026, on the occasion of Vijay Dashmi, a day symbolising victory and new beginnings..

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal said, “Ours is a winning partnership, both on and off the field. The success of this agreement will be measured by the opportunities it creates and the difference it makes to the lives of the people of New Zealand and India. For India, 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market opens significant new opportunities for our exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers, and women entrepreneurs. For our farmers, the agreement combines new opportunities with appropriate safeguards. The Agricultural Productivity Partnership, with action plans for apples, kiwifruit and honey, establishment of Centres of Excellence, promote better orchard management, reduce post-harvest losses, and improve agricultural productivity, supporting stronger farm incomes across the country. The agreement also aligns with the vision of our Hon’ble Prime Minister for Viksit Bharat 2047: that is a developed and prosperous India built on competitiveness, innovation, productive capacity, and inclusive prosperity when India celebrates 100 years of independence.”

New Zealand’s Minister for Trade and Investment, Hon. Todd McClay, stated, “The entry into force of India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement is a watershed moment in the relationship between our two countries. For New Zealand exporters, the FTA opens the door to 1.4 billion consumers and one of the world’s fastest-growing major economies. New Zealand’s current exports to India will benefit from tariff elimination or substantial tariff reductions. At the same time, all Indian goods will be able to enter New Zealand duty-free, creating new opportunities for Indian exporters and placing them on a level playing field with New Zealand’s other FTA partners. The success of this agreement will ultimately be measured by the opportunities it creates and the extent to which our businesses use it.”

Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, said, “FTAs are about creating a deep economic partnership between countries. As a part of the FTA, we see this partnership also driving a lot of New Zealand investment in India. All the other big economies around the Pacific have got a much deeper trade with New Zealand. This FTA opens up the opportunity that we can also be a major contributor to the bilateral trade between India and New Zealand. The job is now to translate this opportunity into actual benefits for our people. We are working with all the Industry and the associations to take this message forward to every district across the country.”

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India and New Zealand have continued to deepen and expand their engagement. The FTA reflects India’s commitment to forging partnerships with developed economies that deliver market access, create employment opportunities and empower youth, women and MSMEs, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047

Representatives from industries in India and New Zealand also participated in the ceremony and spoke about opportunities created by the Agreement for their respective sectors, including services, footwear, engineering and agriculture.

On the occasion, the first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off by the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry. Flag-offs of a range of products across the agriculture, gems and jewellery, engineering, sporting goods, footwear and leather sectors are also planned for the entry-into-force day. These initiatives reflect the confidence of Indian manufacturers and the opportunities the Agreement opens up for exporters across the country.

New Zealand has eliminated customs duties on all tariff lines covering Indian exports, removing peak tariffs of up to 10%. Textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods, automobiles and auto components, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, agricultural products and processed foods are expected to benefit. Duty-free access for wooden logs, coking coal and metal waste and scrap will further strengthen manufacturing and MSME supply chains. The pharmaceutical and medical device industries will benefit from streamlined regulatory processes.

New Zealand has made its best services offer in any of its trade agreements to date, with market access in around 118 sectors and Most-Favoured-Nation commitments in about 139 sub-sectors. For the first time, it has also provided dedicated access in Health and Traditional Medicine Services, covering Ayurveda, Yoga and other AYUSH systems.

Indian youth and professionals will have access to a quota of 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas and 1,000 Working Holiday visas every year. There will be no numerical cap on Indian students, with post-study work rights of up to three years for STEM Bachelor’s and Master’s graduates and up to four years for doctoral scholars.

The Agricultural Productivity Partnership is a key component of the Agreement, extending cooperation beyond tariff concessions to bring global technology, training and best practices to Indian farmers. It includes dedicated Action Plans for kiwifruit, apples and honey, with cooperation also extending to horticulture, forestry, livestock and fisheries.

New Zealand is providing technical assistance for establishing Centres of Excellence for kiwifruit, apples and honey. Under the Kiwifruit Action Plan, Phase I sites have been identified at Pfutsero in Nagaland and Magra in Uttarakhand. Two further Centres of Excellence for apples are proposed in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, while the Honey Action Plan envisages Centres of Excellence in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal. These initiatives aim to support farmers through technology transfer, improved cultivation practices and enhanced productivity.

Representatives from Himachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh, along with collaborating organisations from New Zealand, were present for the entry into force.

All Tariff Rate Quotas for apples, kiwifruit and Mānuka honey are formally linked to the delivery of the Action Plans, under the oversight of a Joint Agriculture Productivity Council. This links market access with farmer welfare.

New Zealand has committed to facilitate USD 20 billion of investment into India. The investment is expected to benefit agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and start-ups, and support innovation, entrepreneurship and employment generation under the Make in India vision.

To protect farmers, dairy producers, fisherfolk and rural communities, sensitive products such as dairy, sugar, edible oils and key agricultural commodities remain excluded from concessions. Robust Rules of Origin, a bilateral safeguard mechanism and strong anti-circumvention provisions will ensure that the benefits flow only to genuine Indian exporters.

The Agreement opens an advanced overseas market to India’s MSMEs, women-led enterprises, start-ups, artisans and first-generation entrepreneurs. Zero duty and faster customs processes will lower landed costs and widen their customer base. Structured cooperation will provide enhanced access to trade-related information and linkages with New Zealand’s SME ecosystem, with a specific focus on enterprises owned by women and youth.

New Zealand has also committed to facilitate the registration of Indian Geographical Indications, opening avenues for protection of products associated with rural artisans and traditional industries.

The India–New Zealand FTA is a people-centric and inclusive partnership, anchored in the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 and the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. It seeks to empower farmers, MSMEs, women-led enterprises, entrepreneurs, artisans, youth and professionals.

Negotiations were launched on 16 March 2025 and concluded on 22 December 2025, within nine months. The Agreement was signed on 27 April 2026. It supports the India–New Zealand Strategic Partnership: Roadmap to 2030, which sets an aspirational goal of doubling bilateral trade in goods and services to NZ$7 billion (₹35,000 crore) by 2030.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Saturation Campaign of Financial Inclusion (FI) Schemes to Run from 21st October 2026 to 31st December 2026
Campaign to Cover 2.70 Lakh Gram Panchayats (GP) and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)
Under the Campaign, Banks will Conduct Camps for Various Activities including Enrolments under PMJJBY, PMSBY and APY, Opening of PMJDY Accounts, Re-KYC, Awareness Sessions on Digital Frauds, among others
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi

A nationwide campaign will be organized by Department of Financial Services (DFS) for the saturation of Financial Inclusion (FI) schemes and other key interventions at the Gram Panchayat (GP) & Urban Local Body (ULB) level. The campaign will run from 21.10.2026 to 31.12.2026 covering 2.70 lakh GPs and ULBs in the country. During this period, banks will conduct camps for the following activities:

  1. Enrolments under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) and Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
  2. Aadhaar Seeding in PMJJBY & PMSBY
  3. Opening of PMJDY Accounts
  4. Re - KYC for existing PMJDY & other saving accounts
  5. Generating C-KYC id, wherever pending
  6. Updating nominations in saving accounts and other facilities like lockers, wherever pending
  7. Awareness sessions on FI schemes, digital frauds and ‘Aapki Poonji, Aapka Adhikar’ regarding unclaimed financial assets
  8. Sourcing of KCC applications to support the objective of saturation of eligible PM-Kisan beneficiaries
  9. Enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna to support the objective of saturation of KCC accounts, for the upcoming Rabi season

 

The campaign reflects Government’s commitment to empowering citizens at the last mile, and build a more inclusive society by bringing them into the formal financial system. A preparatory meeting with senior management of Banks and SLBC was held today under chairmanship of JS(FI), DFS. The progress under the campaign will be closely monitored by key stakeholders including State administration, Banks and DFS.

President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON THE EVE OF VIJAYADASHAMI
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu sends her greetings to fellow citizens on the eve of Vijayadashami.

In a message, the President has said, “On the auspicious occasion of Vijayadashami, I extend my heartfelt greetings to all Indians living in the country and abroad.

The festival of Vijayadashami has a special significance. It symbolises the victory of Bhagwan Shri Ram over Ravana. Bhagwan Shri Ram is revered as the embodiment of righteousness and moral conduct. This festival celebrates the triumph of Dharma and justice over Adharma and injustice.

Indian culture is rooted in the ideals of morality and duty. On this occasion, let us resolve to uphold the noble ideals of our cultural traditions and contribute towards building an inclusive society and a Viksit Bharat.

On this sacred occasion, I extend my heartfelt wishes for the happiness, good health and well-being of all citizens”.

item.category: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

item.description: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Bureau of Indian Standards Organises Nationwide Interactive Sessions to Promote AYUSH with Quality Standards Over 600 experts, practitioners and industry leaders participate to advance standardization, safety, patient care, and international acceptance in the fields of AYURVEDA, YOGA, and SOWA-RIGPA Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi In a major push towards standardisation in India’s traditional systems of medicine, the AYUSH Department of the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) conducted two national events…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
Bureau of Indian Standards Organises Nationwide Interactive Sessions to Promote AYUSH with Quality Standards
Over 600 experts, practitioners and industry leaders participate
to advance standardization, safety, patient care, and international acceptance in the fields of AYURVEDA, YOGA, and SOWA-RIGPA
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

In a major push towards standardisation in India’s traditional systems of medicine, the AYUSH Department of the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) conducted two national events on standardization in Ayurveda, Yoga, and Sowa-Rigpa. By bridging traditional heritage with scientific quality control, BIS aims to boost consumer trust, and drive international recognition for the AYUSH sector. The nationwide campaign brought together over 600 key stakeholders including top researchers, industry pioneers, academic leaders, and practitioner:

PRAGATI 2026: National Seminar on Standardization in Ayurveda and Yoga

Hosted in Belagavi, Karnataka by BIS in association with KLE Shri BMK Ayurveda Mahavidyalaya and the KLE Academy of Higher Education & Research, PRAGATI 2026 brought together 600 participants to deliberate the role of Indian Standards in strengthening the Ayurveda and Yoga sectors. Ms. Shrishti Dixit, Scientist-E & Head (AYUSH), BIS, highlighted BIS’s work in formulating Indian Standards and expanding India's role in global standardization via ISO. During the seminar, the dignitaries emphasized that well-defined standards are vital for quality assurance, patient safety, credible research, and effective regulation. Key themes addressed during the seminar included:

  • Standardized Practice & Education: Highlighting the need for uniform terminology, educational benchmarks, and clinical guidelines in Yoga and Ayurveda.
  • Industry & Start-up Support: Guidance from industry leaders including Dr. Bindu Indira (Himalaya Wellness Company) and Dr. Srinivas Patil (Karnataka AYUSH Drugs Manufacturers Association) on how adopting BIS certification accelerates market access and builds consumer trust.
  • Interactive Open House: Expert panel discussions led by Prof. (Dr.) Kashinath Samagandi (All India Institute of Ayurveda) and Vaidya Jayant Deopujari (Chairperson, Ayurveda Sectional Committee, BIS) interacyed with the delgates on on practical issues in adopting standards across education, research, manufacturing and clinical practice, and discussed the gaps that need to be addressed for wider implementation.

 

ADVANCING SOWA-RIGPA STANDARDIZATION IN LEH, LADAKH

BIS convened a Brainstorming Session alongside its 5th Sowa-Rigpa Sectional Committee meeting at the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR) in Leh (UT of Ladakh). Delegates included Padma Shree Dr. Padma Gurmet (Chairperson of the BIS Sowa-Rigpa Sectional Committee and Founding Director of NISR), Dr. Arjun Singh (Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences), and Dr. Usama Akram (Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine) and Dr Mahe Alam from BIS. Deliberations focussed on -

  • Raw Material Quality & Safety: Establishing rigorous testing parameters for single herbs, raw materials, and finished formulations along with drug quality, safety and efficacy, laboratory and analytical requirements, pharmacopoeial standards and quality assurance.
  • IPR & Traditional Knowledge: Safeguarding indigenous knowledge through patents, trademarks, and geographical indications for quality assessment

 

The initiatives were supported by premier national institutions, including the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), and Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS). BIS reaffirmed its commitment to continuously engage with industry and academia, facilitating simple online submission portals for new standardization proposals.

Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is the National Standard Body of India, responsible for the harmonious development of the activities of standardization, and conformity assessment. Through its dedicated Ayush Department, BIS is shaping quality standards that enable traditional Indian systems of medicine to achieve global excellence.

***

RT/BIS
