item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
A Success Story under NAMASTE
From Sanitation Workers to Mechanised Service Entrepreneurs
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

Access to financial assistance and modern equipment creates new opportunities for sanitation workers to improve their livelihoods and achieve financial independence.

The journey of T. Ravi Kumar, P. Sekhar, T. Nikhil and E. Ailaiah from Nellore, Andhra Pradesh, demonstrates how collective entrepreneurship and mechanisation can help sanitation workers build sustainable livelihoods while promoting safer and more efficient sanitation services.

The four beneficiaries were engaged in sanitation work and aspired to improve their income and working conditions by adopting mechanised sanitation services. However, the high cost of modern equipment, coupled with limited access to finance, made it difficult for them to purchase machinery individually. Despite their experience in the sanitation sector, financial constraints restricted their ability to expand their livelihood opportunities and achieve greater economic stability for their families.

A significant change began when the beneficiaries attended an awareness camp organised by the Nellore Municipal Corporation, where they learned about the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) under the NAMASTE Scheme. The scheme opened up an opportunity for them to pursue their shared goal of establishing a mechanised sanitation service through a group project. With financial assistance in the form of a bank loan and upfront capital subsidy, they procured a Mini Jetting Machine to undertake mechanised sewer and septic tank cleaning services.

The total project cost was Rs 35.85 lakh, of which Rs 21.89 lakh was financed through a bank loan and Rs 13.96 lakh was provided as capital subsidy. This support enabled the beneficiaries to overcome the initial financial barrier and acquire modern sanitation equipment that would otherwise have remained beyond their individual means.

 

Following the procurement of the machine, the Nellore Municipal Corporation engaged the group’s equipment on a long-term basis, with monthly hiring charges of approximately Rs 78,500. This arrangement provided a regular source of revenue and created a more sustainable livelihood opportunity for all four beneficiaries. After meeting operational expenses, each group member now earns approximately Rs 37,000 per month, significantly strengthening their financial position and ability to meet household needs.

The intervention has enabled the beneficiaries to move beyond the limitations of traditional sanitation work and become owner-operators of mechanised sanitation equipment. Their improved earnings have contributed to greater financial stability, while access to mechanisation supports safer and more efficient sanitation operations. The opportunity to work collectively has also demonstrated the value of group entrepreneurship in overcoming financial barriers and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities.

Supported during 2021–22, the group’s journey reflects the transformative potential of the Swachhta Udyami Yojana under NAMASTE. By facilitating access to capital, modern equipment and assured work opportunities, the initiative has helped T. Ravi Kumar, P. Sekhar, T. Nikhil and E. Ailaiah strengthen their livelihoods, enhance their occupational dignity and work towards a more secure future for their families. Their success illustrates how targeted financial assistance and mechanisation can empower sanitation workers to become entrepreneurs while contributing to improved sanitation services.

*******

item.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will pay homage to the martyrs on Police Commemoration Day at National Police Memorial in New Delhi on Wednesday, 21st October 2026
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Home Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Home Affairs Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will pay homage to the martyrs on Police Commemoration Day at National Police Memorial in New Delhi on Wednesday, 21st October 2026 Union Home Minister will flag-off a nationwide motorcycle rally themed ‘Fight Against Drugs’ As part of this rally police riders from all States/UTs and Central Forces would reach Ekta Nagar, Gujarat to join the Ekta Parade on October 31, 2026 On October 21, 1959, ten valiant Policemen laid down their lives in an ambush laid by heavily armed Chinese troops at Hot Springs,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will pay homage to the martyrs on Police Commemoration Day at National Police Memorial in New Delhi on Wednesday, 21st October 2026
Union Home Minister will flag-off a nationwide motorcycle rally themed ‘Fight Against Drugs’
As part of this rally police riders from all States/UTs and Central Forces would reach Ekta Nagar, Gujarat to join the Ekta Parade on October 31, 2026
On October 21, 1959, ten valiant Policemen laid down their lives in an ambush laid by heavily armed Chinese troops at Hot Springs, Ladakh
October 21 is observed in commemoration of these martyrs and of all other martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty
In recognition of the sacrifices made by Police personnel and their paramount role in preserving national security and integrity, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi dedicated National Police Memorial to the nation on Police Commemoration Day-2018
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will pay homage to the martyrs on Police Commemoration Day at National Police Memorial in New Delhi on Wednesday, 21st October 2026.

The Home Minister will flag-off a motorcycle rally of about 90 Police riders from States/UTs (Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi); Central Armed Police Forces (CRPF, CISF, BSF, SSB, ITBP and NSG) and some Central Police Organisations (RPF, NDRF and NIA). This is part of a nationwide rally themed ‘Fight Against Drugs’, wherein Police riders from all States/UTs and Central Forces would reach Ekta Nagar, Gujarat to join the Ekta Parade on October 31, 2026.

On October 21, 1959, ten valiant Policemen laid down their lives in an ambush laid by heavily armed Chinese troops at Hot Springs, Ladakh. Since then, October 21 is observed as Police Commemoration Day every year. In recognition of the sacrifices made by Police personnel and their paramount role in preserving national security and integrity, the Prime Minister dedicated National Police Memorial (NPM), Chanakyapuri, New Delhi to the nation on Police Commemoration Day-2018.

The Memorial gives Police Forces a sense of national identity, pride, unity of purpose, common history and destiny, besides reinforcing their commitment to protect the nation even at the cost of their lives. The Memorial comprises a Central Sculpture, the ‘Wall of Valour’ and a Museum. The Central Sculpture, which is a 30 feet high granite monolith cenotaph, stands for strength, resilience and selfless service of Police personnel. The Wall of Valour on which the names of martyrs are engraved stands as a steadfast acknowledgement of the bravery and sacrifice of Police personnel who have laid down their lives in the line of duty since Independence. The museum is conceptualized as a historical and evolving exhibition on policing in India. The Memorial is a site of pilgrimage, a place of reverence for Police personnel and citizen alike.  The NPM is open to public on all days except Mondays. Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) organise band display, parade and retreat ceremony at the NPM on every Saturday and Sunday in the evening, starting one hour prior to sunset.

On the lines of previous years, Police Commemoration Day, i.e., October 21, will be observed across the country to pay homage to police martyrs. The main function will be organised at National Police Memorial, New Delhi, where a joint parade of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Delhi Police would be held.  As per custom, the Union Home Minister will preside over the function. Union MoS (Home), MPs with Police background, Heads of CAPFs/CPOs amongst others will also pay homage to the martyrs by laying wreaths. Retired DGs, officers from Police fraternity and other dignitaries will also attend the event.

Apart from paying homage to the Police martyrs, Union Home Minister will address the assembly. The programme will conclude with Union Home Minister laying a wreath at the altar dedicated to the martyrs of Hot Springs. The event will be telecast live on Doordarshan, webcast on Police websites and covered by AIR and media.

As a part of the remembrances, CAPFs/CPOs will organise various Commemorative Events at NPM from October 22 to 30, which will include visits of family members of martyrs, Police Band Display, motorcycle rallies, Run for Martyrs, blood donation camps, essay/painting competitions for children and display of video films showcasing sacrifice, valour and services of Police personnel. Similar programmes will be organised by all the Police Forces across the country during this period.

National Police Memorial

Chanakyapuri, New Delhi

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Adoption of Best Practices under Special Campaign 6.0: Conduction of Artificial Intelligence Workshop for senior officers of Ministry of Women & Child Development
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Women and Child Development, including all Autonomous/ Statutory Bodies under its administrative control, has initiated efforts and finalised action plans & targets to implement Special Campaign 6.0 for improving Swachhata and disposal of pending references from 2nd October - 31st October, 2026, on the lines of the Special Campaigns held in the preceding 5 years.

In accordance with the directions stipulated in the Special Campaign guidelines regarding adoption of Best Practices during the implementation phase of the campaign, an Artificial Intelligence Workshop was conducted for Under Secretary & above-level officers of the Ministry on 17.10.2026 by National e-Governance Division. The workshop was designed as a hands-on programme with approximately 70% of the sessions devoted to the practical use of AI tools.  A total of 42 participants, including Secretary, Additional Secretaries, Joint Secretaries and other senior officers of the Ministry, participated in the workshop. The following topics were covered in the workshop:

  • Introduction to AI
  • Prompt Engineering and AI Tools for Office Productivity
  • Hands-on with AI Tools
  • Ethical and Responsible use of AI and Sovereign AI

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Social Justice Empowerment Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Reviews Key Central Government Schemes, Programmes, Initiatives In Mysuru, Karnataka
Secretary Underscores The Need To Ensure Transparent And Effective Measures To Implement All The Central Government Schemes And Initiatives
Shri Pant Asks Officers, Officials To Cover All Eligible Prospective Beneficiaries Under Various Schemes And Programmes; Directs Them To Reach Out To The Probable Beneficiaries At Their Doorsteps With The Information About Various Schemes
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 5:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Secretary of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant took a comprehensive review of the Ministry’s Schemes, Programmes and Initiatives under implementation, with the State Social Welfare Department Administration at Mysuru, in Karnataka today.

The meeting was attended by the State and district government officials of the Department of Social Welfare and OBC Welfare. MD Tanda Development Corporation, also attended the meeting.

The Union Secretary reviewed the progress of the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA); Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM AJAY); National Action Plan for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE);  Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) and Other Senior Citizen Schemes, in the meeting.

The Meeting also reviewed the progress of Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship for SCs, OBCs, EBCs and DNTs, besides progress of Strengthening of Machinery for Enforcement of Protection of Civil Right Act, 1955 and Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989.

In addition, the progress of the schemes and programmes including Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in the Act of Begging (SMILE), Welfare of Transgender Persons (SMILE) and Construction of Hostels for OBC Boys and Girls, was also reviewed during the high level meeting.

Addressing the meeting, the Union Secretary underscored the need to ensure transparent and effective measures to implement all the central government schemes and initiatives, to cover all eligible prospective beneficiaries under various schemes and programmes.

He exhorted upon all officers and officials to reach out to the probable beneficiaries with the clear information about features of the various schemes, programmes and initiatives, so that the benefits under various central government schemes, could be doled out at the doorsteps of the probable beneficiaries.

Shri Pant undertook Site Visits in Mysuru and appreciated the sincere work and contribution of the officers and others in taking forward the government programmes in the larger public interest.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
SWAVLAMBAN 2026 – CURTAIN RAISER PRESS CONFERENCE
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Curtain Raiser Press Conference for the fifth edition of the Indian Navy’s flagship Naval Innovation and Indigenisation Seminar, Swavlamban 2026, was conducted in New Delhi on 19 Oct 2026 under the chairmanship of VAdm Ajay Kochhar, Vice Chief of the Naval Staff (VCNS).

The annual NIIO Seminar Swavlamban is scheduled to be conducted on 26 and 27 Oct 2026 at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi. Swavlamban 2026 will build upon the Indian Navy’s continuing efforts to translate indigenous technological innovation into operational capabilities and strengthen the foundations of Aatmanirbharta. The seminar will bring together innovators, industry partners, Start-ups, MSMEs, academia, investors and the Defence Forces to explore collaborative solutions for emerging maritime security challenges.

Addressing the media, the VCNS remarked that the evolution of Swavlamban since 2022 has connected the Indian Navy’s operational requirements with the technological capabilities of Indian industry and academia. Emphasising the changing character of modern warfare, the VCNS underscored the importance of developing niche technologies into deployable systems at sea. For a Navy operating across extended distances and undertaking prolonged deployments, he highlighted the importance of durable indigenous technologies for combat readiness, operational flexibility and sustained capability enhancement.

The exhibition at Swavlamban 2026 will include thematic areas, showcasing indigenous innovations that have emerged as success stories, covering niche technologies in Maritime Surveillance, Counter-UAS, Artificial Intelligence and Quantum, NBCD, Safety and Efficiency Enhancers. Engagements with venture capitalists and investors will form a key component of the seminar, facilitating discussions on funding opportunities, scaling of promising enterprises and commercialisation of indigenous technologies.

This year’s seminar will provide a dynamic platform for deliberations on future and emerging technologies with transformative potential to enhance naval operations and strengthen India’s maritime capabilities. Panel with SMEs will hold sessions on self-reliance and strengthening the iDEX ecosystem to build resilient supply chains, foster academic entrepreneurship and highlight the journeys of start-ups.

Swavlamban 2026 will also witness release of the Swavlamban 5.0 Document, the Compendium on Technology Imperatives, and the Naval Unified Systems, Ethernet and Tactical Utilisation (NAUSETU) Interface Standards.

The event seeks to strengthen the collaboration of the Indian Navy with the innovation ecosystem for a future-proof force, aligning technological goals with the evolving requirement of modern-day warfare.

Defence Secretary Launches New DBIM-Compliant MoD and DoD Websites
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh launched the revamped websites of Ministry of Defence (MoD) and Department of Defence (DoD) on October 19, 2026. The modern, accessible and user-friendly platforms are fully compliant with the Digital Brand Identity Manual (DBIM) 3.0 and the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW) 3.0.

The websites provide seamless access to information on MoD policies, initiatives, activities, notifications, defence-related updates and other important resources for citizens, stakeholders and users. The content is available in 22 Indian official languages, ensuring wider outreach and improved accessibility. The website can be accessed at www.mod.gov.in.

The initiative aligns with the Government's vision of Digital India and e-Governance, promoting transparency, efficiency, accessibility and citizen-centric delivery of information through a secure and modern digital platform.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NFSC Fellowship
Supporting Solapur Maharashtra’s Dr Shrikant Dilip Khandare’s Journey to Ph.D. Completion
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi

With the right support and encouragement, scholars from disadvantaged backgrounds become empowered to pursue their research aspirations, strengthen their knowledge and skills, and work towards achieving their academic goals.

Financial assistance plays an important role in enabling them to focus on their studies and realise their full potential.

Higher education and advanced research create valuable opportunities for academic excellence, professional growth and meaningful contributions to society.

Dr Shrikant Dilip Khandare, a scholar from Solapur, Maharashtra, pursued his doctoral studies with the aim of contributing to sustainable solutions for environmental challenges. After qualifying the CSIR-UGC NET in June 2018, he continued to work towards his academic aspirations. However, financial uncertainty posed challenges to the continuation of his research and created concerns about completing his Ph.D.

Coming from a family whose circumstances were described as unstable, Dr Khandare faced uncertainty about sustaining his doctoral studies. Despite his determination to continue his research, financial constraints threatened his academic progress. He acknowledged that, without financial assistance, he might have had to discontinue his doctoral programme. Nevertheless, he remained committed to pursuing his research and achieving his academic goals.

Dr Khandare’s research aspirations are closely connected to addressing environmental challenges, particularly plastic waste and pollution. He aims to contribute to the development of sustainable solutions to tackle these issues. His academic journey reflects the potential of research and higher education to support environmental sustainability and generate knowledge that can contribute to addressing pressing societal concerns.

Financial assistance under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) became an important source of support in Dr Khandare’s academic journey. He began receiving assistance in October 2019, including fellowship support and House Rent Allowance (HRA), amounting to a total of ₹9.90 lakh. This assistance helped him continue his doctoral studies and devote greater attention to his academic work without the constant uncertainty of financing his education.

With the support received under the NFSC scheme and his sustained commitment to research, Dr Khandare successfully completed his Ph.D. The fellowship played a significant role in enabling him to continue his doctoral programme and achieve this important academic milestone. His experience highlights how timely financial assistance can help scholars overcome economic barriers and pursue advanced education.

Dr Shrikant Dilip Khandare’s achievement demonstrates the importance of fellowship assistance in strengthening access to higher education and research. His journey illustrates how targeted financial support, combined with perseverance and academic commitment, can help scholars navigate financial uncertainty, complete doctoral studies and work towards their research ambitions. The NFSC scheme continues to represent an important avenue for supporting eligible Scheduled Caste students in pursuing advanced education and research.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
item.description: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions Union Minister Jitendra Singh inaugurates workplace creche and Blood Donation Camp at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi Model creche spread over 2,000 sq. ft. has capacity for 30–35 children; 27 children already enrolled: Dr. Jitendra Singh Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0 puts over 2,000 sq. ft. of underutilised office space to productive use as a workplace creche for Central Government employees and their families Over 100 People Enrol for Blood Donation at Kartavya Bhawan-3, Reflecting Strong Participation by Central Government Employees Posted…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Union Minister Jitendra Singh inaugurates workplace creche and Blood Donation Camp at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi
Model creche spread over 2,000 sq. ft. has capacity for 30–35 children; 27 children already enrolled: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0 puts over 2,000 sq. ft. of underutilised office space to productive use as a workplace creche for Central Government employees and their families
Over 100 People Enrol for Blood Donation at Kartavya Bhawan-3, Reflecting Strong Participation by Central Government Employees
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi

Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0 is being advanced through a broader approach to governance that combines efficient utilisation of government office spaces with employee welfare and a more supportive working environment, said Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, while inaugurating a workplace creche and Blood Donation Camp at Kartavya Bhawan-3, Delhi today.

Referring to the continuous reform journey under Prime Minister Narendra Modi since May 26, 2014, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that governance reforms must go beyond simplifying administrative procedures and ensuring transparency to address the practical needs of government employees. He said that providing workplace facilities that enable employees, particularly working parents, to discharge their responsibilities with greater focus is an important step towards more efficient administration and better public service delivery.

Describing the reform journey as a “Reform Express”, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the working conditions of government employees must receive due attention so that they can devote their full concentration to official responsibilities. He referred to workplace facilities such as gyms, pantry and dining areas as part of the effort to create an employee-friendly environment, adding that the newly established crèche at Kartavya Bhawan-3 extends this approach by addressing the childcare needs of working parents.

Established in accordance with the guidelines of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the creche at Kartavya Bhawan-3 is spread over more than 2,000 square feet and has the capacity to accommodate approximately 30–35 children. Of these, 27 have already been enrolled, with the process of filling the remaining slots underway.

The facility includes child-friendly washrooms, a dedicated play area with toys and learning materials, audio-visual equipment, clean drinking water, a sleeping area, a nurture and feeding room, and a kitchen or dry pantry. Safety provisions include CCTV surveillance, soft-cushioned flooring and walls, and a medical kit.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that dependable childcare at the workplace is particularly important for working mothers, who often have to balance professional responsibilities with concerns about their children’s care, nutrition and well-being. Employees whose children have enrolled at the creche had conveyed that the facility had made it easier for them to concentrate on their work, knowing that their children were receiving appropriate care and attention.

The initiatives at Kartavya Bhawan-3 complement the wider emphasis on efficient governance by addressing the needs of the workforce alongside improvements in administrative systems. The underlying principle is that a supportive workplace enables employees to perform their duties with greater concentration, contributing to more effective public service delivery.

The creche will be managed by Grih Kalyan Kendra (GKK), a society under DoPT with experience in welfare activities for Central Government employees and their families. GKK operates around six other creche facilities across Delhi and has partnered with NGO Mobile Creches to strengthen the capacities of teachers and caregivers through training and support for quality childcare practices.

The Blood Donation Camp and the creche inauguration represent complementary expressions of public service, voluntary contribution to society and institutional support for government employees and their families. Together, they reflect the broader spirit of Seva Sankalp, combining social responsibility with a commitment to responsive and inclusive governance.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that Kartavya Bhawan represents the Government’s commitment to a modern, efficient and citizen-centric administration, and that its working environment must reflect care, inclusiveness, dignity and sensitivity towards employees’ needs. He appreciated DoPT, Grih Kalyan Kendra and all officials associated with establishing the creche.

In a related initiative aligned with the objectives of Swachhata and Special Campaign 6.0, DoPT has also adopted electric vehicles for departmental use. Eighteen diesel and petrol vehicles were condemned and replaced with electric vehicles, contributing to cleaner and more sustainable government operations.

The programme was attended by senior officials associated with the concerned Ministries and Departments. Secretary, Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), Ms. Rachna Shah, and other senior officials.

item.description: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0 Records 3 Times More Cleanliness Campaign Sites and Earns ₹491.28 Crore in 17 days, Surpassing Special Campaign 5.0 DARPG in Ministry of Personnel freed 1,200 square feet of space on a single floor within its office premises as part of Special Campaign 6.0 Dr. Jitendra Singh Reviews Mid-Campaign Progress; 116 Lakh Square Feet of Space Freed as on October 19, 2026 Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:56PM by PIB Delhi Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0 Records 3 Times More Cleanliness Campaign Sites and Earns ₹491.28 Crore in 17 days, Surpassing Special Campaign 5.0
DARPG in Ministry of Personnel freed 1,200 square feet of space on a single floor within its office premises as part of Special Campaign 6.0
Dr. Jitendra Singh Reviews Mid-Campaign Progress; 116 Lakh Square Feet of Space Freed as on October 19, 2026
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:56PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State for PMO, Department of Atomic Energy, Department of Space, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, reviewed the progress of Special Campaign 6.0 and highlighted the improvement in performance over Special Swachhata Campaign 5.0 last years, in terms of cleanliness campaign sites covered, revenue earned through scrap disposal and space freed.

As on October 19, 2026, Special Swachhata Campaign 6.0 had covered 8,34,509 cleanliness campaign sites, compared to 2,75,432 during the corresponding period of Special Campaign 5.0 in 2025, registering a 3.03-fold increase. Revenue earned through scrap disposal stood at ₹491.28 crore, against ₹304.72 crore during the corresponding period last year, representing a 1.61-fold increase. The campaign had also freed 116 lakh square feet of space, compared to 113.12 lakh square feet during the corresponding period of Special Campaign 5.0.

The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) in the Ministry of Personnel has freed 1,200 square feet of space on a single floor within its office premises as part of Special Campaign 6.0. The initiative reflects the campaign’s focus on optimising the utilisation of available office space and ensuring that premises are used in accordance with functional requirements.

The Minister noted that the campaign builds on the experience of previous editions, with the objective of improving performance year after year. What began with the clearance of physical files has progressively expanded to include electronic files, e-waste management and the disposal of obsolete materials. The recovery of revenue through scrap disposal has also emerged as an important component of the campaign.

As part of the ongoing implementation phase, Dr. Jitendra Singh has urged Secretaries to ensure wider participation in Special Campaign 6.0 by extending activities to field offices and establishments across the country. He has emphasised the importance of organising dedicated one-day campaigns across offices and establishments, alongside sustained efforts to improve cleanliness and ensure the effective disposal of obsolete materials.

The campaign also focuses on clearing pending references and public grievances, reviewing physical and electronic files, and freeing up office space for productive utilisation. These efforts complement the physical cleanliness drive and extend its scope to the functioning of government offices.

Among the major contributors, the Department of School Education and Literacy had reported 4,15,353 cleanliness campaign sites, while the Ministry of Railways had generated ₹425.06 crore through scrap disposal as on October 19, 2026.

Special Campaign 6 is being implemented from October 2 to October 31, 2026. The progress review reflects the achievements recorded during the ongoing campaign, with implementation continuing until October 31.

The Minister also underscored the importance of creating greater awareness and motivation among the general public regarding cleanliness, responsible waste disposal and recycling. He highlighted the need to promote scientific management of e-waste and showcase technologies for reusing and recycling waste, including applications involving used cooking oil and plastic, to encourage wider understanding of sustainable waste-management practices.

The meeting was attended by Secretaries to the Government of India, with Ms. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG); Ms. Rachna Shah, Secretary, Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT); Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST); Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala, Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES); Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR); and Dr. Rajesh Sudhir Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology (DBT), attending in person. Other Secretaries to the Government of India joined the meeting virtually.

Secretary, DARPG, presented the progress of Special Campaign 6 across Ministries, Departments and their field establishments. DoPT informed the meeting that it had adopted electric vehicles for the Department, contributing to the objectives of Swachhata and Special Campaign 6. The Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST), highlighted the importance of assessing office space from the perspective of “utility versus availability” to ensure its optimal utilisation. Dr. Jitendra Singh urged all Secretaries to adopt this approach while reviewing space in their respective Ministries and Departments, aligning its utilisation with actual functional requirements. The Minister also urged all Secretaries to share successful initiatives and best practices with DARPG and other Ministries and Departments to facilitate the wider dissemination and replication of successful models. This would enable other Ministries and Departments to learn from these experiences and adopt similar practices, wherever relevant, to strengthen the implementation of Special Campaign 6.


 

*****

NKR/AK/NM

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Introduces Toll Plaza Feedback Feature on Rajmargyatra App to Improve National Highway User Experience
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant initiative to improve user experience at toll plazas, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has introduced ‘Toll Plaza Feedback’ feature on the Rajmargyatra mobile app to enable National Highway users to share their experience at toll plazas. The initiative aims to strengthen citizen participation and support efforts to make National Highway journeys safer, smoother and more convenient.

Simple and User-friendly Feedback Process

NHAI has been encouraging user feedback to improve service delivery at the toll plazas.  After Crossing a national highway toll plaza, Annual pass users will receive a notification from their the Rajmarg yatra app inviting them to share their toll plaza experience. In addition, all users can now access “Toll Plaza Feeback” feature within the menu section of the app to submit their feedback on any toll plaza. Users can rate their experience on a scale and select options relevant to their journey as well as add remarks, if any.

The feature provides National Highway users with a channel to report their experiences and highlight issues requiring attention. It will also support NHAI efforts to identify and monitor areas, where improvements in toll plaza services may be required.

NHAI encourages National Highway users to actively use the Toll Plaza Feedback feature and share their experiences through the Rajmargyatra app. Citizen participation will help NHAI to address user concerns and work towards improving service delivery at the toll plazas across the National Highway network.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat Organises 1,174 Programmes Across 36 States and UTs Under Fifth Week of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan
3.43 Lakh Youth and Citizens Participate in Yoga, Meditation and Drug-Free India Awareness Activities
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan, Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) organised the fifth week of the 100 Weeks Campaign on the theme “Yoga & Meditation for Nasha Mukt Yuva” and “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Par Charcha” (Neighbourhood Youth Parliament) on 17 October 2026. Organised in collaboration with spiritual organisations, university associations and industry associations, the initiative covered 36 States and Union Territories, witnessing the participation of 3,43,288 youth and citizens across 1,174 programmes.

The programmes featured a range of activities, including the Nasha Mukt Yuva Pledge, yoga and meditation sessions, awareness discussions and youth engagement activities. These initiatives aimed to encourage healthy lifestyles, promote physical and mental well-being, and raise awareness about the prevention of substance abuse. The Neighbourhood Youth Parliament discussions also provided a platform for dialogue and youth participation in advancing the vision of a drug-free India.

The campaign was organised in collaboration with partner organisations, including Heartfulness, Project Point, CIPU, ASSOCHAM, FICCI, CII and Brahma Kumaris. Their participation reflected a collective effort by spiritual institutions, industry bodies and other stakeholders to strengthen awareness and encourage young people and citizens to adopt healthier lifestyles.

 

Across the campaign, 3,380 activities were organised and 3,43,288 pledges were taken, reflecting the extensive engagement of youth and citizens in reaffirming their commitment to a drug-free India. The programmes brought together diverse stakeholders to encourage collective responsibility in preventing substance abuse and promoting awareness at the community level.

The widespread participation across States and Union Territories, supported by public representatives and partner organisations, reinforces the importance of sustained community engagement in building a healthier and drug-free society. Through the 100 Weeks Campaign, MY Bharat continues to encourage youth participation and collective action towards the vision of Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat.

***

Pawan Singh Faujdar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Government to Stay Live on Mobile: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Launches New Portal for Farmers
Farmers to Access All Agricultural Schemes on Their Mobile Phones: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Farmers to Get Direct Access to Government Assistance Without Visiting Offices: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
Single Portal for All Ministry Services to Empower Farmers Digitally: Union Agriculture Minister
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

Advancing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Digital India and his commitment to farmers’ welfare, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today formally launched the upgraded Agri Welfare Portal. The portal aims to provide farmers across the country with direct, easy access to government schemes, financial assistance and reliable agricultural information on their mobile phones, eliminating procedural hurdles and the role of intermediaries.

Addressing the launch programme, Shri Chouhan said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s clear vision is to ensure that the government remains accessible to citizens and farmers at all times through their mobile phones. Technology, he said, could fulfil its true purpose only when it reached farms and rural communities and made farmers’ lives easier. With the upgraded portal, farmers will no longer need to visit multiple government offices or navigate different websites to obtain information about schemes or submit applications. The platform will also bring together Farmer Producer Organisations, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, agricultural scientists, researchers and startups, creating a common digital platform for the wider agricultural ecosystem. Emphasising the importance of reliable information, Shri Chouhan directed officials to ensure that the portal remained accurate and regularly updated. He said outdated or incomplete information could undermine public trust in the system, making continuous updates essential to its success. He also stressed that the language and processes must be simple enough for small and marginal farmers, including those with limited formal education, to understand and use the platform with ease. To help farmers make effective use of the portal and other digital tools, a special training campaign will be conducted through Krishi Vigyan Kendras across the country.

Shri Chouhan also commended the entire technical team for developing the upgraded portal within the stipulated time. Developed in compliance with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology’s Digital Brand Identity Manual 3.0 and Guidelines for Indian Government Websites 3.0, the portal is designed to offer a secure, mobile-friendly and accessible digital experience, including for persons with disabilities. The platform will serve as a single-window gateway to major government initiatives, including PM-KISAN, AgriStack and the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, making it easier for farmers to access relevant services and information through a common interface. Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Secretary Shri Atish Chandra, Additional Secretary Pramod Meherda, senior officials from the Digital Agriculture Division and other officials from the Ministry and the National Informatics Centre were present at the launch.

 

Key Benefits of the Agri Welfare Portal

All services in one place: Information on the Ministry’s schemes, subsidies, rules and digital services will be available on a single portal, reducing the time and effort farmers spend navigating multiple platforms.

Greater transparency and fewer intermediaries: Online eligibility checks, direct application facilities and the transfer of financial assistance through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) will make processes more transparent and reduce the role of intermediaries.

Designed for rural connectivity: Built with rural users in mind, the portal is lightweight and user-friendly, enabling smooth operation on basic smartphones and in areas with weak internet connectivity.

Timely and reliable agricultural information: Farmers will be able to access authentic information on weather conditions, scientific farming practices, the availability of seeds and fertilisers, and prevailing market prices for agricultural produce.

Accessible to persons with disabilities: Designed in line with modern government accessibility standards, the portal supports screen readers and simple navigation, enabling visually impaired users and other persons with disabilities to access its services more easily.

***

SS/DK

item.title: CCPA Acts against Online Listing online listing, hosting, advertising and facilitating the sale of Regulated and Hazardous Explosive Substances
item.category: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
item.description: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution CCPA Acts against Online Listing online listing, hosting, advertising and facilitating the sale of Regulated and Hazardous Explosive Substances After CCPA intervention 3,940 sellers delisted from these 7 online platforms Any instance of sale of explosives on online platform may be reported at the National Consumer Helpline number 1915 Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) , under the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
CCPA Acts against Online Listing online listing, hosting, advertising and facilitating the sale of Regulated and Hazardous Explosive Substances
After CCPA intervention 3,940 sellers delisted from these 7 online platforms
Any instance of sale of explosives on online platform may be reported at the National Consumer Helpline number 1915
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), under the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, read with the Explosives Act, 1884, the Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012 and other applicable rules, has initiated regulatory action against the un-authorized online listing, hosting, advertising and facilitating  the sale of regulated and hazardous explosive substances, such as Ammonium Nitrate, Gun Powder, Picric Acid and Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate (PETN), on digital platforms. The action is aimed at strengthening consumer safety, public security and responsible e-commerce practices.

These substances are classified as explosives and regulated under the Explosives Act, 1884 and the rules framed thereunder. Their lawful sale and purchase require the prescribed license, and online platforms are expected to ensure that sellers’ valid PESO (Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation) license details are disclosed and that the identity and licensed status of buyers are verified before a purchase.

The CCPA initiated action regarding the online listing and sale of such substances on online platforms including:

  1. IndiaMART
  2. TradeIndia
  3. Dial4Trade
  4. Justdial
  5. Sigma-Aldrich India
  6. ExportersIndia
  7. Ibuychemikals

 

The platforms furnished details of 3,940 sellers and listing entries in all, as set out below. The listings have been delisted from all the platforms.

The CCPA has so far passed final orders in the following matters:

  • Dial4Trade: penalty of ₹10 lakh for the sale of Ammonium Nitrate.
  • ExportersIndia (Weblink.In Pvt. Ltd.): penalty of ₹10 lakh for the sale of Ammonium Nitrate and Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate (PETN).
  • ExportersIndia (Weblink.In Pvt. Ltd.): penalty of ₹10 lakh for the sale of Picric Acid.

 

      1. Dial4Trade Technologies Private Limited
  • A penalty of ₹10 lakh was imposed by CCPA on the Company and the company was directed to discontinue the listing and facilitation of sale of Ammonium Nitrate and any other explosive substance on its platform.
  • The company has challenged the order before the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) under Section 24 of the Act. After hearing the parties on 9 October 2026, the NCDRC dismissed the appeal.
  • In the Order, the listings were held to be misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices under Sections 2(28) and 2(47) of the Act and the company was directed to discontinue the listing and facilitation of sale of the said substances on its platform.

 

      1. ExportersIndia (Weblink.In Private Limited)
  • A penalty of Rs 10 lakh was imposed on the company by the CCPA for on line listing, hosting, advertising and facilitating the sale of Ammonium Nitrate and PETN, explosives whose sale is regulated under the Explosives Act, 1884 and the rules framed thereunder.
  • In another case a penalty of Rs 10 Lakh was imposed on the company for online listing, hosting, advertising and facilitating the sale of Picric Acid explosive whose sale is regulated under Explosives Act, 1884 and the rules framed thereunder.
  • ExportersIndia has filed appeals under Section 24 of the Act before the NCDRC, which are likely to be listed for hearing in the coming period.

 

      1. IndiaMART InterMESH Limited.
  • CCPA had issued notices to IndiaMART InterMESH Limited, concerning the online listing, hosting, advertising sale/ facilitating sale the Ammonium Nitrate, PETN/Gunpowder, Picric Acid hazardous substances on its platform.
  • The Director General – Investigation has completed his investigation in the matter. The report of the DG – Investigation has been shared with the company. IndiaMART has submitted its reply to the Investigation Report.
  • In compliance with the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the company has been afforded multiple opportunities for a hearing, during which it has presented its comprehensive submissions.
  • The company has approached the Hon’ble Delhi High Court by way of a writ petition challenging the show cause notices issued by the CCPA.

 

      1. Justdial
  • CCPA had issued notices to Just Dial Limited concerning the online listing, hosting, advertising sale/ facilitating sale   of Ammonium Nitrate.
  • The Director General – Investigation has completed his investigation in the matter. The report of the DG – Investigation has been shared with the company. Justdial has submitted its reply to the Investigation Report.
  • Under provisions of the Consumer Protection Act 2019 opportunity of hearing has to be given to the company before passing a final order. So far, four opportunities of hearing were given to the company. Each time the company has sought adjournments. The next and final hearing in the matter is scheduled to be held on 23rd October 2026.

 

Matters under Investigation by Director General - Investigation

  • Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals Private Limited for online listing, hosting, advertising sale/ facilitating sale of Ammonium Nitrate, PETN and Picric Acid
  • TradeIndia (Infocom Network Private Limited) for online listing, hosting, advertising sale/ facilitating sale of Picric Acid and PETN
  • Ibuychemikals for online listing, hosting, advertising sale/ facilitating sale of Picric Acid

 

The action reinforces the Government’s commitment to ensuring that digital marketplaces do not facilitate unauthorized access to regulated or dangerous substances in violation of applicable laws and consumer safety standards.

The CCPA remains committed to protecting consumer rights, ensuring safe digital marketplaces, preventing unfair trade practices, and strengthening consumer trust in the rapidly evolving e-commerce ecosystem.

***

RT/ARC

item.title: DRI seizes over seven kg amphetamine and three kg cocaine as it intensifies crackdown on drug trafficking in country; three arrested
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance DRI seizes over seven kg amphetamine and three kg cocaine as it intensifies crackdown on drug trafficking in country; three arrested Intelligence-led interceptions at Bengaluru & Delhi airports and near Nagpur expose attempts to traffic contraband concealed in passenger baggage Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:23PM by PIB Delhi The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has intensified its crackdown on narcotics trafficking through coordinated, intelligence-led operations, resulting in the seizure of around 7.1 kg amphetamine in two operations and around…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes over seven kg amphetamine and three kg cocaine as it intensifies crackdown on drug trafficking in country; three arrested
Intelligence-led interceptions at Bengaluru & Delhi airports and near Nagpur expose attempts to traffic contraband concealed in passenger baggage
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 4:23PM by PIB Delhi

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has intensified its crackdown on narcotics trafficking through coordinated, intelligence-led operations, resulting in the seizure of around 7.1 kg amphetamine in two operations and around 3.1 kg of cocaine in a third operation, leading to the arrest of three persons. The seizures were made at Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru; near Nagpur; and Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI), New Delhi.

Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted a passenger arriving at Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru, from Delhi on 14th October 2026. Examination of the passenger’s baggage led to the recovery of 5.166 kg amphetamine. The recovered substance was seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, and passenger was arrested.

Two days later, in another intelligence-led operation, officers of DRI intercepted an Indian national travelling by bus from Delhi to Hyderabad near Khapa Phata, Saoner, at outskirts of Nagpur. Examination of his backpack revealed a white crystalline substance concealed inside a new ladies’ suit.

As the backpack appeared unusually heavy, officers examined its inner lining and discovered another concealed packet containing a similar substance. Field testing yielded a positive result for amphetamine. In total, 1.97 kg amphetamine, was recovered and seized under the NDPS Act, 1985. The passenger was arrested.

In a separate operation on 15/16.10.26, acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted an Indian passenger who had arrived at Terminal 3 of IGI Airport, New Delhi, from Ghana. A systematic examination of his baggage led to the recovery of six transparent packets containing white powder, weighing 3.134 kg in total. Field testing confirmed a positive result for cocaine. The substance was seized under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and the passenger was arrested.

These operations underscore DRI’s sustained efforts to disrupt narcotics supply chains, detect ingenious concealment methods and prevent the movement of dangerous narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances through the country’s air and road networks.

****

Under the active guidance of Secretary, DSIR and a close monitoring by the nodal officer of the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Significant progress during implementation phase of Special Campaign 6 in DSIR
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 3:38PM by PIB Delhi

​The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology is actively implementing Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October, 2026 with a focus to institutionalize Swachhata, reducing pendency, disposal of e-waste, efficient record management, creation of clean and sustainable work places.

Under the active guidance of Secretary, DSIR and a close monitoring by the nodal officer of the Department and counterparts of CSIR, CEL and NRDC, as a part of the targets fixed for the implementation of Special Campaign 6 in the Department, out of the targets of 9805 physical files, 7781 files have already been reviewed and 1448 files weeded out.

The Department has achieved 100% target of reviewing e-files, easing of rules and 95% disposal of pending public grievances and appeals. Out of the target of 150 cleanliness campaign sites, the Department has already conducted cleanliness campaigns at 95 sites in the Headquarters of DIR/ CSIR and CSIR laboratories across the country. A revenue of an amount of Rs. 12,08,047 /- is earned and 2980 square feet space is freed so far.

The Department along with CSIR & its laboratories, CEL and NRDC, will continue to intensify its efforts during the remaining period of Special Campaign 6 with an aim to achieve 100% the fixed targets and to create a positive work environment with a vision to a cleaner, green and healthier India.

 

NKR/AK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas Successfully Completes Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
9,845 Cleanliness Target Units transformed; 937 public spaces cleaned; 143 water bodies cleaning drives and 276 preventive health checkups organised
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 12:47PM by PIB Delhi

Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoPNG), along with CPSEs under its administrative control and its attached offices participated in the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign from 17th September, 2026 to 2nd October, 2026. The campaign was started with pledge-taking ceremony, administrated by Secretary (PNG), on 17th September, 2026 at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi.

During the campaign, Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, regularly reviewed progress and directed all stakeholders to maximize participation and intensify efforts to further strengthen the campaign.

Key Achievements under the Campaign

Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units and Public Spaces

Under the first pillar, the Ministry and its organisations undertook cleanliness and transformation activities at identified locations, alongside initiatives covering markets, neighbourhoods, toilets, offices and water bodies.

9,845 CTUs have been transformed, with participation of 99,548 people. In addition, 937 public spaces have been cleaned, with 45,526 participants contributing to these activities.

Under the campaign, 143 cleanliness drives were undertaken at water bodies, with the participation of 1,264 individuals to promote cleanliness and conservation of water resources. In addition, 543 mohalla cleanliness drives were also organised.

Swachh Pathshala: Yuva for Swachhta

The campaign engaged students, educational institutions and community stakeholders to promote cleanliness and environmental awareness among young people.

A total of 18,700 schoolchildren participated in the reported activities. These included awareness and demonstration activities, stakeholder engagement, school-level cleanliness initiatives, Jal Sanchay Samvad and Gyan Yatra activities. The campaign also recorded 3,109 student participants in Gyan Yatra activities.

Safai Mitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir

Recognising the important contribution of sanitation workers, the Ministry's organisations conducted 234 Safai Mitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir. These camps recorded the participation of 7,098 sanitation workers.

276 preventive health check-ups were organised for 4,365 participants, while 3,518 PPE kits were distributed. The initiatives reflect the emphasis on sanitation workers' safety, health, dignity and access to welfare benefits.

Jan Bhagidari for Swachhta

Citizen participation was encouraged through awareness campaigns, composting initiatives, plastic-reduction activities and community events. The campaign also witnessed 450 composting awareness drives, 154 Sports for Swachhta activities involving 3,530 participants, and Say No to Plastics activities with 2,662 participants, promoting sustainable waste management and community participation in cleanliness initiatives.

 

 

Swachhata Se Samriddhi

Under the fifth pillar, activities focused on waste-to-wealth initiatives and the circular economy, including Kabaad Se Jugaad and Kabaad Se Kala. The reported achievements included engagement with 191 art colleges and institutions, 175 plastic recycling melas, assessment of 135 Plastic Waste Management Units (PWMUs), 687 entries under Kabaad Se Jugaad and 607 entries under Kabaad Se Kala.

These activities encouraged creative reuse of waste and promoted awareness of resource recovery and sustainable waste management.

 

Sustaining the Spirit of Swachhata

The achievements reflect the collective efforts of the Ministry, its CPSEs and associated organisations, employees, students, sanitation workers and citizens. Through cleanliness drives, awareness programmes, welfare camps and waste-management initiatives, the campaign sought to strengthen public participation and encourage the adoption of cleanliness as a sustained practice.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas remains committed to promoting cleanliness, environmental responsibility and community participation, contributing to the broader vision of a clean and developed India.

******

The implementation of the Campaign is being closely monitored under the guidance of Secretary (LR), with a strong focus on accountability, regular reviews and achievement…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
Department of Land Resources Advances Special Campaign 6 with Focus on Swachhata, Records Management and Pendency Disposal
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi

 

The Department of Land Resources is implementing Special Campaign 6 with a focused emphasis on institutionalizing Swachhata, strengthening records management and expediting the disposal of pending matters. The implementation of the Campaign is being closely monitored under the guidance of Secretary (LR), with a strong focus on accountability, regular reviews and achievement of time-bound outcomes.

Progress under the Campaign is reviewed weekly by Secretary (LR) in meetings with senior officers. Secretary (LR) has also visited the Department’s offices and Record Room and directed all Divisional Heads to ensure effective monitoring of cleanliness drives, systematic review of records and weeding out of files in accordance with the prescribed procedures. The Nodal Officer is conducting regular review meetings with the Divisions and inspecting office premises to assess progress and ensure effective implementation. Officers and officials have been sensitized to the objectives of the Campaign and are actively participating in its various activities.

The Department has made significant progress in the disposal of pending matters and the review of records. Of the 12 identified cleanliness activities, 5 have been completed. Further, 90% of public grievances have been disposed of against the target set for the Campaign. In the area of records management, 945 out of 1,280 physical files and 242 out of 501 e-files have been reviewed for recording, weeding out or closure, as applicable. Progress under the Campaign is being regularly updated on the SCDPM Portal of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).

As part of its efforts to promote awareness and encourage employee participation, the Department organized a debate on “Swachhata Evam Jal Sanchay” on 29 September 2026. Recognizing the importance of mental and physical well-being, a Yoga Session was organized for employees on 30 September 2026 at the Rejuve Wellness Centre, Shivaji Stadium Annexe Office, New Delhi. On the same day, the Department also felicitated its cleaning and housekeeping staff in recognition of their dedicated services and valuable contribution towards maintaining cleanliness in the workplace.

In the spirit of the Swachhata Hi Seva initiative and its theme, “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath”, the Department organized a Shramdaan activity at the public park near Scope Complex, New Delhi, on 1 October 2026. Further, the Department observed Swachhata Pakhwada from 1 to 15 October 2026, reaffirming its commitment to promoting cleanliness, hygiene and sustainable behavioural change in the workplace.

To encourage environmental awareness and community participation, officers and staff were encouraged to undertake plantation activities at their homes and in nearby areas on 2 October 2026 under the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative. Other activities planned under the Campaign include another Yoga Session, a lecture on mental health and a painting competition for employees.

The Department is also disseminating information on the activities undertaken and progress achieved under the Campaign through its social media platforms, including X, Facebook and Instagram, with a view to raising awareness and highlighting its initiatives.

Through sustained monitoring, systematic records management, expeditious disposal of pending matters and active participation of officers and staff, the Department of Land Resources is making concerted efforts to achieve the objectives of Special Campaign 6. These initiatives reflect the Department’s continued commitment to institutionalizing Swachhata and fostering a clean, efficient, well-organized and responsive work environment.

SS/HR

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India announces the 10 winners of its online Human Rights Quiz-2026 organised ahead of its 33rd Foundation Day in collaboration with MyGov
The Quiz aimed to promote awareness of Human Rights, PHR Act and NHRC’s Functions
The quiz saw participation from all States and Union Territories (UTs) of the country with 1,67,127 views and 26,459 submissions
Most submissions were in the age group of 18-24
Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu topped the state-wise participation
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 12:02PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission has announced the 10 winners of its online 'Human Rights Quiz-2026: Celebrating Life, Liberty, Equality and Dignity'. It was organised in collaboration with MyGov from 1st September to 10th October 2026 in the run-up to its 33rd Foundation Day. The quiz sought to engage everyone in learning about human rights, the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993 and the functions, powers and duties of the NHRC in promoting and protecting human rights across the country.

The 1st prize of Rs.15,000/- has been won by Ms. Aarti Mahajan. The 2nd prize of Rs.10,000/- has been won by Ms. Ritika and the 3rd prize of Rs.5,000/- has gone to Ms. Tooba Benazeer. The seven consolation prizes of Rs.2,000/- each have gone to Shri Aditya Gupta, Shri Tarun, Shri Rani Mandal, Shri Basant Kumar Mahato, Shri Likhth Kumar A and Ms. Deepika Madasu.

The quiz saw participation from all States and Union Territories (UTs) of the country. It attracted 1,67,127 views with 26,459 submissions. Out of them, most submissions were in the age group of 18-24. Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu topped the state-wise participation.

5,753 participants secured 15 out of 15 score, of which the 10 winners were decided by a draw of lots by the MyGov team as per the terms and conditions of the quiz. Participants were required to answer a maximum of 15 questions within 300 seconds.

item.description: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution India to Host 61st Meeting of International Committee of Legal Metrology for the First Time in New Delhi from 26–28 October 2026 More than 100 international delegates and legal metrology experts to participate in the meeting OIML Strategy Workshop and international seminar to deliberate on emerging technologies, digitalisation and the future of global legal metrology Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 11:26AM by PIB Delhi India will host the 61st Meeting of the International Committee of Legal Metrology (CIML) for the first…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
India to Host 61st Meeting of International Committee of Legal Metrology for the First Time in New Delhi from 26–28 October 2026
More than 100 international delegates and legal metrology experts to participate in the meeting
OIML Strategy Workshop and international seminar to deliberate on emerging technologies, digitalisation and the future of global legal metrology
Posted On: 19 OCT 2026 11:26AM by PIB Delhi

India will host the 61st Meeting of the International Committee of Legal Metrology (CIML) for the first time from 26 to 28 October 2026 in New Delhi. The meeting is being organised by the Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India, in association with the International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML).

The meeting is expected to bring together more than 100 international delegates and legal metrology experts from across the world, including representatives of OIML Member States, Corresponding Member States and international organisations. Hosting the meeting for the first time marks a significant milestone in India's growing role in international cooperation, harmonisation of measurement standards, promotion of fair trade and consumer protection.

OIML Strategy Workshop and International Seminar

An international seminar on “Evolutions in Legal Metrology” will be organised on 26 October 2026. The seminar will bring together experts from different countries to exchange experiences and best practices on the modernisation of legal metrology systems. Discussions will cover digitalisation of regulatory services, international harmonisation and recognition of measuring instruments, e-learning tools and innovative approaches to legal metrology administration.

An OIML Strategy Workshop will also be organised on 27 October 2026, providing a platform for participating countries and international experts to deliberate on the future strategic direction and priorities of the organisation. Discussions are expected to cover emerging challenges, technological advancements, digital transformation, international cooperation and the evolving requirements of legal metrology systems worldwide.

Key Areas of Deliberation

During the three-day programme, CIML members will deliberate on important matters relating to the development and revision of international recommendations, technical activities of the OIML, the OIML Certification System (OIML-CS), digital transformation, capacity building and international cooperation.

The meeting will facilitate the exchange of technical knowledge and experience among participating countries, supporting efforts to strengthen measurement systems and promote internationally recognised standards.

The 60th CIML Meeting was held on 13 and 15 October 2025 in Paris, France, with representatives of 55 Member States present or represented, along with representatives of 12 Corresponding Members and five organisations in liaison. Key outcomes included the approval of technical publications relating to automated refractometers, weights and traffic speed meters, along with discussions on the framework for the OIML Certification System, digitalisation and international cooperation.

Strengthening India's Role in Global Legal Metrology

Hosting the 61st CIML Meeting provides India with an opportunity to showcase its reforms and advancements in legal metrology on an international platform. The Department of Consumer Affairs has undertaken several initiatives to modernise the regulatory framework, simplify compliance procedures, promote trust-based regulation and facilitate Ease of Doing Business while ensuring robust consumer protection.

The meeting is expected to witness participation from representatives of OIML Member States, including France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Japan, China, Australia, Switzerland, the United States of America, South Africa and Brazil, among others. Representatives of Corresponding Members and associated international organisations are also expected to participate.

The diverse participation will provide opportunities to exchange experiences, share best practices and strengthen international cooperation in legal metrology. The meeting, along with the OIML Strategy Workshop and international seminar, will contribute to discussions on reliable measurements, fair trade, technological innovation and consumer confidence, while advancing India's vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Benefits for Industry and Consumers

The meeting is expected to benefit Indian manufacturers by enhancing awareness of international measurement standards, conformity assessment requirements and the OIML Certification System. This can support the development of quality products and facilitate access to international markets.

Greater harmonisation of measurement requirements can also help reduce technical barriers to trade and avoid duplication in testing and certification, where applicable. For consumers, reliable and accurate measurements are essential to ensuring fairness in transactions, correct quantity declarations and greater confidence in goods and services.

The event will also provide India with an opportunity to share its experience in regulatory reforms, digitalisation and Ease of Doing Business, while contributing to international discussions on modern and effective legal metrology systems.

International Cooperation in Legal Metrology

The International Organization of Legal Metrology (OIML) is an intergovernmental organisation established in 1955 to promote the global harmonisation of legal metrology procedures. It develops international recommendations, standards and related documents for measuring instruments used in trade, industry, healthcare, safety and environmental protection.

The International Committee of Legal Metrology (CIML) is the principal decision-making body responsible for guiding the technical and administrative activities of the OIML. Its annual meeting provides a global platform for deliberations on policy matters, technical developments and international cooperation in legal metrology.

The hosting of the 61st CIML Meeting reinforces India's commitment to international collaboration and the development of harmonised measurement standards, supporting fair trade, consumer protection and confidence in measurement systems worldwide.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA’S GREETINGS ON DURGA PUJA
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 10:47PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu sends her greetings to her fellow citizens on Durga Puja.

In a message, the President has said, “On the auspicious occasion of Durga Puja, I extend my heartfelt greetings and best wishes to all Indians residing in the country and abroad.

The festival of Durga Puja reflects India’s rich spiritual heritage. The victory of Maa Durga over Mahishasura is an inspiring example of the triumph of divine forces over evil. Maa Durga is worshipped as the deity who blesses people with wisdom to work for well-being of others. The festival of Durga Puja brings Indians together. The celebrations beautifully showcase our traditions, lifestyle, art and culture.

Durga Puja reflects our tradition of revering the strength of women. We can express our true devotion to Maa Durga by ensuring respect for women in every aspect of personal and social lives.

I pray that the blessings of Maa Durga bring happiness and prosperity to all citizens and that our nation continues on the path of rapid development”.

 

****

MJPS/SS/PRK

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Social Justice Empowerment Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Visits Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 in Mysuru, Karnataka
Nine Days Mela Features 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans
12 States, Union Territories Participating in the Mela
Secretary Reiterates Government’s Commitment To Ensure Strong Market Access, Encourage Entrepreneurship And Advance Economic Empowerment Of Disadvantaged Communities
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Secretary of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant visited the ongoing Nine Days Shilp Samagam Mela 2026, at Mysuru in Karnataka this evening.

The Mela is being organized by the Ministry through joint partnership of three national corporations under the Ministry namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), which provide financial assistance to artisans and eligible beneficiaries.

During the visit to Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds, the Secretary inspected stalls and talked to the Stall Managers and visitors.

The Union Secretary is on a two days official visit to Mysuru to take comprehensive review of the Ministry’s Schemes, Programmes and Initiatives under implementation, with the Administration. He is also undertaking Site Visits in Mysuru.

Shri Pant said through such initiatives, the Ministry continues to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and advance the economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities.

The Shilp Samagam Mela continues until October 19 Monday, offering visitors an opportunity to explore India’s traditional crafts and handloom products while supporting the livelihoods of artisans.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela is underway since October 11 and provides a marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Safai Karamcharis, enabling them to showcase their traditional handicrafts, handloom products and other goods to a wider audience.

The Official informed that the ongoing Mela features 83 stalls, including 80 stalls allotted to artisans, among them 37 women artisans. Artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, are participating in the exhibition.

He said the stalls feature with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience.

The Official further said the Mela is designed to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through direct interaction with visitors and prospective customers, participating artisans can display their products, expand their customer base and improve the market reach of their enterprises. The initiative also promotes India’s rich cultural heritage and supports the preservation of traditional art forms and skills, he added.

He added that the Mela also serves as an important platform for disseminating information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry and its three national corporations, helping eligible beneficiaries learn about available financial assistance and entrepreneurship opportunities.

The Official informed that the Ministry facilitates artisans’ participation by providing free stalls and support towards travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods and meals, in accordance with the applicable arrangements.

It is pertinent to mention that in addition to the Mela, the Ministry is promoting the BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) initiative to expand market access for products made by target-group artisans through digital platforms in India and abroad. Branding products under BHARAT TULIP is intended to improve their visibility, facilitate online sales and connect traditional artisans with a wider customer base.

The Ministry has been organizing Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022, benefiting 975 artisans through 13 fairs held so far.

The ongoing Mysuru edition is the first Shilp Samagam Mela of the financial year 2026–27.

The Ministry also proposes to organize additional fairs in Guwahati (Oct 21 to 28, 2026); Dilli Haat in New Delhi, Jodhpur and Lucknow during the current financial year, alongside participation in major exhibitions such as the India International Trade Fair 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in February 2027.
