item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Home Affairs
On October 20, 2026, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah will meet families of those who lost their lives —in Mansa, Sangrur and Gurdaspur— for speaking against 'chitta' (synthetic drug) traders in Punjab
Union Home Minister says, Punjab government has left no stone unturned in pushing the state into an abyss of drug abuse, a situation that has caused many families to lose their children
The grief these families are enduring over their loss cannot be expressed in words
Attempts to silence those who raise their voices against this dark drug trade will never succeed; the people of the state will give a befitting reply
Government of India will track down drug traffickers and put them behind bars, ensuring that Punjab—and the entire nation—is rid of drug menace
 
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 9:10PM by PIB Delhi

On October 20, 2026, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah will meet families of those who lost their lives —in Mansa, Sangrur and Gurdaspur— for speaking against 'chitta' (synthetic drug) traders in Punjab.

In a post on X platform, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Punjab government has left no stone unturned in pushing the state into an abyss of drug abuse, a situation that has caused many families to lose their children. He said that the grief these families are enduring is beyond words. Attempts to silence those who raise their voices against this dark drug trade will never succeed, and the people of the state will provide a befitting response. Shri Shah said that the Government of India will track down those involved in the 'chitta' trade and put them behind bars, ensuring that Punjab—and the entire country—is completely rid of this drug menace.

आप-दा सरकार ने पंजाब को नशे के गर्त में धकेलने में कोई कोर-कसर नहीं छोड़ी है, जिसके कारण अनेक परिवारों को अपने बच्चों को खोना पड़ा है। AAP सरकार के संरक्षण में फल-फूल रहे चिट्टा कारोबारियों के खिलाफ आवाज उठाने वाले जिन लोगों को हाल ही में अपना जीवन गँवाना पड़ा, मंगलवार (20 अक्टूबर) को उनके परिजनों से मानसा, संगरूर व गुरदासपुर में मिलूँगा। इन परिवारों ने जो खोया है, उस दुःख को शब्दों में बयान नहीं किया जा सकता। नशे के इस काले कारोबार के खिलाफ उठने वाली आवाजों को दबाने की कोशिश कभी सफल नहीं होगी और प्रदेशवासी इसका मुँहतोड़ जवाब देंगे। भारत सरकार चिट्टा कारोबारियों को चुन-चुनकर जेल की सलाखों के पीछे भेजेगी और पंजाब सहित पूरे देश को नशे के इस कारोबार से मुक्त बनाकर रहेगी।

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Education

Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, is actively implementing Special Campaign 6 from Oct 2 to 31, 2026 , with a focus on improving administrative efficiency, promoting cleanliness across school campuses and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Education
Department of School Education and Literacy focuses on administrative efficiency, cleaner school campuses and responsible e-waste Management as part of Special Campaign 6
Nationwide e-waste awareness and collection drive to be organised on October 28, 2026.
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi

Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, is actively implementing Special Campaign 6 from Oct 2 to 31, 2026, with a focus on improving administrative efficiency, promoting cleanliness across school campuses and strengthening responsible electronic waste (e-waste) management. The Campaign also seeks to encourage school students and communities to adopt sustainable practices.

Key focus areas under Special Campaign 6 include:

  1. Minimising Pendency and Enhancing Efficiency in Official Work

Efforts are being undertaken across the Department and its organisations to minimise pendency in official work, review files across various categories, digitise records, weed out obsolete files and strengthen record management practices. These measures aim to streamline administrative processes, optimise the use of office space and promote efficient functioning.

 

  1. Promoting Cleanliness across School Campuses

Spearheaded by Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, schools across the country are undertaking cleanliness drives to maintain clean and hygienic campuses. These efforts aim to strengthen a culture of cleanliness and collective responsibility among students and school staff to create healthier learning environments.

  1. Strengthening e-Waste Awareness and Collection in Schools

As part of Special Campaign 6 and under the aegis of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, e-waste awareness and collection drives are being undertaken in schools across the nation to sensitise students and teachers to the importance of responsible e-waste management.

The activities focus on raising awareness about the environmental impact of electronic waste and encouraging students to become active participants in e-waste management by reducing electronic waste and ensuring that discarded equipment is disposed of through authorized channels.

These efforts seek to nurture environmentally conscious behaviour among students and strengthen the role of schools in promoting sustainable practices.

 

  1. Installation of e-waste bins and Murals at Kartavya Bhavan 2

To mark the International e-waste Day on October 14, 2026, DoSEL installed a creative e-waste mural and e-waste bins at Kartavya Bhavan 2. The mural is made from 50 kg e-waste collected by school students. Aligned with the vision of the National Education Policy 2020 and Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, the mural promotes the message of “Reduce, Reuse and Recycle”. The bins provide a designated facility for collecting discarded electronic items and reinforce the importance of appropriate e-waste management in institutional settings.

  1. Commitment to Environment Friendliness

Secretary, DoSEL, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar chaired a video conference with States/UTs and autonomous bodies on October 16, 2026 to review preparations for the nationwide e-waste awareness and collection drive scheduled on October 28, 2026. The Secretary briefed the participants about the activities to be carried out including the IEC campaign and emphasized upon chalking out a plan for handing over the e-waste collected in schools to authorized vendors.

By combining school-level cleanliness drives with e-waste awareness and collection initiatives under the aegis of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, Special Campaign 6 reinforces the importance of collective action in building clean, environmentally responsible educational institutions.

The campaign aims to institutionalize Swachhata, reduce pendency, promote efficient record management and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Special Campaign 6.0: Department of Posts Achieves Significant Progress in Grievance Redressal, Cleanliness, E-Waste Disposal and Space Management
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts, under the Ministry of Communications, has made significant progress during the implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, being undertaken across postal establishments throughout the country from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign aims to institutionalize Swachhata, reduce pendency, promote efficient record management and ensure responsible disposal of e-waste, while improving the working environment and citizen experience at postal establishments.

Under Special Campaign 6, the Department has set ambitious targets for the resolution of 1,50,000 public grievances, disposal of 1,500 appeals and cleanliness drives at 1,35,000 sites nationwide. The campaign builds on the Department’s continued efforts towards efficient public service delivery, accountable governance and sustainable office management.

Significant Progress Till 16th October 2026

The Department has recorded the following achievements during the implementation phase:

Cleanliness Drives: Cleanliness activities have been undertaken at 73,814 sites, including post offices, accounting for approximately 55% of the overall target of 1,35,000 sites.

Public Grievance Redressal: A total of 1,00,214 public grievances have been resolved against the campaign target of 1,50,000, achieving approximately 67% of the target.

Appeal Disposal: 764 appeals have been disposed of against the target of 1,500, achieving approximately 51% of the target.

Scrap Disposal and Revenue Generation: A total of 3,06,026 kg of scrap has been disposed of since 2nd October 2026, generating revenue of ₹67.56 lakh.

E-Waste Management: In line with the campaign’s focus on scientific e-waste management, 17,980 kg of e-waste has been disposed of, generating revenue of ₹27.64 lakh. These efforts reflect the Department’s commitment to responsible handling and disposal of obsolete electronic equipment.

Innovative Initiatives: Turning Waste into Wealth

Postal Circles have also undertaken innovative initiatives to promote recycling, reuse and the productive utilization of available resources.

In West Bengal Circle, departmental carpenters and Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) renovated the Senior Manager’s Chamber at the Mail Motor Service (MMS), Kolkata, using recycled wooden scrap. The initiative exemplifies the concept of “Waste to Wealth”, demonstrating how discarded materials can be creatively reused to improve office infrastructure.

Citizen-Centric Governance and Service Delivery

As part of its citizen-centric initiatives, the Department has also introduced DigiPost, a phygital mail service through which traffic e-challans issued by Gujarat Police are digitally transmitted for physical delivery to citizens. The initiative demonstrates the potential of the postal network to facilitate the delivery of digitally generated citizen services through its extensive physical reach.

The Department of Posts will continue to intensify its efforts during the remaining period of Special Campaign 6 to achieve the prescribed targets, sustain cleanliness practices, ensure scientific e-waste management and reinforce its commitment to responsive, efficient and citizen-centric governance.

Ministry of Defence
LOKAYAN 2026 – INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI DEPARTS SALALAH, OMAN
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy’s three-masted sail training ship INS Sudarshini departed Salalah, Oman, post her visit from 14- 17 Oct 2026, continuing her historic transoceanic deployment, Lokayan-2026. The voyage reflects the Indian Navy’s rich maritime heritage and its commitment to nurturing professional seamanship, resilience and leadership among naval trainees.

During the port call, professional interactions and sporting engagements fostered camaraderie and reinforced bonds of friendship between the Indian Navy and the Royal Navy of Oman, further strengthening people-to-people ties.

As Lokayan-2026 progresses through its tenth month, INS Sudarshini’s voyage exemplifies the Indian Navy’s spirit of exploration, professional excellence and commitment to maritime diplomacy. Traversing international waters, the ship serves as an ambassador of India, fostering goodwill and maritime partnerships while carrying the civilisational ethos of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam and advancing the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
NCRTC Celebrates Namo Bharat Diwas 2026, Marking Three Successful Years of Namo Bharat Operations
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi

NCRTC celebrated ‘Namo Bharat Diwas 2026’, marking three successful years of Namo Bharat operations and a transformative journey in regional mobility on 17th October 2026 in New Delhi. The occasion was graced by Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal; Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu; Secretary, Department of Capital Development, MoHUA, and Chairperson, NCRTC, Smt. D. Thara; and Secretary, Department of Urban Development, Shri Satendra Singh. Managing Director, NCRTC, Shri Shalabh Goel, along with the Directors and senior officials, welcomed the dignitaries.

On this occasion, NCRTC reflected on the remarkable journey of Namo Bharat, highlighting key milestones, initiatives to strengthen multimodal connectivity, first- and last-mile connectivity to enhance the commuter experience, and initiatives such as Solar on Track and the development of a 110 MW captive solar power plant to promote the environmental and financial sustainability of the project. These achievements and the progress made by the project were showcased through a film, highlighting the efforts, innovations and initiatives that continue to shape Namo Bharat’s journey.

Speaking on the occasion, Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, said, “Namo Bharat’ is not merely a name; it embodies the spirit of putting the nation first, along with the values of dedication, culture and traditions. Namo Bharat rapid rail is ushering in a new era of regional connectivity in India, giving a new dimension to the future of urban transportation. Since its inauguration by Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 20 October 2023, the 82-km-long Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut corridor has recorded over 4.5 crore passenger journeys. This achievement reflects the growing trust of the people in modern, safe and seamless transportation.”

He also added, “I believe that better transportation does not merely reduce distances between cities but also connects people with new opportunities, thereby accelerating regional development and economic progress. I commend all the officers, engineers, technical experts, employees and workers of NCRTC for their dedicated and committed contribution towards realising this ambitious project.”

Namo Bharat operations commenced in October 2023 with the inauguration of the 17-km Priority Section between Sahibabad and Duhai Depot. Post which, the entire corridor was operationalised in a phased manner. On 22 February 2026, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi dedicated the entire 82-km Namo Bharat corridor to the nation, along with Meerut Metro. Namo Bharat currently serves over 1.1 lakh commuters daily and has recently recorded its highest-ever single-day ridership of around 1.68 lakh. With its fast, frequent and reliable services, Namo Bharat is helping people travel more efficiently, bringing workplaces, educational institutions and economic centres within easier reach and giving commuters greater convenience and more time in their daily lives. Two more priority Namo Bharat corridors i.e. Delhi-Panipat-Karnal and Delhi-Gurugram-Behror are likely to receive the approval soon. Two other corridors, Ghaziabad-Jewar and Noida-Faridabad-Gurgaon, are also in the DPR stage.

The occasion also celebrated the people behind this transformation. Addressing the gathering, Managing Director, NCRTC, Shri Shalabh Goel, said, “NCRTC was established with a vision to develop a modern, safe, reliable and environmentally friendly regional transport system in the country. Today, when we look back, it is a matter of pride to see that we have not limited this vision to paper but have made concrete and remarkable progress towards translating it into reality.” He expressed special gratitude to the families who have stood firmly beside team members through every challenge, acknowledging their unwavering support as an integral part of the organisation’s journey.

The occasion also featured the Annual NCRTC Awards, where employees were felicitated for their exemplary performance during the year. The awardees were recognised for their dedication, and commitment to excellence, acknowledging their invaluable contribution to the successful implementation and operation of Namo Bharat. The awards celebrated not only individual achievements but also the collective spirit and teamwork that continue to drive NCRTC’s journey forward. Adding a vibrant cultural dimension to the celebrations, music and dance performances added colour and energy to the occasion.

The journey of Namo Bharat stands as a testament to the power of modern public transport to bring people closer to opportunities and contribute to a more connected, accessible and sustainable region. With commuters at the heart of its vision, NCRTC remains committed to advancing safe, comfortable, reliable and efficient mobility while continuing to build on the achievements of Namo Bharat for the people of the region.

item.description: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Union Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Visits Munsyari Coldwater Fisheries Cluster; Interacts with Trout Farmers and Reviews Cluster Development Initiatives Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 2:31PM by PIB Delhi Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, undertook an official visit to Munsyari, district Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, on 18 October 2026 to review the progress of coldwater aquaculture development in the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Union Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Visits Munsyari Coldwater Fisheries Cluster; Interacts with Trout Farmers and Reviews Cluster Development Initiatives
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 2:31PM by PIB Delhi

Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, undertook an official visit to Munsyari, district Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, on 18 October 2026 to review the progress of coldwater aquaculture development in the Himalayan region.

During the visit, the Secretary interacted with trout farmers at Johar Matsya Swayatt Sehkarita, Namjala Trout Farm, Munsyari, and appreciated the pioneering role of local cooperatives in adopting rainbow trout farming as a sustainable livelihood option. He noted that Munsiyari, with its glacial streams of the Gori Ganga and ideal water temperature, has emerged as a hub for rainbow trout culture, transforming subsistence farming into a semi‑commercial enterprise.Dr. Likhi interacted with trout fish farmers, who shared their experiences and insights on trout farming in the region.

The Government of India has notified 34 fisheries clusters across the country. Pithoragarh has been notified as a Cold Water Fisheries Cluster under PMMSY, with significant potential to strengthen fisheries cooperatives, enhance livelihood opportunities and promote sustainable fisheries development in the Himalayan region.The visit by the Secretary, Department of Fisheries, marks an important step towards further strengthening trout farming in Uttarakhand and other Himalayan regions.The Department of Fisheries, Government of Uttarakhand, is exporting trout to Nepal and supplying trout to the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) under an MoU entered between the Government of Uttarakhand and ITBP.

The Secretary highlighted that coldwater fisheries in hilly states such as Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh are of strategic importance for livelihood diversification, nutritional security, and export potential.He emphasized that the Government of India, under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), has invested over ₹2,299 crore in coldwater regions, supporting raceways, hatcheries, feed mills, cold storages, and post‑harvest infrastructure.

India’s coldwater fisheries are concentrated in six hilly states and UTs — Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh. These regions, with their glaciated rivers, high‑altitude lakes, and pristine streams, provide ideal ecological conditions for rainbow trout and other high‑value coldwater species. Under PMMSY, more than 5,600 raceways, 54 hatcheries, 293 cold storages, and 260 feed mills have been sanctioned across these states. Trout production has grown six‑fold in the last decade, reaching nearly 5,000 MT annually, with Uttarakhand achieving its first international export to Nepal in June 2026.

In Uttarakhand, projects worth ₹317 crore have been sanctioned, including modern fish markets, landing centres, and an integrated aquapark at Sitarganj. The state has also launched the Trout Protsahan Yojna with an outlay of ₹170 crore, aiming to establish 1,500 raceways, 100 mini hatcheries, and 600 cold‑storage facilities by 2028–29.

The Secretary commended the role of ICAR‑Central Institute of Coldwater Fisheries Research (DCFR), Bhimtal, in introducing rainbow trout to Munsiyari and providing scientific support in seed production, disease management, and farmer training. He also appreciated the historic achievement of Uttarakhand’s first trout export to Nepal in June 2026, which has opened new avenues for international trade.

The visit also underscored the socio‑economic impact of trout farming in border villages, providing livelihood diversification, eco‑tourism opportunities, and assured institutional market linkages with the Indo‑Tibetan Border Police (ITBP).

He underlined that coldwater aquaculture is not only enhancing farmers’ incomes but also contributing to eco‑tourism, conservation of endangered species like Mahseer, and strengthening border village economies.

Biofortified crops are being developed to improve the intake of essential vitamins and minerals through daily food consumption. In this context, ICAR-CPRI (Indian Council of Agricultural Research- Central Potato Research Institute) developed nutrient-rich coloured potato varieties,…
item.content:encoded:
PIB Backgrounder
India’s Nutrient-Rich Purple Potato
Kufri Jamunia: Integrating Nutrition into one of India’s Most Common Staple Crops
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 1:44PM by PIB Delhi

Hidden hunger remains a major nutritional challenge despite adequate calorie intake in many populations. Biofortified crops are being developed to improve the intake of essential vitamins and minerals through daily food consumption. In this context, ICAR-CPRI (Indian Council of Agricultural Research- Central Potato Research Institute) developed nutrient-rich coloured potato varieties, including Kufri neelkanth, Kufri manik, and Kufri jamunia. These varieties contain important antioxidants and micronutrients, such as anthocyanins, iron, and zinc. Among them, Kufri jamunia represents a major advancement due to its higher levels of Vitamin C, anthocyanins, and carotenoids. Its improved nutritional profile, attractive purple flesh, and strong consumer appeal make it an important variety for addressing hidden hunger and improving nutritional security.

 

Potatoes Beyond Calories: Addressing Hidden Hunger

Hidden hunger remains a major public health challenge despite adequate calorie intake. It occurs when people consume sufficient food but lack essential vitamins and minerals in their diet. To address this challenge, scientists are increasingly developing biofortified crops with enhanced nutritional value. Biofortification improves the nutrient content of crops through plant breeding, enabling food to naturally provide higher levels of essential nutrients. Unlike conventional food fortification, which adds nutrients during processing, biofortification integrates nutrition directly into the crop. This makes it a sustainable and cost-effective approach to improving nutritional quality in commonly consumed foods. It also strengthens long-term nutritional security.

One important outcome of biofortification research has been the development of coloured potato varieties with enhanced nutritional value. These include red, purple, and blue-fleshed potatoes. These potatoes contain natural pigments, such as anthocyanins and carotenoids, which give them their distinctive colours. Coloured potatoes are rich in antioxidants and micronutrients such as iron and zinc.

 

Nutrient-Rich Coloured Potato Varieties Developed by ICAR-CPRI

ICAR-CPRI (Indian Council of Agricultural Research- Central Potato Research Institute) has developed the following nutrient-rich coloured potato varieties:

  • Kufri Neelkanth was the first purple-skinned specialty potato variety developed by ICAR-CPRI (Central Potato Research Institute), released in 2018. The variety is suitable for cultivation in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh. It is known for its high antioxidant content. The variety is suitable for people of all age groups.
  • Kufri manik was released in 2021. It produces attractive, deep red tubers with a round shape, medium eyes, and yellow flesh. The variety is rich in nutrients and contains high levels of anthocyanin, zinc, and iron.
  • Kufri jamunia was officially released in 2024. The variety contains higher levels of ascorbic acid, anthocyanin, and carotenoids than Kufri manik and Kufri neelkanth. Its purple flesh indicates high antioxidant content and better nutritional quality. Kufri jamunia also contains enhanced levels of zinc and iron. The variety is suitable for table purposes and adds novelty to different food preparations due to its unique purple colour. Hence, this variety is observed to have very high consumer appeal.

 

Kufri jamunia: A Biofortified Purple Potato for Nutritional Security

Kufri jamunia is a medium-maturing potato variety with medium-tall plants and a semi-compact canopy. The tubers are dark purple on the skin and purple in the flesh. They are oblong, with shallow eyes and a mealy texture. Each plant produces 10–12 medium to large tubers.

 

Salient characteristics of Kufri jamunia are:
• Produces 32-35 tonnes per hectare under recommended cultivation practices.
• Recorded around 49 tonnes per hectare yield in station trials at 90 days duration.
• Marketable yield reached nearly 90% of total production in trials.
• Shows medium dormancy of around 6-8 weeks. Hence, tubers do not sprout quickly.
• Possesses good storage quality with low rottage and minimal weight loss.

 

Key Nutritional Components in Kufri Jamunia

Kufri jamunia contains 42.05 mg/100 g of anthocyanins in flesh and 80.66 mg/100 g in skin. It also contains around 42.75 mg/100 g of Vitamin C in the flesh. The carotenoid content is around 161 µg/100 g fresh weight in flesh. In addition, the variety contains about 22.77 ppm zinc and 32.23 ppm iron in the flesh. The following table compares the nutritional value of Kufri jamunia with conventional yellow-skinned potato:

Nutrient (per 100 gm)

Kufri Jamunia

Common Potato

Vitamin C

42.75 mg

23.15 mg

Zinc

2.28 mg

0.28 mg

Iron

3.22 mg

0.57 mg

 

Culinary Uses of Kufri jamunia

Apart from its nutritional advantages, Kufri jamunia is suitable for a wide range of culinary applications. The variety is valued for its attractive purple colour, mealy texture, and pleasant flavour. This makes it suitable for both traditional preparations and processed food products. Its distinctive pigmentation also enhances the visual appeal of dishes and processed foods.

Purple-fleshed potatoes such as Kufri jamunia can be used in several preparations, including:

  • Traditional dishes: vegetable curry, paratha, puri, and raita
  • Breakfast and snack preparations: daliya, halwa, upma, dosa, and idli batter
  • Processed products: potato flour for bakery items, soups, and cookies

In addition, the tubers can be processed into dehydrated products such as anthocyanin-rich daliya, suji, and flour, which can be used as ingredients in various food formulations.

 

States Suitable for Kufri jamunia Cultivation

For large-scale adoption, a crop variety must perform reliably across different agro-climatic conditions. Kufri jamunia has demonstrated stable performance in multi-location trials and has been recommended for cultivation in the North Indian plains. The variety is considered suitable for several states where potatoes are widely grown.

These regions provide favourable climatic and soil conditions for the successful cultivation of this variety.

 

The Nutritional and Agricultural Promise of Kufri jamunia

Kufri jamunia represents an important advancement in the development of biofortified potato varieties in India. By combining good agronomic performance with enhanced nutritional quality, the variety offers benefits for both farmers and consumers. Its rich content of antioxidants, vitamins, and micronutrients makes it a valuable addition to efforts to improve dietary diversity and address hidden hunger. With its attractive appearance, culinary versatility, and adaptability to several states in the North Indian plains, Kufri jamunia has strong potential for wider cultivation and consumption in the future.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes massive 137 kg consignment of crystal meth; busts coastal drug trafficking network; 4 arrested in Tamil Nadu
Major intelligence-led operation foils suspected attempt to smuggle drug to Sri Lanka through maritime route
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 1:17PM by PIB Delhi

In a major crackdown on organised drug trafficking, in one of the biggest narcotics seizures in Tamil Nadu’s coastal region in recent years, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized 137 kg (gross) crystal methamphetamine, a banned synthetic drug, from a coastal village in Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu.  

Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers conducted an intensive surveillance and enforcement operation during 16–17 October 2026, successfully uncovering a suspected coastal drug-trafficking network attempting to smuggle the narcotic substances to Sri Lanka. The consignment was intended to be smuggled to Sri Lanka through mid-sea transfer. The value of the seized contraband in the illicit drug market is estimated to be in excess of Rs 100 crore.

The operation followed specific intelligence indicating that a large consignment of narcotic substances had been transported to a coastal location in Nagapattinam district for storage and onward smuggling to Sri Lanka. A subsequent search led to the recovery of six duffel bags containing 27 silver-foil packets, with each weighing approximately 5 kg were recovered. The packets contained a white crystalline substance suspected to be methamphetamine of high purity.  The contraband was seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.

In a simultaneous search at the premises of the suspected organiser, DRI officers seized Rs. 10 lakh in cash suspected to represent sale proceeds. Two four-wheelers and one two-wheeler allegedly used for transporting the narcotic substance were also seized. The operation successfully exposed the drug trafficking network including persons involved in organising the coastal export, transportation, storage and logistics of the consignment. Four persons, have been arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985, and remanded to judicial custody.

 Through this operation, DRI has not only removed a significant quantity of contraband  drugs from illicit circulation but also successfully dismantled a drug-trafficking network. This major seizure underscores DRI’s sustained efforts and enforcement capabilities in disrupting organised drug-trafficking networks and preventing the use of India’s coastline as a corridor for illicit narcotics trafficking.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh to represent India at SCO Council of Heads of Government Meeting in Tajikistan
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 11:22AM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh will visit Dushanbe, Tajikistan to represent India at the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (CHG) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), scheduled to be held on October 19-20, 2026. The meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO Member States, particularly in the areas of trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges. It is also expected to review the progress of ongoing cooperation initiatives and consider decisions relating to the Organisation's financial and institutional functioning.

India remains actively engaged in various SCO mechanisms and continues to contribute to regional cooperation through initiatives in areas such as start-ups and innovation, digital public infrastructure, and people-to-people exchanges. The meeting will provide an opportunity for India to exchange views with other SCO Member States on advancing practical and mutually beneficial cooperation within the Organisation.

The previous CHG meeting was held in Moscow, Russia, on November 18, 2025, where India was represented by External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Electronics & IT

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
STPI Tech Conclave highlights AI's Potential in Healthcare & Assistive Technologies
Programme brings together government, academia, healthcare experts and startups to explore AI applications in health, inclusion and well-being
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 10:59AM by PIB Delhi

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), and the Centre for Innovation, Incubation and Entrepreneurship (CIIE), IIT BHU, organised a Tech Conclave on “AI for Health & Assistive Technologies” at IIT BHU, Varanasi. The programme brought together government representatives, academic experts, healthcare professionals and startups to explore how artificial intelligence can advance healthcare, improve accessibility and support inclusion and citizen well-being through practical, scalable solutions.

The inaugural session commenced with the ceremonial lighting of the lamp, followed by welcome remarks by Prof. Manoj Kumar Meshram, Faculty In-Charge, CIIE, IIT BHU. The session featured a keynote address by Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, Government of India, followed by special addresses from Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, and Prof. Amit Patra, Director, IIT BHU. Special addresses were also delivered by Shri Sumit Mahajan, CEO, Uttar Pradesh Startup Mission, IT & Electronics Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, and Dr. Mallika Tiwari, Professor, Department of Oncology, Institute of Medical Sciences, BHU.

Delivering the keynote address, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, MeitY, Government of India, said, “Artificial Intelligence can play an important role in making healthcare more accessible, strengthening clinical decision-making and improving service delivery, particularly for communities with limited access to healthcare services. He emphasised the need to integrate AI education across disciplines and leverage the convergence of technology, medical sciences and research to develop practical solutions. He underscored AI's transformative potential in improving healthcare accessibility, affordability and quality through applications such as disease screening, medical diagnostics, remote ICU monitoring and AI-assisted surgical planning. He encouraged stronger collaboration among IIT (BHU), STPI, industry and startups to develop scalable healthcare and assistive technology solutions. He also highlighted the support available through the IndiaAI Mission and other MeitY initiatives, while emphasising STPI's role in connecting startups with investors, venture capital networks and market opportunities to build a sustainable innovation ecosystem.

Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, reflected on the transformation of India's technology ecosystem over the past three decades. Highlighting STPI's pivotal role in facilitating the growth of India's IT/ITeS industry since 1991, he emphasised the opportunity to replicate this success in Artificial Intelligence through indigenous innovation and entrepreneurship. Recalling how students earlier primarily aspired to secure campus placements, he noted that today's startup ecosystem enables young innovators to become job creators. Highlighting STPI's industry linkages and 27 Centres of Entrepreneurship, he underscored the importance of translational research, intellectual property creation and market access. He further emphasised the need to strengthen startup ecosystems beyond established technology hubs, particularly in emerging regions, through closer collaboration among academic institutions such as IIT (BHU), industry and government.

Prof. Amit Patra, Director, IIT BHU, addressing the STPI Tech Conclave on AI for Health & Assistive Technologies, highlighted IIT (BHU)'s efforts to strengthen its startup and entrepreneurship ecosystem through the establishment of the Centre for Innovation, Incubation and Entrepreneurship (CIIE). He emphasised the importance of creating a structured institutional framework to nurture entrepreneurial thinking among students, faculty and aspiring innovators, enabling them to transform innovative ideas into viable startups. He underscored the need to connect aspiring entrepreneurs with multiple funding sources and build a sustainable pipeline of startups, reaffirming IIT (BHU)'s commitment to fostering innovation and technology-driven entrepreneurship.

The conclave also featured two panel discussions— “Empowering Citizens Through AI: Health, Inclusion & Well-being” and “From Innovation to Impact: Translating AI Research into Scalable Healthcare & Assistive Solutions” bringing together experts from government, academia, healthcare and startups to discuss AI’s potential and its translation into practical, scalable solutions. Vote of Thanks was given by Shri Praveen Kumar Dwivedi, Additional Director and OIC, STPI Lucknow

The first panel discussion, “Empowering Citizens Through AI: Health, Inclusion & Well-being,” featured Prof. Manoj Kumar Meshram, Coordinator, CIIE-IIT BHU; Dr. Sanjay Kumar Singh, Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT BHU; Prof. Avanish Singh Parmar, Professor, Department of Physics, IIT (BHU); Dr. Shiru Sharma, Professor, Department of Biomedical Engineering, IIT BHU; Dr. Ruchi Chawla, Associate Professor, Department of Pharmaceutical Engineering and Technology, IIT BHU; Shri Shahbaz Ahmad, Founder, Arkision AI Pvt. Ltd.; and Shri Amit Kumar Verma, Additional Director, STPI. The discussion focused on the potential of AI to support more accessible and inclusive healthcare and improve citizen well-being. The multidisciplinary participation highlighted the importance of bringing together technological expertise, healthcare-related research and entrepreneurial perspectives to explore solutions that respond to people’s needs.

The second panel discussion, “From Innovation to Impact: Translating AI Research into Scalable Healthcare & Assistive Solutions,” featured Shri Rajeshwar Singh Jenwar, Director, MeitY; Dr. Akash Mishra, Assistant Professor, Centre of Biostatistics, IMS-BHU; Dr. Durgesh Narayan Singh, Scientific Officer, BioNest BHU; Ms. Tripti Verma, Founder, LeminAi; and Shri Shyam Kumar, COO, STPI MedTech Centre of Entrepreneurship at SGPGIMS, Lucknow. The session centred on the journey from research and innovation to practical, scalable solutions in healthcare and assistive technology. The mix of institutional, scientific and startup perspectives underscored the value of collaboration in helping promising ideas move towards real-world application.

The conclave reinforced the importance of collaboration among government, academia, healthcare institutions and startups to harness AI for accessible healthcare, assistive technologies and inclusive well-being. Through continued engagement, research translation and entrepreneurship support, STPI and CIIE, IIT BHU, aim to contribute to an innovation ecosystem that develops practical, responsible and scalable technology solutions for societal needs.

About STPI:

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), engaged in promoting the IT/ITES industry, innovation, research and development, startups, and product and intellectual property creation in emerging technology domains. These include the Internet of Things, blockchain, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, robotics, augmented and virtual reality, animation and visual effects, and data science and analytics. STPI supports innovation across domains such as gaming, fintech, agritech, medtech, autonomous and connected mobility, ESDM, cybersecurity, Industry 4.0 and drones.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister expresses grief over loss of lives in mishap in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh
Prime Minister announces ex-gratia
Posted On: 18 OCT 2026 10:25AM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi has expressed deep grief over the loss of lives due to a mishap in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

The Prime Minister conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.

The Prime Minister announced that an ex-gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund (PMNRF) would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs. 50,000.

The Prime Minister’s Office posted on X;

“Distressed to learn about the loss of lives due to a mishap in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. My condolences to the bereaved families. Praying for the speedy recovery of the injured.

An ex-gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs. 50,000: PM @narendramodi”

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat–NSS Launches Month 2 of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan with Nationwide Observance of Yoga evam Aatm-Suraksha Diwas
91,179 participants engaged across 183 institutions and community locations nationwide
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 10:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, through MY Bharat and the National Service Scheme (NSS), launched Month 2 of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat 100 Week Sankalp Abhiyan with the nationwide observance of “Yoga evam Aatm-Suraksha Diwas” (Yoga and Self-Defence Day) on October 16, 2026. Inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, the campaign has entered its second month under the theme “Fit Youth, Addiction-Free Youth (Shakti evam Seva),” focusing on physical fitness, mental resilience, discipline and self-confidence as key elements of a healthy, addiction-free society.

The Week 5 intervention witnessed the participation of 91,179 people across 183 educational institutions, NSS units and adopted villages nationwide. The activities brought together local leaders, police officials, sports authorities, medical experts and certified yoga instructors to promote healthy lifestyles, personal safety and awareness about substance abuse.

As part of the initiative, 332 yoga sessions engaged 34,290 participants, including 19,882 women, while 311 self-defence demonstrations reached 31,507 participants, including 18,364 women. An additional 180 community awareness activities engaged 25,391 participants. The yoga sessions incorporated the Common Yoga Protocol and relaxation techniques to highlight the importance of physical well-being and stress management. Self-defence demonstrations focused on practical safety techniques, situational awareness and personal security, particularly for young women.

Women accounted for 57.1% of the total participation, reflecting their strong engagement in the campaign. Regional Directorates, including Delhi, Jaipur, Lucknow, Patna and Trivandrum, recorded notable female participation. The activities were supported by partner organisations, including Anuvrat Vishva Bharati Society, BAPS, Bharat Scouts & Guides and MY Bharat Kendras.

The nationwide observance also generated significant digital outreach, with 4,197 social media posts shared organically under the campaign hashtag #NashaMuktYuva.

By integrating yoga, self-defence and community awareness, the initiative reinforces the role of physical fitness, mental well-being and personal resilience in preventing substance abuse. Through the 100 Week Sankalp Abhiyan, MY Bharat and NSS continue to mobilise young people and communities towards the vision of a Viksit Bharat and an addiction-free India, guided by the NSS motto, “Not Me, But You.”.

***

Pawan Singh Faujdar

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
AIIA Marks Its 10th Foundation Day with Two MoUs, Major Academic Publications and Digital Launches
KAUMARACON 2026 Concludes with Global Deliberations on Ayurvedic Child Healthcare
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 9:38PM by PIB Delhi

The three-day International Conference on Kaumarabhritya, KAUMARACON 2026, organised by the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, through its Department of Kaumarabhritya, concluded on Saturday with international scientific deliberations on advancing Ayurvedic child healthcare. The concluding day coincided with the Institute’s 10th Foundation Day, celebrating a decade of progress in Ayurveda education, research, clinical excellence and global collaboration.

The conference brought together international experts, academicians, researchers, clinicians, policymakers and industry representatives to discuss the role of Ayurveda and Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine (TCIM) in paediatric healthcare, emphasising scientific validation, interdisciplinary research and preventive care.

The scientific session on Traditional, Complementary, and Integrative Medicine (TCIM) in Global Child Health featured perspectives from experts representing the United Kingdom, Sri Lanka, Germany, Nepal, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Italy and the United States, among other countries. Discussions covered Ayurvedic paediatric education, regulatory frameworks, traditional medicine practices and opportunities for international collaboration in child healthcare. A panel discussion on Industry–Academia Synergies: Catalyzing Research, Innovation, and Commercialization in Child Healthcare, chaired by Prof. (Vd.) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, with Dr. A. Raghu, Advisor (Ayurveda), Ministry of Ayush, as co-chair, explored research-driven product development, quality assurance and the translation of academic findings into accessible healthcare solutions. A round-table conference on Policy, Education, and Research in Kaumarabhritya further examined strategies to strengthen Ayurvedic paediatrics through specialised education, research and policy support.

The Foundation Day ceremony was graced by Shri Ramvir Singh Bidhuri, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, as Chief Guest; Padma Bhushan Vaidya Devendra Triguna Ji and Prof. Dr. Abhimanyu Kumar, Former Director, AIIA and CEO, CAYEIT, as Guests of Honour; and Dr. Ashok Kumar Varshney, National Organising Secretary, Arogya Bharati and Member, National Medical Commission, as Special Guest. Prof. (Vd.) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, was also present. A major highlight was the signing of two Memorandum of Understanding between AIIA and Rashtriya Ayurved Vidyapeeth, and AIIA and Arogya Bharati, to strengthen institutional collaboration and knowledge-sharing in Ayurveda.

More than 15 academic publications and educational resources were launched. The Institute also launched its new Digital Brand Identity Manual (DBIM)-compliant website, the e-course Foundations of Entrepreneurship & Startup Development for Ayush Professionals (FESDAP), and A Textbook of Research Methodology and Medical Statistics. The online launch of the eBook Rooted and Rising: Journey of All India Institute of Ayurveda documented the Institute’s institutional journey and achievements.

Congratulating the AIIA family, Shri Ramvir Singh Bidhuri, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, said, “I witnessed the foundation-laying ceremony of AIIA and have seen its remarkable growth from 2016 to 2026. The hospital is doing commendable work, with the Hon’ble Prime Minister extending support at every stage of its growth.”

Thanking the Hon’ble Minister and acknowledging the efforts of the Institute’s team, Prof. (Vd.) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, said, “The success of KAUMARACON 2026 is a result of the tireless efforts of the AIIA family, who have worked day and night to make this conference a grand success.”

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
EXERCISE KONKAN-26 CONCLUDES OFF PLYMOUTH, UK
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 9:06PM by PIB Delhi

KONKAN-26, the India-UK bilateral maritime exercise, concluded off Plymouth, UK, on 15 Oct 2026. Conducted from 08-15 Oct 2026, the exercise enabled the Indian Navy and the Royal Navy to engage across a wide range of professional and operational domains.

The Indian Navy was represented by the stealth frigate INS Trishul, while the Royal Navy deployed HMS Sutherland, a Duke-class anti-submarine warfare frigate. The exercise was conducted by Fleet Operational Standards and Training (FOST), Royal Navy.

The intensive four-day Sea Phase, conducted from 12-15 Oct 2026, encompassed advanced seamanship manoeuvres, joint tactical exercises, communication procedures, anti-surface asymmetric warfare, anti-submarine warfare and weapon firings in a multi-threat maritime environment. These serials enhanced interoperability between the participating units.

Through the exchange of professional expertise and Best Practices, KONKAN-26 reinforced the ability of the Indian Navy and the Royal Navy to operate together across complex maritime scenarios, furthering the enduring maritime partnership between India and the UK.

The programmes promoted drug prevention, healthy lifestyles and the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) organises five drug awareness programmes for MP youth Mission Yuva Raksha
CBN Madhya Pradesh partners with Brahma Kumaris to promote preventive awareness among youth against drug abuse
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi

Under Mission Yuva Raksha, the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), Madhya Pradesh Unit, organised five drug-awareness programmes at educational institutions in Neemuch, Jaora, Jawad, Mandsaur and Garoth during October 2026. The programmes promoted drug prevention, healthy lifestyles and the vision of a “Nasha Mukt Bharat.”

On 5th October 2026, an awareness programme on the harmful effects of drug abuse and the importance of a drug-free life was attended by approximately 200 students and teachers of the Swami Vivekanand Government PG College, Neemuch.

Awareness programme – Swami Vivekanand Govt. PG College, Neemuch

On 13th October 2026, the programme organiseed by CBN addressed substance abuse, its impact on youth health and future prospects, and healthy living. Approximately 200 students and faculty members, along with 25 staff members, participated at the Sardar Patel College of Nursing, Jaora.

Awareness programme – Sardar Patel College of Nursing, Jaora

On 15th October 2026, CBN organised in association with Brahma Kumaris, Neemuch, the programme promoted drug-free living and awareness of addictive substances. Approximately 450 students and teachers attended at the CM Rise Government School, Jawad.

CBN Awareness programme with Brahmakumaris– CM Rise Government School, Jawad

 

On the same day, the CBN Madhya Pradesh Unit’s Mandsaur-I Division organised the camp focused on drug prevention, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a drug-free society under Yuva Raksha and Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan. Approximately 450 students attended of the CM Rise School, Sabakheda, Mandsaur.

Awareness programme – CM Rise School, Sabakheda, Mandsaur

Similarly, the Office of the District Opium Officer, CBN, Garoth, in collaboration with Brahma Kumaris, organised an awareness programme attended by approximately 230 students at the Sanskar Valley Higher Secondary School, Garoth, on 15th October 2026.

Awareness programme – Sanskar Valley Higher Secondary School, Garoth

Across the programmes, participants were scientifically briefed on the harmful effects of drug abuse on physical and mental health, education, family life and careers. Activities included awareness sessions, question-and-answer competitions, educational videos, presentations, meditation and poster-making. Participants were encouraged to resist substance abuse, adopt healthy lifestyles and contribute to a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

The programmes also emphasised personal responsibility and collective participation in drug prevention. Participants took pledges to stay away from drugs and support awareness initiatives in their schools, families and communities. The programmes received positive participation and reinforced the importance of preventive education among youth.

Through these four awareness programmes, CBN Madhya Pradesh Unit reaffirmed its commitment to complementing enforcement activities with preventive awareness and demand-reduction initiatives, particularly among students and young people.

By engaging educational institutions and encouraging interactive learning, awareness activities and personal commitments to a drug-free life, CBN seeks to empower youth to make informed choices and become active ambassadors of drug prevention in their communities.

The initiatives reflect the continued commitment of the Central Bureau of Narcotics towards the vision of Nasha Mukt Bharat and the creation of a healthier, safer and drug-free society.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
NBA disburses Rs 1.19 Crore to 29 State Biodiversity Boards and one UT Biodiversity Council under Access and Benefit Sharing Mechanism
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 7:32PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs 1.19 crore under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) mechanism to 29 State Biodiversity Boards and one Union Territory Biodiversity Council to support biodiversity conservation, sustainable use of biological resources and community welfare. The amount represents ABS contributions received from companies for research and commercial utilisation of agricultural biological resources. 

As the biological resources were procured through markets or traders, individual benefit claimers could not be readily identified. Accordingly, the NBA adopted the distribution mechanism recommended by the Expert Committee and approved by the Authority. The allocations were determined in proportion to the estimated cultivation areas of the respective biological resources, based on official agricultural statistics published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare through its Unified Portal for Agricultural Statistics.

The allocation details for the ten highest-receiving States, along with the amount distributed among other States and the Union Territory, are given below:

The allocation covers agricultural biological resources, including maize (Zea mays L.), rice (Oryza sativa L.), pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum) and cotton (Gossypium hirsutum).

ABS contributions were received from M/s Corteva Crop India Pvt. Ltd., M/s Pioneer Overseas Corporation, M/s Pioneer Hi-Bred Private Limited, M/s Limagrain India Private Limited (formerly M/s Bisco Biosciences Private Ltd.), M/s Limagrain (Thailand) Co. Ltd., M/s Limagrain Brasil S.A. and M/s Syngenta India Ltd. for the utilisation of maize and sweet corn varieties. M/s Limagrain India Pvt. Ltd. also contributed for five maize hybrids, two rice hybrids and three pearl millet hybrids. For cotton, contributions were received from M/s Corteva Crop India Pvt. Ltd. for research involving 16 varieties and M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited for the commercial utilisation of 14 hybrids.

The agriculture sector is emerging as a potential contributor to India’s ABS mechanism, demonstrating how the utilisation of agricultural biological resources can generate benefits for conservation and local communities. Such contributions can support the conservation and sustainable use of India’s agricultural biodiversity, including traditional varieties and genetic diversity.

As on date, the NBA has disbursed Rs 86 crore realised from the agriculture sector to various beneficiaries. The funds allocated to the State Biodiversity Boards and the Union Territory Biodiversity Council shall be utilised exclusively for activities specified under Section 32(2) of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002. These activities include biodiversity documentation, conservation and sustainable use, strengthening local biodiversity governance, research, capacity building and enhancement of community livelihoods.

The NBA has so far disbursed more than Rs 203 crore, supporting biodiversity conservation and the livelihoods of local communities. As India prepares for the seventeenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17), scheduled for 19-30 October 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia, these efforts underscore the country's commitment to conserving its biological heritage while ensuring that the benefits derived from it contribute to the well-being of local communities.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM reviews Paddy Stubble Management Measures in Firozpur and Faridkot; stresses Timely Availability of CRM Machinery and Farmer Facilitation
High-level team visits Hotspot Villages to assess Ground-level Implementation of Measures to prevent Stubble Burning
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

Following its visit to Moga district of Punjab, a high-level team of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), led by Dr. T.S. Panwar, Member (Technical), CAQM, visited Firozpur and Faridkot districts today to review the ground-level implementation of measures to prevent paddy stubble burning during the ongoing harvesting season.

The team held a joint review meeting with the Deputy Commissioners (DCs) and concerned district officers of Firozpur and Faridkot at the DC Office in Firozpur. During the meeting, the team reviewed the preparedness of the district administrations and coordination among concerned departments for effective in-situ and ex-situ management and utilisation of paddy stubble. The availability and deployment of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery, field-level surveillance, monitoring of hotspot areas and enforcement measures were also reviewed.

The team emphasised the need to strengthen in-situ and ex-situ management of paddy straw, ensure timely availability and optimal utilisation of CRM machinery, and enhance coordination among farmers, aggregators, industries and other stakeholders. The deployment of drones and low-cost sensors for technology-based monitoring and trend analysis was also reviewed, along with efforts to sensitise farmers about the ill-effects of stubble burning and PM2.5.

 

The Commission stressed the need to facilitate farmers’ access to CRM machines and other in-situ management machinery, along with better coordination with aggregators for effective ex-situ management of paddy straw. The district administrations were advised to ensure timely availability of machinery and close coordination among all stakeholders to prevent stubble-burning incidents.

Following the review meeting, the CAQM team visited selected hotspot villages in Firozpur and Faridkot to assess the prevailing ground-level situation and review the implementation of measures to prevent stubble burning. The visit is part of CAQM’s continued monitoring and review of paddy management measures in hotspot districts of Punjab, with the objective of strengthening in-situ and ex-situ management of paddy straw and preventing stubble-burning incidents in the region.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026-Mysuru, Karnataka
Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 Features 83 Stalls, Including 80 Stalls Allotted To Artisans, Among Them 37 Women Artisans
 12 States And Union Territories Participating in the Mela
Union Social Justice Empowerment Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant To Visit Mela in Mysuru
Secretary To Review Central Schemes, Programmes, Initiatives along with Site Visits in Mysuru, Karnataka
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Secretary of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant is visiting the ongoing Nine Days SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 at Mysuru in Karnataka tomorrow. The Mela is being organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

The Secretary is also taking comprehensive review of the Ministry’s Schemes, Programmes and Initiatives under implementation along with Site Visits in Mysuru.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Mela is underway at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds in Mysuru, since October 11. The Mela will conclude on October 19 Monday.

He said the Mela provides a marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Safai Karamcharis, enabling them to showcase their traditional handicrafts, handloom products and other goods to a wider audience.

The Official said the Mela has been jointly organized by three national corporations under the Ministry namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), which provide financial assistance to artisans and eligible beneficiaries.

The ongoing Mela features 83 stalls, including 80 stalls allotted to artisans, among them 37 women artisans. Artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, are participating in the exhibition.

The stalls feature with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience.

The Mela is designed to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through direct interaction with visitors and prospective customers, participating artisans can display their products, expand their customer base and improve the market reach of their enterprises. The initiative also promotes India’s rich cultural heritage and supports the preservation of traditional art forms and skills.

The SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026 will continue at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds until October 19 Monday, offering visitors an opportunity to explore India’s traditional crafts and handloom products while supporting the livelihoods of artisans. Through such initiatives, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to strengthen market access, encourage entrepreneurship and advance the economic empowerment of disadvantaged communities.

The MELA also serves as an important platform for disseminating information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry and its three national corporations, helping eligible beneficiaries learn about available financial assistance and entrepreneurship opportunities.

The Ministry facilitates artisans’ participation by providing free stalls and support towards travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods and meals, in accordance with the applicable arrangements.

In addition to the Mela, the Ministry is promoting the BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) initiative to expand market access for products made by target-group artisans through digital platforms in India and abroad. Branding products under BHARAT TULIP is intended to improve their visibility, facilitate online sales and connect traditional artisans with a wider customer base.

The Ministry has been organizing Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022, benefiting 975 artisans through 13 fairs held so far.

The ongoing Mysuru edition is the first Shilp Samagam Mela of the financial year 2026–27.

The Ministry also proposes to organize additional fairs in Guwahati (Oct 21 to 28, 2026); Dilli Haat in New Delhi, Jodhpur and Lucknow during the current financial year, alongside participation in major exhibitions such as the India International Trade Fair 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in February 2027.

Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, has undertaken Trade Margin Rationalisation (TMR) of 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs in public interest to address excessive trade margins, make cancer treatment more affordable, and improve…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Pharmaceuticals
Trade Margin Rationalisation on 137 Anti-Cancer Drugs
The revised prices will become effective from November 9, 2026.
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi

The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, has undertaken Trade Margin Rationalisation (TMR) of 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs in public interest to address excessive trade margins, make cancer treatment more affordable, and improve access to anti-cancer medicines. The intervention is expected to bring down the MRP of the identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs by up to 70%, depending on their existing price structures.

The intervention builds upon the success of NPPA's 2019 pilot TMR exercise, under which trade margins for 42 anti-cancer drugs were capped at 30%. Following that exercise, MRP of 526 brands of non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines was reduced by up to 90%. The present exercise extends this approach to a larger set of anti-cancer drugs, based on the list recommended by the Expert Committee under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The Expert Committee comprised leading oncologists, medical specialists, experts from hospitals across the country, and Government officers. It deliberated upon and recommended 137 drugs for inclusion under TMR. This list would be updated periodically. Considering the drugs recommended by the Committee, NPPA has capped trade margin at 30% of the Maximum Retail Price (MRP), in accordance with Paragraph 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013. The Gazette notification dated October 17, 2026 is available on the official website of NPPA https://nppa.gov.in/en . This measure is expected to bring significant relief to the many patients and families affected by cancer, who often face high financial burden due to high cost of treatment.

All manufacturers will be required to inform NPPA of their revised prices within 7 days of publication of the Gazette notification. The revised prices will become effective from November 9, 2026. Manufacturers will be required to display the price lists on their website and widely disseminate to all retailers and hospitals. All the retailers and hospitals shall charge reduced prices effective 9th November, 2026 and display the revised prices in their pharmacies. Hospitals shall also prominently display revised prices on their websites. Consumers can use the Pharma Sahi Daam app and NPPA website to check revised prices of drugs.

As substantial supply of anti-cancer drugs is directly made to hospitals and medical institutions, they shall be responsible for ensuring revised prices of such drugs from the date of implementation. State Drug Controllers will take necessary steps to ensure compliance by manufacturers, dealers including retailers, hospitals and medical institutions.

The measure for TMR on anti-cancer drugs aims to control excessive trade margins in the distribution and retail channel while safeguarding legitimate manufacturer revenues and preventing artificial market shortages. Pharmaceutical companies will be required to maintain current production and supply levels for the notified formulations to ensure timely and uninterrupted access for patients.

By making anti-cancer drugs more affordable and accessible, this initiative will help ease the financial burden on patients and their families and support the broader public-health objective of equitable access to cancer treatment.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
FIRST TRAINING SQUADRON DEPARTS SEYCHELLES, REINFORCING MARITIME COOPERATION
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi

Ships of the Indian Navy’s First Training Squadron (1TS) — INS Tir, INS Sujata, and Indian Coast Guard Ship Sarathi — departed Port Victoria, Seychelles, on 15 Oct 2026, on completion of their port call, which commenced on 12 Oct 2026, during the ongoing training deployment. The engagement reinforced the longstanding India-Seychelles partnership through professional training, capacity building, and interactions with the country’s leadership and maritime community.

During the port call, Senior Officer, First Training Squadron, along with the Commanding Officers of the visiting ships, called on Maj Gen Michael Rosette, Chief of Defence Forces, Seychelles Defence Force (SDF). Discussions focused on the enduring partnership and bilateral cooperation between the two forces.

The programme featured professional activities and cross-training visits, along with firefighting and small-arms training for SDF personnel. The First Training Squadron also conducted a Passage Exercise (PASSEX) with Seychelles Coast Guard Ship Andromache, featuring joint patrolling, communication drills, and coordinated manoeuvres. Outreach initiatives included a medical camp, distribution of essential supplies at the Point La Rue elderly home, a visit by schoolchildren, and a musical performance by the Indian Navy Band.

The deployment underscores the strong bonds of friendship between India and Seychelles and reflects the Indian Navy’s commitment to capacity building and regional partnerships in line with the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Department of Commerce Organises “Leveraging FTAs” Outreach Programme in Jaipur to Strengthen Export Opportunities
FTA Outreach Programme Aims to Raise Exporter Awareness and Promote Effective Utilisation of Trade Agreements
Posted On: 17 OCT 2026 6:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Commerce organised an outreach programme “Leveraging FTAs – Outreach Programme” in Jaipur, Rajasthan, to create awareness about the benefits available under India’s Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and facilitate their effective utilisation by exporters. The programme was addressed by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Mohit Yadav, and witnessed participation from exporters across sectors and representatives of the Government of Rajasthan, Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Jaipur Special Economic Zone and the Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC).

The programme aimed to help Indian enterprises translate preferential market access under FTAs into export opportunities through targeted information, capacity building, practical guidance and coordination among the Department of Commerce, State Governments, industry associations and exporters.

The programme assumed significance in the context of India’s expanding engagement with the global economy. At the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi stated, “Our constant endeavour is to ensure that India’s capabilities open new doors of opportunity for other countries as well.” In his Independence Day address on 15 August 2026 and on other occasions, the Prime Minister has highlighted the opportunities created by FTAs for Indian producers, farmers and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), while emphasising the importance of meeting international quality standards to access global markets.

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal has also highlighted the commercial opportunities offered by India’s FTAs, noting that preferential market access can create opportunities for farmers, women entrepreneurs, youth, MSMEs, artisans and industry. He has urged businesses to utilise reduced- or zero-duty access by focusing on quality and competitiveness.

India’s exports of merchandise and services have continued to register growth. Cumulative exports during April–September 2026–27 are estimated at US$ 476.20 billion, compared with US$ 418.31 billion during the corresponding period of 2025–26, registering estimated growth of 13.84%. Major drivers of merchandise export growth in September 2026 included electronic goods, petroleum products, organic and inorganic chemicals, engineering goods, and cotton yarn, fabrics, made-ups and handloom products.

The programme provided a platform for exporters from Rajasthan to discuss opportunities under India’s FTAs and the practical challenges involved in availing preferential market access. India’s trade agreements and arrangements with partners, including the UAE, Australia, the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries and the United Kingdom, offer avenues for Indian goods and services to access overseas consumers, buyers, investors and value chains, subject to the provisions and implementation status of the respective agreements.

The discussions focused on identifying export-ready products, understanding tariff preferences and rules of origin, meeting quality and certification requirements, and strengthening connections with overseas buyers. These areas are important for enabling businesses to make effective use of the market access available under India’s trade agreements.

A sector-specific presentation was delivered by Joint Director General of Foreign Trade, Jaipur, Shri Md. Moin Afaque, on export opportunities for the gems and jewellery sector under India’s recently concluded FTAs. The presentation highlighted that India ranks eighth among global gems and jewellery exporters, with a 2.9% share in the US$ 1 trillion global market. It also outlined the import market opportunities available under India’s new FTAs, including immediate duty-free access across tariff lines in each of the agreements, as stated in the presentation.

The presentation examined India’s competitive position vis-à-vis major supplier countries and identified product categories and FTA markets where Indian exporters could benefit from tariff advantages. Emerging opportunities were highlighted in lab-grown diamond jewellery, coloured gemstones, Kundan-Meenakari heritage jewellery, smart and wearable jewellery, recycled and ethically sourced gold jewellery, and pearl and cultured jewellery. These opportunities are particularly relevant for Rajasthan, given the State’s established presence in the gems and jewellery sector.

Rajasthan has significant potential to contribute to India’s export growth through textiles and garments, handicrafts, gems and jewellery, engineering goods, stone and minerals, and agricultural and processed-food products. The Rajasthan Economic Review 2024–25 outlines the State’s ambition to become a US$ 350 billion economy by 2029 and achieve exports of ₹1.5 lakh crore by 2029, as envisaged under the Rajasthan Export Promotion Policy (REPP) 2024. The Rajasthan Budget 2026–27 also sets out the vision of Viksit Rajasthan @ 2047, with the goal of building a US$ 4.3 trillion economy by 2047. These objectives align with the national vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.

FTAs can provide opportunities for Rajasthan’s farmers and farmer-producer organisations (FPOs) to access new markets for eligible agricultural produce, millets, spices and processed foods, subject to food-safety, traceability and other importing-country requirements. For MSMEs and artisans engaged in textiles, handicrafts, jewellery and engineering, tariff preferences can improve price competitiveness and support participation in international supply chains. Women-led enterprises and self-help groups can benefit from export training, e-commerce and buyer linkages, while larger businesses can explore investment, technology partnerships and market diversification. The benefits available will depend on the product, partner country and applicable FTA provisions.

By connecting enterprises in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Bhilwara and other districts with international buyers and supply chains, the outreach programme seeks to strengthen Rajasthan’s participation in global trade. Greater awareness of trade preferences, export documentation, product standards, logistics and market intelligence can help first-time exporters expand beyond domestic markets.

State Government support, along with initiatives for developing industrial areas and parks, sector-specific task forces focused on exports, and policies and schemes promoting credit facilities, financial incentives, market linkages, skill development, quality certification, technology upgradation and e-commerce, can further support entrepreneurship, employment and livelihoods. These efforts can contribute to Rajasthan’s development aspirations under Viksit Rajasthan 2047 and the national vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
